articles.title: White Sox Designate Jordan Leasure For Assignment
body: The White Sox officially announced their signing of right-hander Dustin May. Fellow righty Jordan Leasure has been designated for assignment as the corresponding 40-man roster move.

articles.title: White Sox Sign Dustin May
body: November 18: The Sox made it official today.

November 17: The White Sox and right-hander Dustin May are in agreement on a three-year, $52.5MM contract. The team has yet to officially announce the deal. May is represented by Paragon Sports International.

It’s a surprisingly strong deal for the pitcher. The White Sox are placing a notable bet on the right-hander’s relative youth — he’ll pitch next season at 29 — and power arsenal, while looking past his lengthy injury history and middling bottom-line results when healthy in each of the past two seasons.

May played the 2026 season on a one-year, $12.5MM deal originally signed with the Cardinals, who traded him to the Brewers alongside reliever JoJo Romero at the deadline. He posted back-end results in St. Louis and was torched for a 5.65 ERA in 10 starts (36 2/3 innings) with Milwaukee before also struggling in the playoffs. May finished out the regular season with a 4.70 ERA in a career-high 145 2/3 innings (4.77 in 156 2/3 frames, including the playoffs).

Over the past two seasons, May has combined to toss 278 innings with a 4.82 ERA. He’s fanned a roughly average 22.2% of his opponents in that time with similarly average command (8.8% walk rate) and ground-ball tendencies (42%).

articles.title: Dipoto: “Zero” Chance Mariners Trade Another Starter
body: The Mariners’ blockbuster acquisition of third baseman Maikel Garcia earlier today subtracted righties Bryce Miller and Logan Evans from their rotation outlook. It’s been known for some time that Seattle was much, much more open to dealing from its rotation supply this winter than in offseasons past, but it seems that swap with the Royals is where the starting pitching trades both start and end.

President of baseball operations Jerry Dipoto told the Mariners beat today that there’s “zero” chance he moves another starting pitcher now that Miller and Evans are out the door (link via Adam Jude of the Seattle Times). Dipoto added that the Mariners would like to add another right-handed bat, a veteran infield presence and, with Jose A. Ferrer headed to Kansas City as part of that swap, bring in an established left-handed reliever.

Seattle’s 2027 rotation now lines up to include Logan Gilbert, George Kirby, Bryan Woo, Emerson Hancock and touted prospect Kade Anderson, the No. 3 overall pick from the 2025 draft. Young right-hander Ryan Sloan is widely considered one of the best pitching prospects in baseball behind Anderson — if not the best — and could arrive in the majors “at any point” next year, according to Dipoto.

articles.title: Seth Halvorsen Undergoes Tommy John Surgery
body: The Dodgers announced that right-hander Seth Halvorsen has undergone ulnar collateral ligament reconstruction surgery, also known as Tommy John surgery, on his throwing arm. He will miss the entire 2027 season.

Halvorsen, 27 in February, was acquired from the Rockies ahead of the trade deadline a few months back. He has huge velocity, with a four-seamer and sinker that both average over 99 miles per hour, but hasn’t translated that into big league results just yet. Between the Rockies and Dodgers, he has thrown 81 major league innings thus far with a 4.78 earned run average. His 49.2% ground ball rate is strong but his 20% strikeout rate and 11.1% walk rate are both worse than average.

Despite the underwhelming numbers, the Dodgers took a shot on the stuff. The club has a strong reputation for helping pitchers reach their ceilings. If that’s going to happen with Halvorsen, it will have to wait.

There’s no injured list during the offseason. It goes away five days after the World Series and doesn’t come back until camps open in the spring. If the Dodgers still believe in the arm over the long term, they could keep Halvorsen on the 40-man through the winter. Once spring training begins, he could be put on the major league 60-day injured list to open a 40-man spot. That would require giving him a full year of big league pay and service time. He was on optional assignment at the end of the 2026 season and still has options, so he could be kept in the minors next year, but that would involve him holding his 40-man spot.

articles.title: Rockies Re-Sign TJ Shook To Minor League Deal
body: The Rockies announced that they have re-signed right-hander TJ Shook to a minor league deal. Prior to the official announcement, it was reported by Thomas Harding of MLB.com, who noted that Shook has been assigned to Triple-A Albuquerque.

Shook, 29 in May, played minor league ball for the Brewers and Mets from 2021 to 2025. The Rockies took him from the latter club in the minor league phase of the Rule 5 draft a year ago. He got to make his major league debut with Colorado this year, allowing seven earned runs in 7 2/3 innings. He was outrighted off the roster at season’s end and elected free agency.

The results were better in the minors, as Shook tossed 57 1/3 innings for the Isotopes with a 3.45 earned run average. There was probably some good fortune in there, as his 21% strikeout rate and 12.1% walk rate were subpar while his 77% strand rate was to the fortunate side. Shook’s fastball only averaged about 92-93 miles per hour on the year but he also mixed in a cutter, slider and changeup.

The Rockies will undoubtedly need arms next year. It’s always a challenge having a competent pitching with Coors Field as a home field but the club has been struggling even more than usual in recent years. Colorado’s pitchers had a collective 5.59 ERA in 2026, worst in the majors. If Shook can earn his way back onto the 40-man, he still has a couple of option years.

articles.title: Royals Designate Kyle Isbel For Assignment
body: The Royals announced their six-player trade with the Mariners, which was reported earlier today. It was a three-for-three swap but all three players heading to Kansas City had 40-man roster spots, compared to just two of the players going to Seattle. The Royals therefore needed to open a 40-man spot and designated outfielder Kyle Isbel for assignment.

Isbel, 30 in March, has played for the Royals in parts of the past six seasons. He has been a standout defender and decent baserunner but hasn’t done much at the plate. He has made 1,832 plate appearances to this point in his career with just 29 home runs and a subpar 5.7% walk rate. He has a.235/.284/.357 slash line and 75 wRC+, indicating he has been 25% worse than league average as a hitter overall.

Despite that lack of punch from the batter’s box, he has been a valuable player thanks to his work on the grass. In over 4,000 innings of outfield work, mostly in center, Isbel has been credited with 34 Defensive Runs Saved, 51 Outs Above Average and a grade of 40 from Fielding Run Value.

That defense was enough for the Royals to stick with Isbel through two arbitration seasons. He made $1.75MM last year and $2.7MM this year. He was slated for one more arb year in 2027 before reaching free agency. MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz projected him for a bump to $3.5MM.

articles.title: Twins Sign Sonny Gray
body: Sonny Gray is headed back to Minnesota. The Twins announced Wednesday that they’ve signed the free-agent righty to a two-year contract that’ll reportedly guarantee him $55MM and contains an opt-out opportunity following the 2027 season. Gray, a client of McKinnis Sports, starred for Minnesota in 2022-23 and finished second in American League Cy Young Award voting in the latter of those two seasons.

Gray’s original departure from the Twins came on the heels of a postseason run that was immediately followed by swift payroll reductions. The Twins’ 2023 payroll pushed upwards of $155MM, but as the Pohlad family explored a sale of the club, payroll was slashed by around $50MM over the next two seasons. The Pohlads eventually walked back their efforts to sell the team, instead bringing in a trio of minority investors to pay off a reported debt in excess of $400MM.

The influx of new owners was accompanied by a changing of the guard among the Pohlad family as well; Tom Pohlad ousted younger brother Joe as the team’s control person last December. Since taking the reins, the elder Pohlad brother has repeatedly gone on the record to speak about increasing payroll, investing in the club and winning back the trust of the fans. While some doubted whether that’d be the case, the reunion with Gray, the qualifying offers for Ryan Jeffers (which he accepted yesterday), and deadline trades to acquire players making notable major league salaries (i.e. Jeff Hoffman, Dean Kremer, A.J. Minter) all back up the discourse from Pohlad over the past 11 months.

articles.title: Athletics Add Trevor Amicone, Casey Weathers To Coaching Staff
body: The Athletics announced a pair of new additions to their coaching staff Wednesday. Trevor Amicone has been hired as the team’s new hitting coach. He’d previously been an assistant hitting coach with the Twins. The A’s also named Casey Weathers their new pitching coach. He’d previously been the Phillies’ director of pitching development.

Amicone spent the 2025-26 seasons as Minnesota’s assistant hitting coach at the major league level. He’d previously been a hitting coach in the Yankees’ minor league ranks for five seasons, breaking in with their Dominican Summer League affiliate before spending the 2023-24 seasons as the hitting coach for the Yankees’ Scranton/Wilkes-Barre Triple-A affiliate. He was one of two assistant hitting coaches in Minnesota. It’s not clear yet whether the Twins will replace him or simply give a larger workload to lead hitting coach Keith Beauregard and remaining assistant Rayden Sierra.

Weathers was a first-round draft pick by the Rockies in 2007 and ranked as one of their best prospects for several years. The now-41-year-old Weathers (no relation to Yankees southpaw Ryan Weathers) pitched in the minors from 2007-16 across four organizations but never reached the majors. Following his retirement as a player, Weathers was hired by the Reds to coach in their minor league ranks. He’s been the pitching coach for their Rookie-level and Triple-A clubs but was hired by Philadelphia to oversee the organization’s pitching development efforts following the 2024 season.

articles.title: Red Sox Acquire Nick Fortes
body: The Red Sox have acquired catcher Nick Fortes from the Rays, according to announcements from both clubs. Tampa gets minor league right-hander Angel Roa in return. The Sox designated catcher Connor Wong to open a 40-man spot for Fortes.

It’s probably not a coincidence that this deal came together just before Friday’s non-tender deadline. The Red Sox and Rays both have a starter behind the plate, as Boston has Adley Rutschman and Tampa has Liam Hicks. Each club also went into the winter with an arbitration-eligible backup on the roster, the Rays with Fortes and the Red Sox with Wong.

MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz projects Wong for a $2MM salary next year. Fortes is projected slightly higher at $3.4MM. Wong’s defense doesn’t get strong grades. He seemed like maybe he was breaking out at the plate in 2024 when he hit 13 home runs and slashed.280/.333/.425. Unfortunately, he has hit.214/.287/.299 over the past two seasons. That has made him replacement level or worse for that span.

Wong still has an option remaining. The Sox could have tendered him a contract and kept him as depth in the minors, but they also have Mickey Gasper on the roster. Gasper is also still optionable and he is cheaper because he hasn’t qualified for arbitration yet. The Sox have decided to move on from Wong. They have some time to work out a trade but the most likely outcome is that he will be non-tendered on Friday.

articles.title: Reds Receiving Trade Interest In Nick Lodolo
body: As clubs around the league scour the market for rotation help, the Reds have been receiving trade interest in left-hander Nick Lodolo, per Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic. There’s no indication any kind of deal is close at the moment.

Lodolo, 29 in February, is down to one final year of club control. He’s eligible for arbitration this winter and projected by MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz to earn $5.7MM for the upcoming 2027 campaign.

If the Reds were to trade Lodolo, they’d be selling low. The former No. 7 overall pick and top prospect broke out with a terrific 2025 season that saw him pitch 156 2/3 innings with a 3.33 ERA, 24.3% strikeout rate, 4.8% walk rate and 42.6% ground-ball rate. All of his numbers trended the wrong direction during an injury-marred 2026 campaign, however.

Recurring blister issues have been a problem for Lodolo over the years, and that was again the case in’26, when he started just 21 games and pitched 108 2/3 frames. Lodolo managed only a 4.97 earned run average in that time. His strikeout rate plummeted to 17.1%, while his walk rate nearly doubled to 9.5%. Lodolo posted a strong 12.4% swinging-strike rate and 32.7% opponents’ chase rate in’25 but saw those numbers drop to 9% and 28.4%, respectively. Both are below average.

articles.title: Latest On Corey Seager
body: It’s no big secret that the Rangers are putting out feelers, trying to line up a Corey Seager trade. Even if they can agree to a framework with another club, Seager would have to give his consent. As a 10-and-5 guy, Seager has full no-trade rights. Jeff Passan of ESPN reports that Seager is open to moving but has a narrow list of teams he’s willing to join. Passan adds there’s no momentum towards a deal right now.

Players get full no-trade protection when they have at least ten years of big league service and have spent at least the last five years with the same club, hence “10-and-5”. Seager is five years into his ten-year pact with the Rangers, so there’s still five years left to go. He’ll make $31MM in each of those remaining seasons for a total of $155MM. Seager is still capable of strong production when on the field but that’s a lot of money for an injury-prone player who will celebrate his 34th birthday in April.

In 2026, Seager went on the injured list for a concussion and twice hit the IL related to lower back inflammation. He also had surgery after the season was done to remove a bone spur from his elbow. He got into just 102 contests on the year, his fourth straight season coming up short of the 125-game mark. He hit 20 home runs but his 23.6% strikeout rate was a career high. His.227/.312/.424 batting line led to a 106 wRC+, tied for the worst mark of his career.

articles.title: Angels Acquire Jace Jung
body: The Angels announced Wednesday that they’ve acquired infielder Jace Jung from the Tigers in exchange for cash. Detroit designated Jung, a former No. 12 overall pick (2022) and top prospect, for assignment yesterday.

The younger brother of Rangers third baseman Josh Jung, Jace has appeared in parts of three major league seasons. He’s totaled only 160 big league plate appearances and carries an ugly.193/.319/.230 batting line. Jung has walked in a stout 15% of his plate appearances but has also fanned at an untenable 30%.

Jung’s time in Detroit’s minor league system has had its ups and downs but has generally been productive. He’s posted an.801 OPS or better at each individual minor league level, including a career.244/.362/.439 slash in 1478 Triple-A plate appearances across the past three seasons. That said, Jung’s production in Triple-A has dipped with each repeat of the level; this year, he produced only a.227/.344/.421 slash in 133 games. By measure of wRC+, he was still seven percent better than average (thanks to that big OBP), but Jung didn’t make particularly strong levels of contact (88.6 mph average exit velocity, 36.5% hard-hit rate).

articles.title: The Best Fits For Trevor Rogers
body: MLBTR’s series of examining the market for the best free agents continues. We’re on to Trevor Rogers, the only starting pitcher who declined the qualifying offer and arguably the #2 pitcher in the class. Rogers’ first couple seasons were up and down, with his career reaching a nadir when he was optioned to Triple-A by the Orioles within three weeks of that club acquiring him at the 2024 deadline. He was in the minors as recently as June 2025, as Baltimore’s acquisition of the southpaw for Kyle Stowers and Connor Norby initially looked disastrous.

Rogers flipped a switch midway through the’25 campaign. He managed a sub-2.00 ERA in his final 17 starts of that season, going from rotation depth to Opening Day starter in 2026. Rogers had a rocky opening to the’26 campaign and missed a couple weeks due to illness, but he was lights out again for the final four months of the season. Rogers pitched to a 2.90 ERA with a 24.8% strikeout rate and tidy 4.4% walk rate from June 1 onward. Only seven pitchers threw more innings than his 121 frames in that stretch.

The former first-rounder is up to 47 starts with a 3.23 earned run average since he returned to the big leagues last June. He’s fanned 23.2% of opponents against a 6.2% walk rate while averaging nearly six innings per start. Rogers doesn’t have the huge swing-and-miss rates associated with most top-end starters, but he gets excellent life on a 94 mph fastball that opponents have a difficult time squaring up. He’s fifth in infield pop-up rate among pitchers with 200+ innings over the last two seasons.

articles.title: Giants Open To Offers On Casey Schmitt In Search For Pitching Help
body: As the Giants scour the market for pitching help, they’ve floated the possibility of trading infielder/outfielder Casey Schmitt, reports Jeff Passan of ESPN. There’s no indication any sort of deal is close, but Schmitt is the type of controllable infielder who could net them some needed arms.

Schmitt, 28 in March, swatted a career-high 21 home runs this past season while slashing.271/.301/.478. His 2.7% walk rate ranked dead last among the 205 big leaguers who totaled at least 400 plate appearances, but a lack of plate discipline seemed to permeate the entire 2026 Giants roster; San Francisco’s 7.4% walk rate was also the worst in baseball, and several Giants hitters posted career-worst walk rates in’26. Schmitt himself walked at a much healthier (albeit still below-average) 7.8% rate as recently as the 2025 season.

While Schmitt has long graded as a plus defender at third base, that spot is spoken for by Matt Chapman. Willy Adames is locked in at shortstop. Rafael Devers and Bryce Eldridge have first base and designated hitter covered. Schmitt could play second base, but if the Giants want to get a real look at former top prospect Marcelo Mayer — who came over from the Red Sox in the Erik Miller deadline swap — that’s the only available spot for Mayer, a former No. 4 overall draft pick.

articles.title: Royals, Mariners Swap Maikel Garcia For Bryce Miller In Six-Player Deal
body: The Mariners and Royals have lined up on a six-player blockbuster, announcing Wednesday that infielder Maikel Garcia, reliever James McArthur and left-handed pitching prospect L.P. Langevin are going from Kansas City to Seattle in exchange for right-handed starters Bryce Miller and Logan Evans as well as left-handed reliever Jose A. Ferrer.

Seattle was known to be hunting for an infielder on the left side to pair with young shortstop Colt Emerson. Kansas City was in the market for pitching help. Both sides accomplished their goals with today’s deal. Garcia was an All-Star and Gold Glove award winner in 2025. Miller will immediately slot into the Royals’ rotation, with Ferrer potentially taking over as closer and at the very least filling a key late-inning role.

Garcia inked a five-year, $57.5MM extension covering the 2026-30 seasons just last winter. The deal also includes a $21MM club option ($3.2MM buyout) for the 2031 season. It added an extra two years of club control, with the club option factored in. Garcia is set to make $7MM in 2027.

After serving as a speedy utility option in his first few seasons, Garcia broke out as a critical cog in Kansas City’s lineup in 2025. He slashed.286/.351/.449 with 16 homers and 23 steals as the everyday third baseman. Garcia posted a career-best 120 wRC+ across 666 plate appearances.

articles.title: Nationals To Sign Hagen Danner To Minor League Deal
body: The Nationals are adding right-hander Hagen Danner on a minor league agreement, reports Spencer Nusbaum of The Athletic. He spent last season in the minors with the Reds and Angels.

The 28-year-old Danner posted a 6.35 ERA in 37 appearances at Triple-A in 2026. He had a middling 22.1% strikeout rate and a massive 15.6% walk rate. Danner was in Spring Training with the Reds and pitched well over nine games (3.12 ERA, 28.6% strikeout rate). He didn’t break camp with the team and struggled with Louisville. Cincinnati released him in July. He latched on with the Angels in August.

Danner was drafted by the Blue Jays out of high school in 2017. He was a catcher back then. Danner transitioned to pitching in 2021. He posted solid results in the minors with Toronto and earned a brief look in the majors in 2023. Danner recorded one out before leaving with an oblique injury in his lone appearance.
The oblique strain ended Danner’s 2023 campaign. He never made it back up with the Blue Jays and was designated for assignment at the end of the 2024 season. He was in Seattle’s system in 2025.

Danner was generally a two-pitch guy at Triple-A this past year. He leaned on a mid-80s slider more than half of the time. He threw a four-seamer that sat at 96.3 mph at a 46.1% clip. Danner also used the occasional sinker and cutter. The pitch mix resulted in an underwhelming 10% swinging-strike rate this season. He’ll likely need to miss more bats and throw more strikes to get another look in the majors.

articles.title: Ryan Jeffers Declined Multi-Year Offer From Twins To Accept QO
body: Ryan Jeffers will be back in Minnesota for another season. The slugging catcher surprisingly accepted the one-year, $23.15MM qualifying offer this afternoon — just days after reports that he planned to decline in search of a multi-year deal. Jeffers apparently had at least one multi-year offer on the table from his longtime club.

Dan Hayes of The Athletic reports that Jeffers rejected a multi-year proposal from the Twins in favor of the QO. Financial terms of that offer aren’t clear, though the 29-year-old clearly preferred to bet on himself with the hefty salary. Jeffers narrowly secured the record for highest salary by a catcher in history, beating the $23.1MM average annual value of J.T. Realmuto’s five-year contract with Philadelphia. (Yankees reliever David Bednar coincidentally also narrowly locked in the salary record at his position as the only other player in this year’s class to accept the qualifying offer.)

Nothing stops the Twins and Jeffers from continuing to discuss multi-year frameworks now that the QO is in place. However, Jeffers seemed excited about the idea of betting on himself with the short-term commitment. “(Owner Tom Pohlad’s) commitments to the 2027 team and the team going forward plays a factor in me coming back and wanting to see where this core goes,” he told Hayes. “Taking the one-year deal gives us opportunities that something else might not.”

articles.title: Mariners, Bryce Conley Agree To Minor League Deal
body: The Mariners are in agreement with right-hander Bryce Conley on a minor league contract, reports Will Sammon of The Athletic. He’ll be in camp as a non-roster invitee.

Conley, 32, spent the 2026 season in the Mets’ system. He started 18 of 29 games between Double-A Binghamton and Triple-A Syracuse, working 111 2/3 innings of 5.48 ERA ball. Conley recorded a combined 23.6% strikeout percentage against 10.7% walk rate, though his underlying numbers were much better at Double-A than against Triple-A opposition.

The Mets called Conley up on August 2 this past season. He was on the roster for one game, didn’t pitch, then got designated for assignment. Conley cleared waivers and qualified for minor league free agency at season’s end. He’s currently a phantom ballplayer but will keep plugging away in hopes of making his debut.

articles.title: Giants Designate Christian Koss, Rowan Wick For Assignment
body: The Giants added three pitching prospects to their 40-man roster on Rule 5 protection day: righties Marty Gair and Josh Bostick plus southpaw Henry Lalane. San Francisco designated reliever Rowan Wick and infielder Christian Koss for assignment in corresponding moves. They already had one opening on the 40-man roster after trading former closer Ryan Walker to Milwaukee over the weekend.

Koss has played in 144 games for San Francisco over the last two seasons. He was close to a league average hitter as a rookie but couldn’t maintain that in 2026. Koss is coming off a.217/.257/.305 slash line with four homers over 221 plate appearances. Even with solid defensive grades around the infield, the bat was light enough to squeeze him off the roster.

The Giants signed Wick to a free agent contract last winter. The righty was coming off a productive run in Japan but was slated to miss the entire 2026 season rehabbing from Tommy John surgery. The Giants took a year to gauge his recovery and determine if they wanted to devote a bullpen spot next season. It was pretty clear they were leaning against that when they declined his $800K club option at the beginning of the offseason.

articles.title: Padres Select Tucker Musgrove, Ian Koenig
body: The Padres announced they’ve selected right-handed pitchers Tucker Musgrove and Ian Koenig onto the 40-man roster. Both players would otherwise have been eligible for the Rule 5 draft, assuming it takes place. San Diego’s roster count climbs to 35.

Musgrove, who is not related to Joe Musgrove, was a seventh-round pick in 2023. A two-way player at NAIA University of Mobile, he became a full-time pitcher in pro ball. Musgrove underwent elbow surgery in his draft year and didn’t throw a professional pitch until 2025. He’s a pure reliever who split the’26 campaign between High-A and Double-A. Musgrove walked 16% of opponents but had an eye-popping 42.8% strikeout rate across 34 1/3 innings, overpowering hitters with an upper 90s fastball with life at the top of the zone.

Koenig has a dramatically different profile. He’s a former undrafted free agent who has been a strike-throwing depth starter in the minors. Koenig made 29 starts and threw 148 1/3 innings this year, finishing the season in Triple-A. He combined for a 4.19 earned run average with a modest 19.4% strikeout rate but only walked 6% of opponents. Koenig threw six pitches in his Triple-A work but relied mostly on a sinker-slider combination, averaging 94 mph on the fastball.

articles.title: Tigers Designate Four Players For Assignment
body: The Tigers announced they’ve designated four players for assignment: infielders Jace Jung and Trey Sweeney, outfielder Matt Vierling, and left-handed pitcher Jake Miller. That clears 40-man roster space for them to finalize the Emilio Pagán signing and select Josue Briceño, Max Anderson and Peyton Graham onto the roster. The three prospects would otherwise have been eligible for the Rule 5 draft.

Vierling was one of the league’s more obvious non-tender candidates. The 30-year-old was projected by MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz for a $3.7MM salary in his final year of arbitration eligibility. He’s coming off a second straight injury-wrecked season, as an adductor strain cost him the final two months. He didn’t perform well even when healthy, batting.207/.255/.335 across 291 plate appearances.

Jung, who turned 26 last month, was the 12th overall pick in 2022. He ranked among the organization’s top prospects for a while but has stalled out in the upper minors. He’s coming off a league average.227/.344/.421 batting line in Triple-A, albeit with 22 home runs. Jung only played six MLB games this year and has a.193/.319/.230 slash in 160 plate appearances at the highest level.

Detroit acquired Sweeney from the Dodgers in the 2024 Jack Flaherty deadline deal. He took over as their primary shortstop down the stretch, improving the infield defense but not providing much at the plate. Sweeney batted.202/.261/.313 across 445 big league plate appearances in 2024-25. He missed the entire’26 season to a right shoulder injury that required arthroscopic surgery in June.

articles.title: Cubs Select Jaxon Wiggins, Brody McCullough
body: The Cubs announced that they have selected right-handers Jaxon Wiggins and Brody McCullough to the 40-man roster. Those players are now protected from the Rule 5 draft, if it even takes place this offseason. The club’s 40-man roster count is now at 36.

The 2021 Rule 5 draft was put on pause as part of the lockout that took place that offseason. It wasn’t clear what would eventually happen. Once the league and the players reached a new deal in March, the draft was scrapped.

This year’s draft is scheduled for December 9, one week after the league is expected to lock out the players again. It’s possible the draft will be banged once more but that’s not guaranteed, so clubs have to proceed as though it might still take place. Some borderline additions might be left unprotected but teams aren’t going to take chances with really notable prospects.

The decision was fairly straightforward with Wiggins, who is now 25 years old. Baseball America lists him as the #4 prospect in the Cubs’ system. He has big strikeout stuff but has had issues controlling it. BA notes that his fastball sits in the upper-90s. He also features a slider, changeup and curveball.

articles.title: Orioles Select Seven Players
body: The Orioles have the league’s biggest group of newcomers on Rule 5 protection day. Baltimore added seven players to their 40-man roster: outfielder Enrique Bradfield Jr., infielder Aron Estrada and pitchers Braxton Bragg, Michael Forret, Nestor German, Patrick Reilly and Levi Wells.

Baltimore dropped four pitchers on waivers this afternoon, released outfielder Rece Hinds to pursue a KBO opportunity, and announced that catcher Zach Morgan cleared waivers and was outrighted to Triple-A Norfolk. Morgan was just claimed off waivers from San Francisco a few weeks ago and will remain in the organization in a non-roster capacity. After all that, their 40-man roster count sits at 38.

Bradfield was the O’s first-round pick in 2023. The speedster batted.263/.344/.363 with 36 stolen bases in 88 Triple-A games this year. He could soon challenge Colton Cowser for center field reps. Estrada is a switch-hitting second baseman who hit.281/.325/.482 with 25 homers in the upper minors this year. He spent most of the season in Double-A.

Forret is probably the most highly regarded of the five pitchers. Baltimore reacquired him from the Rays this summer in the Tyler Wells deal. The 6’3″ righty worked 115 2/3 innings of 3.89 ERA ball with a 25.4% strikeout rate in the upper minors this year. He’ll need to throw more strikes but has a chance to be a league average starter. German could also pitch at the back of the Baltimore rotation as soon as next season, as he’s coming off a 4.08 ERA with a solid strikeout and walk profile over 117 innings with Norfolk.

articles.title: Athletics Acquire Yaqui Rivera From Orioles
body: The Athletics announced they’ve acquired right-hander Yaqui Rivera from the Orioles for minor league righty Josiah Romeo. They added Rivera to their 40-man roster to keep him out of the Rule 5 draft. The A’s also selected catcher Cole Conn onto the roster and designated righties Yunior Tur and Hayden Juenger for assignment.

Rivera adds multi-inning relief depth to the upper levels of the system. The 6’2″ righty initially signed with the Marlins out of the Dominican Republic. Baltimore acquired him as a player to be named later in the 2022 trade that sent Tanner Scott to Miami. Rivera has mostly worked in long relief since then, racking up big strikeout totals with elevated walk rates.

Eric Longenhagen and Brendan Gawlowski of FanGraphs ranked Rivera the #53 prospect in the Baltimore system back in May. They wrote that while he doesn’t have the huge velocity associated with back-end relievers, he has the potential for an above-average to plus slider and changeup. Rivera used a four-pitch mix in Triple-A this year, sitting in the 93-95 mph range while featuring the aforementioned pair of secondaries. He combined for 79 2/3 innings of 3.28 ERA ball between Double-A and Triple-A, striking out 29% of batters faced against a 12% walk rate.

articles.title: Dodgers Designate Jake Cousins, Christian Cairo For Assignment
body: The Dodgers announced they’ve designated reliever Jake Cousins and infielder Christian Cairo for assignment. They needed to open two spots on the 40-man roster to select four pitchers: righty Christian Zazueta and left-handers Jackson Ferris, Adam Serwinowski and Luke Fox. The four prospects are kept out of the Rule 5 draft if it takes place.

Neither Cousins nor Cairo has played in a game for Los Angeles. The Dodgers signed Cousins to a $950K free agent contract last offseason. The righty was rehabbing from June 2025 Tommy John surgery, so the Dodgers hoped he could be a factor late in the season. Cousins was able to embark on a late rehab assignment but walked five batters across 4 1/3 innings at Triple-A Oklahoma City and was never reinstated from the injured list.

MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz projected Cousins for a minimal raise to $1MM if tendered an arbitration contract. This is very likely a precursor to a non-tender on Friday, though they’ll have the intervening few days to see if there’s a trade out there.

Cairo was claimed off waivers from the Mets last week. The glove-first infielder has yet to play at the MLB level. He split the’26 campaign between the Triple-A clubs of the Mets and Phillies, batting.230/.381/.300 over 525 plate appearances. The Mets signed Cairo to a pre-arbitration split contract before putting him on waivers, hoping it’d allow them to sneak him to Triple-A. The Dodgers have five days to trade him or try to get him through waivers themselves.

articles.title: Brewers Select Six Players
body: The Brewers announced that they have selected six players to the 40-man roster. They are infielders Luke Adams and Dylan O’Rae, catcher Matt Wood, left-hander Tate Kuehner, right-hander Cameron Wagoner, and infielder/outfielder Jett Williams. Those players are now protected from being selected in the Rule 5 draft, if it even takes place this offseason.
Milwaukee had multiple 40-man vacancies, but the roster is now full. MLBTR covered the Williams move earlier today.

Outside of Williams, Adams is the most well-regarded name in the group. He’s hit at every level since getting drafted in 2022. Adams flashed surprising speed for a corner infielder in his first three pro seasons, but has settled into the 8-10 steal range recently. The bat is his primary tool right now. Adams delivered a 154 wRC+ in 71 games this past season, with the majority of that action coming at Triple-A. He could factor into the mix at first base with the Brewers in 2027, particularly with Jake Bauers signing elsewhere.

O’Rae has an old-school middle infielder profile, with tons of speed and basically no power. The 22-year-old has stolen 60+ bags in each of his last two healthy seasons. He missed all of 2025 with an injury, but came back in 2026 and hit.273 with 63 steals at Double-A. Rae hit three homers, which was more than he had in his pro career heading into the year.

articles.title: Cardinals Designate Max Rajcic For Assignment
body: The Cardinals announced they’ve designated right-hander Max Rajcic for assignment. They had one opening on the 40-man roster but needed a second to select infielder Jesús Báez and right-hander Jacob Odle, both of whom are now protected from the Rule 5 draft.

It’s a tough break for Rajcic, who was always going to have a difficult time holding his roster spot all winter. The righty made his MLB debut in July but blew out after six games and required Tommy John surgery. He’ll probably miss all of 2027. The Cardinals can keep him in DFA limbo until Friday and then decline to tender him a contract, which will send him directly to free agency without waivers. At that point, they can try to bring the 2022 sixth-round pick back on a two-year minor league contract.

Báez was the team’s obvious choice to keep out of the Rule 5. Acquired from the Mets at the 2025 deadline in the Ryan Helsley trade, he raked at a.283/.328/.587 clip with 39 homers in his first full season in the St. Louis system. Báez ranks as the organization’s #6 prospect at Baseball America. He’ll need to improve his pitch recognition as he faces higher level pitching but clearly has huge power for a player who won’t turn 22 until February.

articles.title: Rockies Select Three Players
body: The Rockies selected the contracts of catcher Bryant Betancourt and right-handers Jackson Cox and Jack Mahoney, per a team announcement. Colorado’s 40-man roster is now at 39 players.

Cox was a second-round pick in 2022. Injuries have slowed his rise through the system. His first pro season was cut short by an elbow issue that required Tommy John surgery. After missing the entire 2024 campaign, Cox made 23 starts at Single-A in 2025.

The 23-year-old Cox made the jump to Double-A this past season. He recorded a 4.25 ERA across a career-best 97 1/3 innings. Cox had a strong 30.9% strikeout rate and kept his walk rate under 10%. MLB Pipeline ranks him eighth among the Rockies’ prospects. Brendan Gawlowski of FanGraphs was a bit lower on Cox, ranking him 20th heading into the season.

Betancourt hit.271 with a career-high 17 home runs between Double-A and Triple-A in 2026. He makes plenty of contact, but hadn’t shown much power until this year. The 23-year-old struggled when he reached the highest minor-league level. Betancourt posted a 79 wRC+ in 38 games with Albuquerque.

Mahoney hit a similar road bump when he made it to Triple-A. After 13 starts with a sub-2.00 ERA at Double-A, he moved on to Albuquerque. The 25-year-old was knocked around for 23 earned runs in 33 1/3 innings with the Isotopes. Mahoney throws strikes, but he’s had a tough time missing bats as he’s moved through the minor league ranks. Colorado tends to churn through arms, so Mahoney could get a look with the big-league club sometime in 2027.

articles.title: Reds Select Carter Graham
body: The Reds announced that infielder/outfielder Carter Graham has been selected to the 40-man roster. That protects him from being exposed in the Rule 5 draft, if it takes place this offseason. Cincinnati had multiple 40-man vacancies, so no corresponding move was required.

Graham, 25, was an eighth-round pick in 2023. He wasn’t really on the prospect radar until a monster showing at the plate this year. Carter made 552 plate appearances in 2026 between High-A and Double-A. He hit 29 home runs and drew walks at a 14.5% clip while only striking out 21.2% of the time. That led to a combined batting line of.300/.421/.565 and a 151 wRC+.

Defensively, he is mostly a first baseman. He has a bit of experience at third base and left field but isn’t considered a terribly realistic options for those spots. With that profile, he really needs to hit, but that’s just what he did in 2026. Baseball America now lists him as the #26 prospect in the system.

It’s not clear if the Rule 5 draft will happen this year. In the last lockout, five years ago, it was held in suspended animation as part of the larger transaction freeze. Once a new deal was reached in March, the draft was scrapped. It’s possible the same could happen this year but it’s not guaranteed. The Reds didn’t want to take any chances with Graham, so he gets a roster spot today.

articles.title: Marlins Select Four Players
body: The Marlins announced that they have selected right-handers Jace Beck, Eliazar Dishmey, and Brandon White, as well as infielder Juan Matheus, to the 40-man roster. Those players are now protected from being selected in the Rule 5 draft, if it takes place this offseason.

Miami had five 40-man vacancies and therefore doesn’t need to make any corresponding moves. Prior to the official announcement, Matheus and Dishmey were reported by Isaac Azout of Fish on First. White was first reported by Christina De Nicola of MLB.com.

Beck came to the organization at the trade deadline in the deal that sent lefty Braxton Garrett to the Cubs. The Marlins also received infielder Jonathon Long in the swap. After a nice start to the season at Double-A, Chicago moved Beck to Triple-A. He pitched poorly in five appearances before the trade. Miami assigned Beck to Jacksonville to close the season. He posted a 6.66 ERA across six starts. He’s likely opening next season with the Jumbo Shrimp.

Dishmey put together a strong season split between High-A and Double-A. He finished with a sub-3.00 ERA and a 33.3% strikeout rate across 23 starts. An 11.2% walk rate isn’t ideal, but Dishmey has shown better control at other stops. He got the free passes down closer to 10% after moving to Double-A. Dishmey has a solid four-pitch mix. FanGraphs doesn’t grade any of his pitches as above-average, but the fastball, curveball, and changeup project to be decent offerings.

articles.title: Guardians Make Multiple Roster Moves
body: The Guardians announced that right-hander Justin Campbell, catcher Kody Huff, and outfielder Jaison Chourio were selected to the 40-man roster.

Chourio is the most well-regarded prospect of the group. MLB Pipeline had him at No. 5 in Cleveland’s system. Chourio slashed.274/.376/.408 in 114 games split between High-A and Double-A in 2026. He stole 40+ bases for the second time in the past three years.

The 21-year-old is the younger brother of the Brewers’ Jackson Chourio. He hasn’t shown the power of his brother, but his speed and on-base skills have been strong in the minors. Chourio could factor into the Guardians’ underwhelming outfield mix as soon as 2027.

Cleveland took Campbell with the 37th overall pick in the 2022 draft. Persistent injuries delayed his pro debut until this season. The righty moved quickly through the system this year, advancing to Triple-A by the end of the campaign. Campbell compiled a 2.48 ERA in 20 starts across three levels.

The 20 starts are a bit deceiving from a workload perspective. Campbell was limited to shorter outings and only tossed 69 innings. He completed five innings in just three appearances. Like Chourio, he’s a candidate to contribute for the big-league squad next year.

The Guardians acquired Huff from the Rockies straight up for righty Cal Quantrill in November 2023. He’d been a middling producer in the minors until this past season. Huff broke out in 2026, posting a 132 wRC+ with 23 homers and 12 steals at Triple-A. He’d totaled 18 home runs in his previous four years as a pro.

articles.title: Blue Jays Select Three Players
body: The Blue Jays announced that they selected outfielder RJ Schreck as well as right-handers Nolan Perry and Daniel Guerra to the 40-man roster. That protects those players from being selected in the Rule 5 draft, if it actually takes place this offseason. Toronto had three 40-man vacancies, so no corresponding moves were necessary.

Five years ago, the Rule 5 draft was held in a limbo state until the lockout was ended, at which point it was scrapped. This year’s draft is scheduled for December 9, a week after the league is expected to lock out the players again. Teams can’t assume that history will repeat itself this time around, so they have to still add any players they don’t want to be at risk of being snaked.

Perry, 23, was the easiest call of this bunch. A 12th-round pick from 2022, Baseball America lists him as Toronto’s #4 prospect. UCL surgery wiped out his 2025 but he got back on track in 2026. He went from Single-A to High-A and Double-A, throwing 82 2/3 innings over 21 games. 20 of those were officially starts, as he pitched behind an opener once. He allowed just 2.50 earned runs per nine on the year while striking out 36% of batters faced.

He only has nine Double-A starts under his belt so far. It’s possible he returns to that level to begin 2027 but it wouldn’t be a surprise if he jumped up to Triple-A and was knocking on the door of the big leagues by season’s end.

articles.title: Diamondbacks Select Six Players
body: The Diamondbacks have selected six players to their 40-man roster, reports Nick Piecoro of The Arizona Republic. The six are infielders Demetrio Crisantes and Cristofer Torin, outfielder Druw Jones, left-hander Spencer Giesting, as well as right-handers Ashton Izzi and Wellington Aracena. Those players are now protected from being selected in the Rule 5 draft, if it takes place. Arizona had seven vacancies on the 40-man roster coming into today so no corresponding moves will be required.

It’s unclear if there will even be a Rule 5 draft this winter. It is scheduled for December 9, a week after the league is expected to lock out the players. Five years ago, the draft was held in limbo until the lockout ended, at which point it was canceled. It’s not a guarantee that the same thing will happen this offseason, so teams still have to give roster spots to any eligible players they don’t want to risk losing.

Jones is perhaps the most recognizable name in the bunch because he is the son of Hall-of-Famer Andruw Jones. The younger Jones was taken by the Snakes with the second overall pick in the 2022 draft. Prospect evaluators often compare him to his father, especially when it comes to his speed and defense. The big question with Jones what he can do from the batter’s box. Jones will take his walks but doesn’t have huge power and strikes out a decent amount.

articles.title: Rays Select Xavier Isaac
body: The Rays selected first base prospect Xavier Isaac onto the 40-man roster. They already had a roster opening, so they won’t need any further moves if he’s the only player they’re protecting from the Rule 5 draft.

Isaac, 23 next month, was Tampa Bay’s first-round pick back in 2022. The lefty-hitting first baseman has top of the scale raw power but began to run into strikeout issues at the High-A level. He continued to walk at huge rates and hit for power, playing his way to Double-A. Isaac was limited to 41 games at that level in 2025 by what was initially an undisclosed injury.

Last offseason, Isaac announced that he’d required a life-saving brain surgery in July 2025. He made it back onto the field this year and had a monster season between the top two minor league levels. Isaac popped 27 homers while hitting.258/.402/.510. He walked at a huge 18.8% clip while striking out 28.4% of the time.

Isaac spent most of the season with Double-A Montgomery. He played his way to Triple-A at the end of August and continued to hit. While his short-term big league path is blocked by Yandy Díaz and Jonathan Aranda, he could be up next season if either player suffers an injury. Díaz is entering the final year of his contract, which would open a path to regular playing time by 2028.

articles.title: Rays Exploring Nick Fortes Trade
body: The Rays are exploring trades involving backup catcher Nick Fortes, reports Marc Topkin of The Tampa Bay Times. Topin subsequently added that talks are ongoing with multiple clubs and it’s unlikely an agreement will be reached tonight.

If a deal is ultimately completed, it’ll end Fortes’ time in Tampa Bay after a season and a half. The Rays brought him in from Miami at the 2025 trade deadline. Fortes split the next calendar year with Hunter Feduccia in a fairly even split of playing time. He was pushed firmly into a backup role when the Rays acquired Liam Hicks (who’d coincidentally also cut into his playing time in Miami) in a four-player trade with the Marlins.

Fortes, who celebrated his 30th birthday last week, is a well-rounded role player. He typically rates as a solid pitch framer and blocker, though his framing grades this past season were a little below average. Fortes has thrown out just shy of 20% of base stealers in his career, slightly below the league mark. He ranks in the top third of the league in average pop time, making up for fringy arm strength with an efficient transfer.

While it’s primarily a glove-first profile, Fortes held his own at the plate this year. He tallied 323 plate appearances and batted.258/.304/.376 with six home runs. Fortes doesn’t have much power but puts a lot of balls in play, striking out less than 14% of the time. His.690 OPS matched the exact league average for catchers this year.

articles.title: Yankees Select Carlos Lagrange
body: 4:45 pm: The Yankees have officially announced the move. The club also announced that left-hander Kyle Carr and outfielder Garrett Martin were added to the 40-man roster.

4:06 pm: The Yankees are expected to select the contract of right-hander Carlos Lagrange, per Francys Romero of BeisbolFR. Adding Lagrange to the 40-man roster protects him from the upcoming Rule 5 Draft.

The 23-year-old Lagrange is one of the top prospects in New York’s system. It comes as no surprise that the club made the move to protect him. Lagrange was rumored as an option for the bullpen this past season, but was never promoted. He’ll be looming once again in 2027.

Lagrange made the jump to Triple-A this past season. He struck out opponents at a near-30% clip, a skill he’s shown consistently in the minors. He had an 11.6% walk rate, also something he’s shown throughout his pro career. A spike in homers contributed to a 4.48 ERA.

The final 2026 line wasn’t amazing, but Lagrange showcased the stuff that has long intrigued scouts. The righty sat at 99 mph with his four-seamer. His sinker was right up there at 98.3 mph. Lagrange also throws a hard slider and a firm changeup, both of which average above 90 mph. He rounds out the arsenal with a mid-80s sweeper.

articles.title: Pirates Select Mitch Jebb, Axiel Plaz
body: The Pirates announced are keeping two players out of the Rule 5 draft in the event it takes place. Pittsburgh selected catcher/first baseman Axiel Plaz and outfielder Mitch J ebb with their two open spots on the 40-man roster.

Plaz was one of the easier calls for any team to keep out of the draft. FanGraphs listed him among the top 100 prospects in the sport over the summer. Baseball America slotted him sixth in the Pittsburgh system in their refreshed organizational rankings last week. Plaz, a right-handed hitter out of Venezuela, raked at a.305/.389/.513 clip with 18 home runs across 412 plate appearances in High-A this year.

Teams won’t leave any Top 100 caliber prospect unprotected even if they’re nowhere close to big league readiness. While it’s unlikely Plaz would be able to hit MLB pitching next season, there’s a good chance a rebuilding team would’ve stashed him on the bench for a year to take a shot on his long-term upside. He’s a work in progress behind the plate and needs to hit the ball in the air more often to tap into his immense raw power, but he’s a talented developmental play as a 21-year-old. He’ll likely open the season in Double-A whenever the lockout is lifted.

articles.title: Astros Select Jackson Nezuh
body: The Astros announced that they have selected right-hander Jackson Nezuh to the 40-man roster. That protects him from being selected in the Rule 5 draft, if it takes place this offseason. The club also announced that outfielder Joey Loperfido has been outrighted to Triple-A Sugar Land. It was reported earlier today that Loperfido was on outright waivers. Houston’s 40-man roster count is now at 39.

Nezuh, 25 in February, was a 14th-round pick in the 2023 draft. He has been working his way up the ladder since then as a multi-inning guy, sometimes as the official starter and sometimes entering games a bit later.

He tossed 103 1/3 innings this year split between Double-A and Triple-A, allowing 3.83 earned runs per nine. His 28.1% strikeout rate was quite strong but he also gave out free passes at a high rate of 11.3%. Baseball America lists Nezuh as Houston’s #18 prospect, noting that he has a five-pitch arsenal that includes a four-seamer, slider, sweeper, curveball and changeup.

It’s unclear whether the Rule 5 draft will take place this offseason. During the 2021-22 lockout, the draft was held in a limbo state but was eventually scrapped once the lockout ended. This year’s draft is scheduled for December 9, a week after the league is expected to lock out the players again. Teams can’t know for sure whether this offseason will follow the same script, so they still have to select players they don’t want plucked away.

articles.title: Mets Select Jefferson Rojas
body: The Mets have selected infielder Jefferson Rojas’ contract, Will Sammon of The Athletic reports. In other moves, New York signed right-hander Chayce McDermott to a major league contract and designated righty Dylan Ross for assignment.

For the Mets, adding Rojas to the 40-man roster before Tuesday’s 6 p.m. deadline was a no-brainer. Otherwise, the team would have been in danger of losing one of its prized prospects to a potential Rule 5 draft this winter. Rojas, whom New York acquired from the Cubs for righty Clay Holmes and outfielder Tyrone Taylor at this year’s trade deadline, ranks as MLB Pipeline’s 68th-best prospect. The 21-year-old is also the Mets’ top-rated farmhand.

The Mets gave Rojas his first-ever Triple-A promotion in mid-September, and he proceeded to slash.308/.345/.692 with three home runs. While that was over a tiny sample of six games and 29 plate appearances, it was a nice way for the righty-swinging Rojas to end the season. He spent most of the year at the Double-A level, where he swatted 24 homers and stole 20 bases in 525 trips to the plate. After the trade, Rojas turned in a quality.280/.336/.593 line with nine HRs and three steals over 135 plate appearances with the Mets’ Double-A affiliate. Along the way, he went down on strikes just 17.8% percent of the time and drew walks at an 8.1% clip.

articles.title: Brewers To Select Jett Williams
body: The Brewers are going to select infielder/outfielder Jett Williams to the 40-man roster, reports Pat Ragazzo of FanSided. Milwaukee has multiple 40-man vacancies and doesn’t need to make a corresponding move. This transaction prevents Williams from being selected in the Rule 5 draft, if it takes place this offseason.

Williams, now 23, was selected by the Mets with the 14th overall pick in the 2022 draft. In January of this year, he was traded to the Brewers alongside right-hander Brandon Sproat in the deal that sent righties Freddy Peralta and Tobias Myers to Queens.

In 2025, Williams had a strong season in 130 games in the minors. His 22.9% strikeout rate was right around par and his 13.3% walk rate was quite strong. He hit 17 home runs and slashed.261/.363/.465 for a 136 wRC+. He also stole 34 bases.

His production declined this year. He was on and off the injured list with wrist injury and only played 81 games. His walk and strikeout profile held steady but he slashed just.233/.340/.384 while the offensive environment in the International League surged, leading to a 96 wRC+. Despite the down year, Williams still has a strong prospect pedigree. Baseball America lists him as the #8 player in Milwaukee’s system and he was a Top 100 guy a couple of years ago.

articles.title: Five Players Reject Qualifying Offer
body: The deadline for players to accept or reject the qualifying offer has now passed. Eight players received a QO. Ryan Jeffers and David Bednar accepted offers from the Twins and Yankees, respectively. Jake Bauers received a QO from the Brewers but already signed with the Red Sox. The other five players have declined, per Alden González of ESPN. Randy Arozarena rejected an offer from the Mariners, Seiya Suzuki from the Cubs, Trevor Rogers from the Orioles, Brandon Lowe from the Pirates and Adrián Morejón from the Padres. Morejón’s decision was previously reported.

The value of the QO is set by averaging the salaries of the 125 highest paid players in the league. This year’s was set at $23.15MM. A team can issue a QO to any impending free agent who has never received one before and who spent the entirety of the most recent season with that club. If the player rejects and signs elsewhere, the team receives draft pick compensation. The signing team would be subject to penalties.

It’s not really a surprise that any of these players rejected. The five players are among the best at their respective positions. Rogers is clearly behind Tarik Skubal but is arguably the best starting pitcher available apart from that. Suzuki and Arozarena are the top two outfielders on the market. Lowe is arguably the top second baseman, depending on how one feels about Jazz Chisholm Jr. and/or Luis Arraez. Morejón is the top reliever.

articles.title: Royals Select Carson Roccaforte, Lucas Braun; Nick Mears Designated For Assignment
body: The Royals have selected the contracts of outfielder Carson Roccaforte and right-hander Lucas Braun, the team announced. In a corresponding move, the Royals designated righty reliever Nick Mears for assignment. They now have a full 40-man roster.

By adding Roccaforte and Braun to their 40-man, the Royals will erase any chance of losing either or both players in the Rule 5 draft this winter. The event might not take place at all because of the impending lockout, but Kansas City wasn’t going to leave valuable prospects unprotected. Both Roccaforte (No. 17) and Braun (No. 16) are among the Royals’ top 20 farmhands at MLB Pipeline.

Roccaforte, whom the Royals took in the second round of the 2023 amateur draft, is a well-regarded defender who has put up good offensive numbers in the minors. After slashing.251/.333/.523 with 30 home runs and 21 stolen bases at the Double-A level in 2026, the lefty-hitting 24-year-old earned a promotion to Triple-A Omaha in late August. In his first action with the Storm Chasers, he put up an even stronger.284/.362/.500 line with five homers and 11 steals in 118 trips to the plate. While Roccaforte posted a solid 10.5% walk rate between the two levels, he also went down on strikes at a 29.1% clip. High strikeout and low contact rates are among the knocks on Roccaforte, but there is a chance he will earn first call to the majors next season. Those odds may increase if the Royals non-tender center fielder Kyle Isbel, whom they could move on from in lieu of paying a projected $3.5MM salary in arbitration.

articles.title: Ryan Jeffers To Accept Qualifying Offer
body: Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers has opted to accept his $23.15MM qualifying offer, reports Tyler Kepner of The Athletic. It’ll immediately (and narrowly) establish a new AAV record for catchers, which had previously been held by J.T. Realmuto at $23.1MM (on a much longer, five-year term). Jeffers, a Boras Corporation client, heads back to the Twins on a one-year deal. It’s an about-face for the slugging backstop, who as of last week was reportedly planning to decline in search of a longer-term deal.

It’s a surprise outcome but surely one the Twins welcome. General manager Jeremy Zoll had already spoken about his hope to retain the 29-year-old Jeffers. The two parties had discussed parameters of contracts beyond just the QO acceptance, Zoll noted last week. Perhaps today’s decision to accept the QO is just a waypoint on the road to a more lucrative multi-year deal that’ll keep Jeffers with the only organization he’s known, but even if that’s not the case, it’s a nice outcome for the Twins.

Had Jeffers departed, Minnesota would have picked up a compensatory draft pick but been left without a clear starting option in 2027. Veteran Victor Caratini is signed through 2027 but is coming off a down year at the plate. Jeffers will step into the primary catching role and push Caratini to a backup role for which he’s better suited. (It’s also possible the Twins look to trade Caratini and add a more affordable backup, though that’s purely speculative.)

articles.title: David Bednar To Accept Qualifying Offer From Yankees
body: Closer David Bednar is expected to accept the $23.15MM qualifying offer from the Yankees, as first reported by Tyler Kepner of The Athletic.

It’s an unexpected development for Bednar, who was set to be one of the top available relievers on the market. He’ll skip the chance at a multi-year deal and return to New York. The Yankees have now retained their closer and one of their top lefties from last season after agreeing to a one-year deal with Tim Hill on Sunday.

Bednar wasn’t the only player to accept the QO. Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers also accepted it. The other six players to receive the offer declined it. One of them, Jake Bauers, already signed with a new team (Red Sox).

By agreeing to the $23.15MM contract, Bednar becomes the highest-paid reliever ever in terms of annual value. Dodgers closer Edwin Diaz set the mark last season with his three-year, $69MM contract ($23MM AAV). It’s a small edge for Bednar, but a record nonetheless.

Bednar delivered a strong campaign on the verge of free agency. He posted a 2.47 ERA across a career-high 69 1/3 innings. The righty saved 35 games as the top ninth-inning option in one of the best bullpens in the league. Bednar saw his elite strikeout rate fall to an above-average level (27.1%), but he also pushed his walk rate down to 7.1%.

The Yankees initially acquired Bednar at the 2025 trade deadline. He’d had an uneven season with the Pirates that included a brief demotion to the minors. Bednar was excellent down the stretch to close the year, emerging as the clear closer in a bullpen that also included Devin Williams and Camilo Doval.

articles.title: Phillies Select Bryan Rincon
body: The Phillies have selected shortstop prospect Bryan Rincon onto their 40-man roster, according to Francys Romero of BeisbolFR. The move protects Rincon from being taken in this year’s Rule 5 draft. Philadelphia’s 40-man roster now stands at 39 players, leaving one more spot to protect a prospect in advance of today’s 5:00 pm CT deadline.

Rincon is a Top 100 prospect in the sport and No. 4 in the Phillies’ system in the view of MLB Pipeline. The club took him in the late rounds of the 2022 draft, and he’s since worked his way through the lower levels of their farm system. This year was the switch-hitting Rincon’s first exposure to Double-A. In 534 plate appearances there, he announced himself with a.267/.410/.517 batting line and a 140 wRC+. Rincon put his plate discipline and speed on full display, walking at a 17.8% clip and stealing 30 bases. He also broke out as a power threat with 26 home runs, despite having combined to hit just 18 in the prior four seasons.

articles.title: Braves Claim Cameron Foster
body: The Braves announced Tuesday that they’ve claimed righty Cameron Foster off waivers from the Orioles. Atlanta also selected right-hander Cedric De Grandpre and Davis Polo to the 40-man roster. Both are now protected from the Rule 5 Draft, if it happens. The 2021 Rule 5 Draft was canceled amid that winter’s 99-day lockout, and another lockout once the current collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59pm ET on Dec. 1 is all but a foregone conclusion. Atlanta’s 40-man roster is now full.

It was reported earlier today that Foster was outrighted off Baltimore’s roster but it appears he hadn’t cleared waivers yet. Atlanta has swooped in to grab him. Foster made his major league debut with the Orioles this year, allowing nine earned runs in nine innings. He also posted a 9.53 earned run average in the minors. Those are obviously not impressive numbers but they were posted in small samples as Foster spent a decent chunk of time on the minor league injured list this year.

Atlanta is presumably focused more on Foster’s 2025 numbers, when he logged 46 1/3 innings on the farm with a 3.11 ERA, 32.6% strikeout rate and 8.4% walk rate. That prompted Baltimore to give him a 40-man spot at this time last year, to keep him out of the Rule 5 draft. His struggles in 2026 bumped him to the waiver wire but Atlanta will give him a roster spot, at least for now. If he still has a spot when the next season begins, he is still optionable.

articles.title: Tigers Sign Emilio Pagán
body: November 17: The Tigers have officially announced the Pagán signing. They also included the details of the bonus clause. Pagán can earn an extra $200K for finishing 35 games, with additional thresholds going up by five (40, 45, 50, 55). In total, it’s another $1MM in incentives.
November 11: Pagán’s deal is for $11.5MM plus a bonus clause, reports Gordon Wittenmyer of the Cincinnati Enquirer.

November 10: The Tigers are in agreement with free agent reliever Emilio Pagán, reports Jon Heyman of The New York Post. It’s reportedly a one-year deal in the $11MM range for the Ballengee Group client. Detroit has a full 40-man roster and will need to make a corresponding move once the signing is official.

It’s this year’s first significant move on the free agent market. Pagán’s market moved quickly, as he finds a new landing spot within two weeks of declining a $10MM player option with Cincinnati. Pagán banks an extra million dollars and presumably will enter the season as A.J. Hinch’s primary closer.

The agreement comes together within hours of Detroit president of baseball operations Scott Harris telling reporters he was seeking a right-handed leverage reliever who could improve the team’s strikeout ability (links via Cody Stavenhagen of The Athletic and Jason Beck of MLB.com). Pagán fanned 25.9% of opponents this year and has a 28% strikeout rate for his career, which will make him one of the team’s better swing-and-miss arms.

articles.title: Tigers Agree To Minor League Deals With Sawyer Gipson-Long, Bailey Horn
body: The Tigers released right-hander Sawyer Gipson-Long and lefty Bailey Horn two weeks ago, but they are now returning to the organization. Gipson-Long and Horn have agreed to minor league contracts with Detroit, Evan Woodbery of MLive.com reports.

The Twins drafted Gipson-Long in the sixth round in 2019, but they sent him to the AL Central rival Tigers for righty Michael Fulmer in August 2022. Gipson-Long made his major league debut a year later and pitched to a sterling 2.70 ERA with 26 strikeouts over a four-appearance, 20-inning stretch. However, elbow issues prevented him from building on that performance in 2024. Gipson-Long wound up missing the entire season after undergoing an internal brace procedure.

The 6-foot-4, 225-pound Gipson-Long returned to the majors in 2025 to throw 31 1/3 innings, though he could only muster a 7.18 ERA. That counts as Gipson-Long’s most recent action at the game’s highest level, as he didn’t make an appearance with Detroit this year. Gipson-Long made 26 starts and threw 108 innings with the Mud Hens, but he walked over 10% of hitters and gave up home runs on 16.7% of fly balls, leading to a bloated 5.58 ERA.

articles.title: Red Sox Sign Jake Bauers
body: Today: The Red Sox made things official with Bauers today, formally announcing his four-year deal. In a corresponding move, they traded left-hander Raymond Burgos to the Athletics.

November 13: The Red Sox and first baseman Jake Bauers are in agreement on a four-year, $58MM contract, reports ESPN’s Jeff Passan. The VC Sports Group client received a $23.15MM qualifying offer from the Brewers but will turn that down and head to Boston on a lucrative multi-year contract.

Due in no small part to his postseason heroics, Bauers’ story is well known by now. The 31-year-old former top prospect was on the cusp of retirement after seemingly flaming out in the majors. He’d called his agent and informed him of the decision but changed course just days later when his wife learned she was pregnant with their second child and wouldn’t be going back to work — and securing health insurance — as they’d planned. Bauers signed back with the Brewers on a minor league deal ahead of the 2025 season and made the club. Bauers struggled for much of the season and looked like a DFA or non-tender candidate until a massive September saved his roster spot.

articles.title: White Sox Designate Joey Bart, Add Two To 40-Man Roster
body: 2:22pm: The Sox have now formally announced Bart’s DFA. Chicago also announced that infielder William Bergolla Jr. and lefty Jaden Woods have had their contracts selected. Both are now on the 40-man roster and protected from the Rule 5 Draft (if it happens).

1:51pm: The White Sox will designate catcher Joey Bart for assignment, reports Robert Murray of FanSided. The former No. 2 overall draft pick was eligible for arbitration one final time this winter and was projected by MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz to earn $2.9MM in 2027.

Bart, 30 next month, came to the White Sox from Atlanta in a deadline deal. The Braves received righty Duncan Davitt, who’d been designated for assignment himself, in that swap. Bart suffered a fractured left hand just days after joining the South Siders, when he was plunked by a 98 mph heater from Erik Miller, his former Triple-A teammate with the Giants organization. Bart played in only three games and went hitless in nine trips to the plate. That brief stint brought his season line to.214/.305/.357 in 128 plate appearances between Pittsburgh, Atlanta and Chicago.

Draft pedigree notwithstanding, Bart doesn’t bring much to the table offensively. He had a nice run with the Pirates from 2024-25, hitting.257/.347/.398 with 17 homers in a combined 614 plate appearances, but those are the only two occasions in seven seasons where he’s produced even average offense. On the whole, Bart is a lifetime.237/.319/.368 hitter.

articles.title: Yankees Claim Chase Hampton
body: The Yankees announced this afternoon that they have claimed right-hander Chase Hampton off waivers from the Orioles. Hampton returns to his original organization after riding the waiver wire with the Nationals, Cardinals, and Orioles since mid-September. With this move, the Yankees’ 40-man roster stands at 34 players, leaving six spots with which to protect Rule 5 eligible players before today’s 5:00 pm CT deadline.

The 25-year-old Hampton was the Yankees’ sixth-round draft pick in 2022 and a Top 100 prospect on MLB Pipeline just two years ago. He missed the entire 2025 season due to Tommy John surgery but was selected onto the 40-man roster for the first time after the season. Optioned to the minors, he made 17 starts across three levels and struggled mightily, delivering an earned run average over 8.00 while walking opponents at a 12.9% clip and allowing more than two home runs per nine innings.

When Aaron Judge returned from the 60-day IL in August, New York designated Hampton for assignment to clear the necessary 40-man roster space. The Nationals claimed, then optioned Hampton on September 12, though he only stuck around for two weeks and did not get into game action for Double-A Harrisburg. The Cardinals claimed Hampton on September 26, followed by the Orioles on November 2. In the end, the waiver carousel brings Hampton back home to New York.

articles.title: Rangers Claim Josh White
body: The Rangers have claimed Josh White off waivers from the Orioles, per a team announcement. Texas now has 38 players on its 40-man roster.

It’s the second waiver claim this month for White. He landed in Baltimore after getting squeezed out in Miami when 40-man rosters were trimmed in early November. White was a fifth-round pick by the Marlins in 2022. He debuted with the club this season, allowing five earned runs in his lone appearance.

White’s brutal debut obscured what was generally a solid campaign. He tossed 56 frames with a 2.41 ERA and a 27% strikeout rate at Triple-A. The righty certainly ran hot with a.233 BABIP, but he was probably a bit unlucky with a near-15% homer-per-nine rate. White’s 13.5% walk rate is a cause for concern, though he showed better control the previous two seasons.

The 25-year-old White has a relatively deep arsenal for a reliever. He flashed a four-pitch mix this season with Jacksonville. White led with a four-seamer around 94 mph, followed by a mid-80s slider that he threw nearly as often as the heater. He also threw a curveball 27.3% of the time. A splitter rounded out the repertoire.

articles.title: Red Sox Trade Angel Bastardo To Royals
body: 1:47pm: The Royals have confirmed the trade and announced that Bastardo has indeed been selected to the 40-man roster.

1:01pm: The Red Sox and Royals have lined up on a minor trade. Right-hander Angel Bastardo is heading to Kansas City, reports Francys Romero of BeisbolFR. Boston gets minor league infielder Jack Pineda in return, according to Alex Speier of the Boston Globe. The Royals may add Bastardo to their 40-man roster, according to Chris Cotillo of MassLive.

The 24-year-old Bastardo was selected by the Blue Jays in the 2024 Rule 5 Draft. He’d been working his way through the Red Sox’ system since signing as an amateur out of Venezuela in 2018. He reached Double-A in 2023 and repeated there in 2024, posting an earned run average over 5.00 in ten starts before undergoing Tommy John surgery that June. After the Rule 5 selection, Toronto stashed Bastardo on the 60-day IL while he continued his recovery. He was returned to Boston this past April after he didn’t make the Blue Jays’ roster out of camp.

In 2026, Bastardo worked as a full-time reliever for the Sox’ Triple-A affiliate in Worcester, posting a 4.64 ERA over 54 1/3 innings. His 31.6% strikeout rate was impressive, but both his 36.6% ground ball rate and especially his 14.3% walk rate were worse than par. Boston re-signed Bastardo to a minors pact a few weeks ago, though he’ll now work towards his major league debut with the Royals.

articles.title: A’s Designate Braden Nett For Assignment
body: The Athletics finalized their acquisition of left-hander Raymond Burgos from the Red Sox this afternoon. In a corresponding 40-man roster move, the team designated right-hander Braden Nett for assignment.

Nett, 24, signed with the Padres as an undrafted free agent in 2022. Yet, he quickly showed promising stuff, and by 2025, both Baseball America and FanGraphs had him ranked among the top 10 prospects in the organization. That summer, he was one of four players the Padres sent to the A’s in the Mason Miller trade. While Leo De Vries was the centerpiece of the deal, Nett was more than a throw-in. Indeed, The Athletic’s Ken Rosenthal had reported earlier that summer that Nett was generating interest on the trade market.

At this time last year, the A’s selected Nett to their 40-man roster to protect him from the Rule 5 draft. Although he had not yet pitched above Double-A, it seemed like he had a realistic chance to make his big league debut at some point in 2026. Unfortunately, injuries plagued the righty throughout the season. He only threw 22 innings at Triple-A and another 14 2/3 at Double-A. While he struck out an impressive 45 batters in those 36 2/3 frames, he walked an unsightly 47 and gave up 36 runs on 41 hits. Those strikeouts suggest he still has promise, but the walks were obviously a huge red flag. From the outside, it’s hard to know whether Nett’s control issues were injury-related or simply a matter of facing Triple-A competition for the first time. Regardless, the A’s decided that he isn’t close enough to MLB-ready to warrant a 40-man roster spot.

articles.title: Nationals Announce Series Of Moves
body: As part of a slew of roster moves on Tuesday, the Nationals selected the contracts of right-handers Jarlin Susana, Travis Sykora and Alejandro Rosario. They also claimed left-hander Philip Abner off waivers from the Orioles and designated four pitchers – righties Josiah Gray, Braxton Roxby and Gus Varland and lefty Carson Palmquist – for assignment.

The Nationals had been expected to add Susana, Sykora and Rosario to their 40-man roster ahead of the 6 p.m. ET Rule 5 protection deadline on Tuesday. There may not be a Rule 5 draft this winter because of the impending lockout, but in case there is, they weren’t going to risk losing any of them. Susana and Sykora are among the Nationals’ premier prospects and two of the top 100 farmhands in baseball. Rosario isn’t on that level, but he still ranks as the Nats’ 19th-best prospect at MLB.com.

This is the second time a team has grabbed Abner off waivers this month. He went from the Mets to the Orioles on Nov. 2, but he’ll now remain in the Beltway with the Nationals. Since debuting in 2025, the soft-tossing 24-year-old has combined for 22 2/3 innings of 6.75 ERA ball between the Diamondbacks and Giants. Abner struck out 15 hitters, walked 14 and yielded six home runs during that span, which explains the inflated ERA. However, he does carry a more encouraging 3.72 ERA over 46 Triple-A frames. Abner also has two minor league options left, meaning the Nationals can send him down without having to designate him for assignment.

articles.title: Angels Select Nelson Rada, Raudi Rodriguez
body: The Angels announced Tuesday that they’ve selected the contracts of outfield prospects Nelson Rada and Raudi Rodriguez. Both are now on the 40-man roster and protected from the Rule 5 Draft — if it happens. (The 2021 Rule 5 Draft was canceled as part of that offseason’s league-implemented lockout.)

Neither selection comes as a major surprise. Rada, in particular, has ranked among the Halos’ top prospects since signing out of Venezuela as an amateur back in Jan. 2022. He’s a plus-running center fielder who’s light on power but makes lots of contact and draws plenty of walks. He reached Triple-A as a 19-year-old late in the 2025 season and spent the entire year there in 2026, batting.278/.376/.363 with three homers, 22 doubles, five triples, 43 steals (in 52 tries), a 12.3% walk rate and an 18.6% strikeout rate.

The 23-year-old Rodriguez has proven to be a nice find in the 19th round of the 2023 draft. He split the 2026 season between Double-A and Triple-A, slashing a combined.264/.374/.410 with 16 homers, 15 doubles, five triples and 36 steals (46 attempts). Rodriguez walked at a 14.3% clip at both levels and fanned in 21.3% of his overall plate appearances (with a slightly lower rate in Triple-A than in Double-A). He has more power than Rada and is an above-average runner. He doesn’t have quite the same speed or defensive chops as Rada but is experienced in all three outfield slots, with Baseball America’s latest scouting report calling him a late-bloomer with fourth-outfielder potential.

articles.title: Rangers Receiving Trade Interest In MacKenzie Gore
body: According to The Athletic’s Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon, multiple teams have expressed interest in trading for Rangers starting pitcher MacKenzie Gore. That’s not particularly surprising. MLBTR ranked him at No. 17 on our list of the Top 40 Trade Candidates of the offseason. The left-hander has been a durable mid-rotation starter for the last four years, pitching to a 4.26 ERA and 4.04 SIERA in 123 starts. He is entering his final year of arbitration eligibility, and MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz projects him to earn $8.7MM, significantly less than a similar pitcher would command in free agency.

Gore also drew trade interest ahead of this year’s deadline. Although the Rangers ultimately chose to keep him in August, they might be more motivated to sell over the winter.
