President of baseball operations Chris Young has already said he needs to “reshuffle” his cards and that he will be “open-minded to any way” he can improve his team’s roster. He probably also needs to shed some salary if he wants to make any meaningful additions. He recently said his club’s payroll next year will be “very similar” to what it was in 2026. Per the MLBTR Payroll Tracker, the Rangers ran an LRD payroll just under $193MM this past season, and currently, they’re projected for a $175MM tab in 2027. That’s not a lot of room to work with.

articles.title: Astros Place Joey Loperfido On Outright Waivers
body: The Astros have placed outfielder Joey Loperfido on outright waivers, according to The Athletic’s Chandler Rome. Loperfido underwent hip surgery last month and is not expected to be ready for Spring Training. This move will take him off the Astros’ 40-man roster, which now stands at 38 players. Loperfido has never been outrighted before, so if he goes unclaimed, he’d need to accept an outright assignment to Triple-A Sugar Land.

Loperfido has taken 487 trips to the plate from 2024-26. In that sample, he’s batted.240/.300/.378 with a 92 wRC+ and an alarming 31.6% strikeout rate. He’s fared well in left field, earning +8 Defensive Runs Saved and +2 Outs Above Average in over 700 innings there, but his grades in the other two outfield spots are middling.

This year was more of the same for Loperfido at the plate. While he walked at an 11.6% clip in 121 plate appearances, his 26.4% strikeout rate was still high, and his 82 wRC+ cast him as 18% worse than the league average hitter. That stands in contrast to last year’s 148 wRC+, though that similarly came in a small sample and was inflated by a monster.431 average on balls in play. Loperfido batted.289/.381/.392 with a 112 wRC+ for Sugar Land this year, showing decent on-base ability but nothing in the way of power.

articles.title: Red Sox Trade Raymond Burgos To Athletics
body: 12:23pm: Burgos is going to the Athletics for minor league right-hander Kenya Huggins, according to Alex Speier of the Boston Globe.

12:09pm: The Red Sox are nearing a trade that would send left-hander Raymond Burgos to an unidentified team, Chris Cotillo of MassLive.com reports. Shipping out Burgos would clear a roster spot for newly signed first baseman Jake Bauers.

Cleveland took Burgos in the 18th round of the 2018 draft, but he never pitched in the majors with the organization. Burgos debuted in the bigs as a member of the Giants in 2024, though he made just one appearance and tossed a single inning with them. After spending 2025 in the minors with the Giants, Burgos began this past season in the Mexican League. He fared well enough with Guerreros de Oaxaca to land on Boston’s radar. The Red Sox brought Burgos in on a minor league pact in May and wound up summoning him to the majors in early August.

articles.title: Mariners Sign Stephen Nogosek To Minor League Deal
body: The Mariners have brought in right-hander Stephen Nogosek on a minor league deal, according to Ari Alexander of 7News. Nogosek receives an invite to big league Spring Training.

It’s been a minute since Nogosek appeared in affiliated ball. He spent the 2025 season with the Royals’ Triple-A affiliate in Omaha. He had a 4.87 earned run average in 57 1/3 innings there, working mostly as a reliever with five short starts mixed in. Nogosek’s 23.9% strikeout rate and 42.4% ground ball rate were decent, but he also walked an even 10% of opposing batters. That wasn’t enough for the Royals to add him to their 40-man roster. Nogosek elected minor league free agency in November 2025, then spent this past year in the Mexican League.

Nogosek’s big league resume is pretty light. He threw a total of 57 1/3 innings with the Mets from 2019-23, the bulk of those coming from 2022-23. In that two-year stretch, Nogosek had a 4.15 ERA over 47 2/3 frames with a 21.6% strikeout rate, 9.9% walk rate, and 45.5% fly ball rate (league average is typically under 40%). The long ball was a particular struggle. Nogosek allowed ten homers combined between those two seasons, which amounted to 1.89 homers per nine innings.

With that middling track record, this is purely a depth signing for the Mariners. The team is coming off an underwhelming 76-86 record, which led to Dan Wilson’s exit and the subsequent hiring of Jason Kanzler as the new manager. As stated by president of baseball operations Jerry Dipoto, the Mariners’ offseason agenda includes adding to the bullpen and at least one bat.

articles.title: Adrián Morejón Declines Qualifying Offer From Padres
body: Left-hander Adrián Morejón has declined the qualifying offer from the Padres, reports Mark Feinsand of MLB.com. He is now officially a free agent and stands as the top reliever on the market.

Morejón and Yankees’ closer David Bednar were the two relievers among the eight players who received the QO. It’s rare that teams issue the QO to relievers, even those of Morejón’s caliber, but his rejection of the offer isn’t exactly surprising. MLBTR ranked him at No. 8 on our list of the Top 50 Free Agents, projecting him for a five-year, $80MM contract. Morejón has already been publicly linked to the Yankees and Marlins, and he will clearly have no shortage of suitors beyond those two.

San Diego will surely be interested in having Morejón back, though he could ultimately price himself out of their budget. The Padres will focus more on rebuilding their rotation from scratch, as four of the five members of their Opening Day rotation, headlined by Michael King, are now free agents. The lone exception is right-hander Randy Vasquez.

articles.title: Orioles Outright Cameron Foster, Release Rece Hinds
body: The Orioles have outrighted right-hander Cameron Foster, reports Andy Kostka of The Baltimore Banner. The team also announced that they’ve released outfielder Rece Hinds so he can pursue an opportunity overseas in the Korea Baseball Organization. Those two moves clear a couple of 40-man roster spots in advance of the Rule 5 protection deadline today at 5:00 pm CT. Baltimore’s 40-man roster now stands at 35 players.

Foster, 27, was selected onto the 40-man roster for the first time last November. He made his big league debut in mid-April and made a total of six relief appearances for the O’s over the next month. Two of those appearances were scoreless, but Foster fared poorly in the other four, ultimately allowing nine earned runs in as many innings with eight walks. The righty was optioned and recalled from Triple-A Norfolk three times after his April debut. In late May, shoulder discomfort forced him to the minor league injured list, where he spent the rest of the season, only briefly returning to the mound for a few rehab outings with High-A Frederick in July.

articles.title: Phillies Receiving Trade Interest In Orion Kerkering
body: The Phillies are receiving trade interest in righty reliever Orion Kerkering, per Matt Gelb of The Athletic. Multiple teams have reportedly expressed interest in Kerkering, who’s coming off a rough season that saw him demoted to Triple-A in late September. It’s unclear how far those talks have progressed, though it’s likely teams are just engaging in due diligence on a buy-low candidate.

Kerkering, 25, debuted in 2023 and put together a solid run from 2024-25. In 2024, he held opponents to a 2.29 earned run average over 63 innings. The peripheral stats were equally impressive, as Kerkering had an above-average 28.8% strikeout rate, 6.6% walk rate, and induced ground balls 53.5% of the time. His 2025 numbers weren’t quite as sharp, but they were still valuable. In 60 innings, he had a 3.30 ERA and 24.4% strikeout rate.

Notably, Kerkering wasn’t as stingy with the free passes in 2025, as his walk rate jumped to 10.2%, which graded out worse than average. He also saw an 11.5% drop in ground ball rate (to a roughly average 42.0%) along with a 13.3% spike in fly balls allowed. Unfortunately, those trends continued in his third full season out of the Phillies’ bullpen.

articles.title: Red Sox Discussing Several Pitchers In Trade Talks
body: The Red Sox have a relatively crowded 40-man roster and several rotation candidates on the mend from injury. Between today’s deadline to protect eligible prospects from the Rule 5 Draft and Friday’s deadline to tender contracts to arbitration-eligible players, there are multiple deadlines this week that could spur some trade action surrounding players on the 40-man bubble — both in Boston and around the league.

With that context in mind, WEEI’s Rob Bradford reports that the Sox are exploring trade interest for right-handers Tanner Houck, Kutter Crawford and Johan Oviedo. None of the three was a prominent factor in last year’s rotation due to injury, but all three have had some big league success. It’s possible that any of the trio could be non-tendered come Friday, but they’re all plenty affordable for teams seeking rotation depth.
[Related: 2026 Non-Tender Candidates]

Houck, 30, pitched only three major league innings last year following Aug. 2025 Tommy John surgery. His 2025 season was a nightmare. The former top prospect logged only 43 2/3 major league innings and posted an 8.04 ERA while trying to pitch through elbow troubles. A season prior, however, Houck tossed 178 2/3 innings with a 3.12 ERA, 20.7% strikeout rate, 6.5% walk rate and massive 55.9% ground-ball rate.

articles.title: Red Sox, Michael Arias Agree To Minor League Deal
body: The Red Sox are in agreement with reliever Michael Arias on a minor league contract, reports Andrew Parker of Sox Prospects. The righty will be in camp as a non-roster invitee.

Arias spent the 2026 season in Double-A with the Yankees. He pitched to a 5.20 earned run average across 53 2/3 innings, striking out 24% of opponents against a 10% walk rate. Arias reached Triple-A as a member of the Cubs’ organization back in 2024, but he split his two seasons in the New York farm system between High-A and Double-A.

That included a pair of seasons on 40-man rosters. The Cubs selected his contract after the 2023 campaign to keep him out of the Rule 5 draft. They designated him for assignment the following offseason and sold his contract to New York. The Yankees kept him on their 40-man roster for all of last year, non-tendering him at season’s end. They immediately brought him back on a minor league deal but never moved him above Double-A given his pedestrian performance.

Arias receives a non-roster invite but is a long shot to break camp. He’ll hope for a season-opening assignment to Triple-A Worcester with a chance to make his MLB debut at some point midseason. A converted shortstop, Arias has only been pitching since 2021. He garnered some prospect attention based on his raw stuff but has struggled to throw enough strikes over his minor league career. This year’s walk rate was still a little high but his lowest full-season mark, and he’s only issued three free passes across 10 2/3 innings in the Dominican Winter League so far.

articles.title: Yankees Have Shown Interest In Randy Arozarena
body: The Yankees expressed some amount of interest in Randy Arozarena at last week’s GM Meetings, reports Jon Heyman of The New York Post. Although it’d be an odd roster fit, Heyman notes that the Yanks are in the mix for a right-handed bat.

Arozarena is attached to a qualifying offer. Francys Romero reported this evening that the three-time All-Star has officially declined the QO from Seattle in advance of tomorrow afternoon’s deadline, which was inevitable. He’ll cost a signing team draft and/or international bonus pool capital. The Yankees are luxury tax payors and would forfeit their second and fifth-highest picks in the 2027 draft, plus $1MM from their international pool to sign another team’s qualified free agent. They’d recoup a pick after the fourth round if David Bednar signs elsewhere.

The Yankees are most focused on the bullpen, where both Bednar and Paul Blackburn hit the market. Their big position player need is on the infield, ideally at third base to push Ryan McMahon off the roster. New York is also looking for a right-handed hitting catcher who can split time with Austin Wells.

Outfield seems a secondary issue. They’re losing Trent Grisham to free agency but have the game’s best corner outfield tandem in Aaron Judge and Cody Bellinger. New York can use Bellinger on a semi-regular basis in center field but probably doesn’t want him playing there every day. Spencer Jones had an encouraging enough rookie season and projects as the primary center fielder, though he’s ideally better suited to a corner.

articles.title: Ken Sanders Passes Away
body: The Brewers announced today that former big leaguer Ken Sanders has passed away. He was 85 years old.

Sanders was born in St. Louis in 1941. He played high school and college ball before signing with the Kansas City Athletics. He got some sporadic playing time in the 1960s, appearing for the A’s and Red Sox.

He was traded to the Brewers prior to the 1970 season, their first season in Milwaukee. The team had started as the Seattle Pilots, an expansion club in 1969. But after just one season, they moved to Milwaukee and became the Brewers.

Sanders had his best seasons in Milwaukee and was one of the better performers during a fairly bleak era for the franchise. The Brewers were well below.500 for their first nine campaigns but Sanders was a bright spot in the early parts of that span. In 1970, he logged 92 1/3 innings out of the Milwaukee bullpen with a 1.75 earned run average. He took over the closer’s role along the way, racking up 13 saves.

The following season was even better for Sanders. He tossed 136 1/3 innings with his ERA bumping up ever so slightly to 1.91. He finished the year with 31 saves, which was enough for the major league lead. That would prove to be his peak. His performance declined a bit in 1972 and he relinquished the closer role. He finished the season with 17 saves and a 3.12 ERA in 92 1/3 innings.

articles.title: Pirates, Chas McCormick Agree To Minor League Deal
body: The Pirates and outfielder Chas McCormick have agreed to a minor league deal, reports Ari Alexander of 7News Boston. McCormick will also receive an invite to big league camp in spring training.

McCormick, 32 in April, has some good major league seasons under his belt but it’s been a few years. From 2021 to 2023, he got into 342 games for the Astros and stepped to the plate 1,184 times. His 27.6% strikeout rate was on the high side but he had a solid 9.4% walk rate and 50 home runs. His combined batting line of.259/.336/.449 led to a 120 wRC+. He also stole 27 bases and got good grades at all three outfield slots. FanGraphs credited him with 7.7 wins above replacement for that span.

He bounced on and off the injured list in 2024 and 2025. He only got into 160 games over those two seasons and had greatly diminished production, hitting just.211/.273/.301. Houston bumped him from the roster around this time a year ago. He became a free agent and signed a minor league deal with the Cubs.

He spent all of the 2026 season with Triple-A Iowa, stepping to the plate 414 times across 102 games. He stole 17 bases, hit 14 home runs, walked at a 12.3% pace and only struck out 20% of the time. Even in the hitter-friendly context of the International League this year, his.285/.383/.468 line was still 19% better than average by measure of wRC+. Despite those strong numbers, the Cubs never called him up. They had Pete Crow-Armstrong, Seiya Suzuki and Ian Happ in the outfield most days and then added Tyrone Taylor at the deadline.

articles.title: Cubs Interested In Trevor Rogers
body: The Cubs are showing interest in free agent left-hander Trevor Rogers, reports Sahadev Sharma of The Athletic. Sharma adds that the club needs multiple arms and is touching base with almost every starter.

Rogers, 29, isn’t a household name but has somewhat quietly been one of the better starters in baseball lately. Dating back to the start of the 2025 season, he has made 48 starts and thrown 279 1/3 innings with a 3.16 earned run average. His 23.2% strikeout rate and 6.1% walk rate in that time were both better than average while his 41.1% ground ball rate was just shy of par. FanGraphs credited him with 7.3 wins above replacement over those two years. Only 16 pitchers were ahead of him in that regard.

The Orioles extended Rogers a $23.15MM qualifying offer at season’s end. MLBTR predicted that he could decline that offer and still secure a five-year deal worth $115MM. Rogers’ numbers leading up to free agency line up fairly well with Ranger Suarez, as Suarez had a 3.33 ERA, 23.2% strikeout rate, 6.2% walk rate and 49.3% ground ball rate in his two seasons prior to free agency. He then landed a five-year, $130MM deal with the Red Sox. We put our Rogers prediction a bit under Suarez because Ranger had the longer track record of success.

As Sharma mentioned, the Cubs need to be in touch with just about every available starter. Matthew Boyd, Kevin Gausman, Clay Holmes, David Peterson, Shota Imanaga and Colin Rea all became free agents a few weeks ago.

articles.title: A’s To Re-Sign Ben Bowden On Minor League Deal
body: The Athletics are bringing left-handed reliever Ben Bowden back on a minor league deal, per their transaction log at MLB.com. The team didn’t formally announce the signing.

Bowden was with the A’s organization in 2025-26, though he only pitched one big league inning this past season — during which he yielded four runs. It’s obviously not how he wanted his lone big league appearance of the year to go, but Bowden posted decent numbers in an exorbitantly hitter-friendly Triple-A setting this year. Through 51 1/3 innings of relief, he yielded a 4.56 ERA with a big 29.2% strikeout rate against a 9.3% walk rate. A year prior, he notched a sparkling 1.36 ERA in 39 2/3 Triple-A frames.

That 4.56 ERA this year doesn’t look like much, but it actually ranked 30th among the 89 pitchers who tossed at least 50 innings in the Pacific Coast League and its supercharged run-scoring environment. Add in his terrific 2025 results, and Bowden has been one of the PCL’s more effective relievers over the past two seasons.

The 32-year-old Bowden has only pitched in parts of three seasons — two quick cups of coffee with the A’s while playing home games at hitter-friendly Sutter Health Park and a lengthier, 35 2/3-inning stint with the 2021 Rockies. He’s been hit hard at each stop, combining for 47 2/3 innings with a 6.65 ERA in the big leagues. Bowden has a respectable 21.1% strikeout rate but has walked more than 12% of his major league opponents and surrendered an average of 1.52 homers per nine major league innings. He carries a 4.17 ERA and 29.8% strikeout rate in parts of seven Triple-A seasons.

articles.title: Orioles Reportedly Showing Interest In Kris Bubic, Matthew Boyd
body: The Orioles are looking for starting pitching and Andy Kostka of The Baltimore Banner reports that they are leaning towards the lefty market. That includes old friend Trevor Rogers but the O’s have also been involved with free agents Kris Bubic and Matthew Boyd. Kostka mentions David Peterson as another lefty who could make sense, without specifying that the Orioles have shown interest in him.

With Rogers reaching free agency, the Baltimore rotation leans right-handed. Kyle Bradish, Shane Baz and Brandon Young currently project as the top three options and those three are all righties. Cade Povich and Luis De León are lefties in the mix for jobs but they aren’t really locks to have spots. Povich has a 5.07 earned run average in his big league career so far. He had a 6.28 ERA in Triple-A this year. He still has an option and could be pushed down to Norfolk again next year. De León had a nice big league debut but he has fewer than 10 innings under his belt.

Ideally, the O’s would get some more established options so that Povich and De León aren’t being relied upon right out of the gate. Bringing back Rogers would be one way to do that but he will be costly since he is one of the top lefty starters on the market. MLBTR predicted Rogers for a five-year, $115MM deal. Since the O’s made Rogers a qualifying offer, they would recoup draft pick compensation if he signs elsewhere. They could then look to more affordable options to try to replace him.

articles.title: Rockies Notes: Goodman, Pitching Needs
body: Rockies catcher Hunter Goodman would be among the top hitters available this winter if the club were interested in fielding offers. There was buzz around Goodman at this year’s trade deadline, but Colorado didn’t seem overly inclined to move him. Jon Morosi of MLB Network noted that other teams expect the Rockies to be more willing to entertain a trade this winter.

The 27-year-old Goodman is under team control through 2029. We project him to make $6.2MM in his first trip through arbitration. The reasonable cost and years of control would likely make the asking price for Goodman quite high. He’s the centerpiece of the offense and president of baseball operations Paul DePodesta didn’t sound eager to part with him or any other member of the lineup at the GM Meetings last week.

“Some of the position players we have, I think it will be much harder for us to trade because we feel like that’s a strength,” DePodesta told reporters, including Kevin Henry of the Denver Gazette. “So we want to be careful about not taking too much away from that. But I think we have to be open-minded.”

Goodman followed up a breakout 2025 with another strong season this past year. He launched 41 home runs and slugged.529, both top-four marks in the National League. Goodman didn’t just feast at hitter-friendly Coors Field, either. He actually had a.882 OPS on the road and a sub-.800 OPS at home. He hit 25 of his home runs away from Coors.

articles.title: Orioles Among Teams Interested In Randy Arozarena
body: The Orioles are in the market for multiple arms this winter, but Andy Kostka of the Baltimore Banner reports that they’re also active in the outfield market. Specifically, he notes that Randy Arozarena is of interest. The O’s also have interest in re-signing Luis Robert Jr., per the report. That’s not all that surprising, given that Baltimore claimed him off waivers in August despite about $5MM in guaranteed money still being left on his contract. Robert suffered an injury and barely played with the O’s, who declined his $20MM club option, but bringing him back at a lesser rate wouldn’t be terribly surprising.

Arozarena is obviously the more prominent of the two in terms of free agent stature. Whereas Robert could in all likelihood be had on a one-year pact, Arozarena should command a four-year deal — perhaps even with a chance at climbing to five years. (MLBTR predicted a four-year, $100MM deal on our annual Top 50 Free Agent rankings.)

articles.title: Jordan Lawlar Underwent UCL Surgery
body: Diamondbacks outfielder Jordan Lawlar had UCL surgery this offseason, reports Steve Gilbert of MLB.com. There had been no previous indication that Lawlar was dealing with an elbow injury. He’s expected to be ready for the start of the 2027 season.

Lawlar has long been one of the top hitting prospects in Arizona’s system, but he’s been routinely hampered by injuries. He broke camp with the club this year but fractured his wrist a week into the season. Lawlar returned after a two-month absence, then went back on the IL a week later with a hamstring strain.

The Diamondbacks reinstated Lawlar in mid-August and he seemed to close the season healthy. He picked up semi-regular work in center field as the club pushed for a Wild Card spot. Arizona ultimately came up just short in chasing down Philadelphia. Lawlar delivered a.781 OPS in September, but was apparently playing through an elbow injury.

“He had some lingering issues with the elbow that he told us about during the year that didn’t really affect him playing or missing any time,” general manager Mike Hazen told Gilbert. “But after the down period at the end of the season when he started up, he kind of still felt it and didn’t really want to go into next season with that still nagging him.”

Gilbert referred to the procedure as “Tommy John brace surgery,” which would suggest it wasn’t a full reconstruction. That helps trim the recovery timeline. Position players typically come back sooner than pitchers anyway.

articles.title: Mets Acquire International Bonus Money From Rangers
body: 10:58 am: Francys Romero of BeisbolFR.com reports that the Mets received $250K in bonus pool money.

10:48 am: The Mets are sending right-hander Juan Arnaud to the Rangers for international bonus pool space, per multiple reports, including from Shawn McFarland of the Dallas Morning News. Arnaud was assigned to High-A Hub City.

There’s about a month remaining in the period to sign international prospects. The window closes on December 15. The Mets had $5.44MM to spend this period, tied for the lowest figure in the league, per AP News. Bonus pool money can be traded in increments of $250K.

Arnaud was signed as an international free agent out of the Dominican Republic in 2021. He’s pitched in five seasons at the lower levels of the minor leagues. Arnaud reached High-A at the end of the 2025 campaign. He repeated the level this season. The 23-year-old compiled a 2.79 ERA over 51 2/3 innings with Brooklyn. He had a strong 30.6% strikeout rate but an unsightly 16.1% walk rate.

Since he’s spent five seasons in the minors, Arnaud is eligible for the Rule 5 draft. Teams have until 5 pm CT on Tuesday to protect players by adding them to the 40-man roster. The Rule 5 draft is scheduled for December 9.

articles.title: Phillies To Sign Geoff Hartlieb To Minors Deal
body: Right-hander Geoff Hartlieb is heading to the Phillies on a minor league deal, per his transaction tracker on MLB.com. The reliever cleared waivers and was sent outright to Triple-A by the Athletics in late October. He elected free agency in early November.

Hartlieb was up and down with the A’s several times last season. He totaled 28 innings across 18 appearances in various stints with the big-league club. The A’s leaned on him to eat innings whenever the bullpen needed a fresh arm. Hartlieb posted a 4.82 ERA with underwhelming strikeout (17.7%) and walk (11.3%) rates.

The 33-year-old Hartlieb has pitched for seven teams in his seven-year MLB career. He’s bounced around frequently since his 2019 debut with the Pirates. Hartlieb hasn’t spent more than a year with one organization after leaving Pittsburgh midway through the 2021 campaign.

Hartlieb made some arsenal adjustments during his time with the A’s. He led with his slider, as he did in a small sample with the Yankees and Tigers in 2025, but threw his four-seamer at a similar clip. Hartlieb also brought back the cutter, which he hadn’t thrown much outside of his time with the Rockies in 2024. Along with the sinker, Hartlieb threw four pitches at least 16% of the time. The slider had a massive 44.2% whiff rate and held hitters to a.167 batting average. The other three pitches were hit hard.

The Phillies bullpen will lose free agent Jose Alvarado, but the rest of the group is expected back in 2027. Hartlieb will be battling guys like Alan Rangel, Max Lazar, and the recently signed Max Kranick for long relief opportunities.

articles.title: Orioles Re-Sign José Barrero To Minor League Deal
body: The Orioles announced that they have agreed to terms on a minor league deal with infielder José Barrero. Presumably, Barrero will receive an invite to big league camp in spring training, though the club announcement didn’t specify that.

Barrero, 29 in April, has been with the O’s for a while now. Baltimore first signed him to a minor league deal in July of 2025. He didn’t get a roster spot in Baltimore that year but the O’s re-signed him to another minor league deal for 2026. He was called up in September and got into a couple of games down to the stretch. He was bumped from the roster at season’s end and became a free agent but is now back with the O’s in a non-roster capacity once again.

The infielder hasn’t done much at the big league level. In 163 games spread across six different seasons with the Reds, Cardinals and Orioles, he has a batting line of.182/.238/.256. His 6% walk rate and 36.2% strikeout rate are both poor figures.

For the Orioles, there’s no harm in having him around as a depth piece. Barrero has experience at the middle infield spots, third base and the outfield, so he gives them cover at a lot of places. He also has a bit of theoretical upside because he was also a Top 100 prospect a few years ago. He hasn’t delivered on that hype. As mentioned, his big league work hasn’t been great. He has also struggled at the Triple-A level, with a.218/.301/.419 slash line and 31.2% strikeout rate over the past five years. If he finally breaks out, that’s great. But even if not, there’s no real cost for the O’s.

articles.title: Brewers Acquire Ryan Walker
body: The Brewers announced that right-hander Ryan Walker has been acquired in a trade with the Giants. Right-handed pitching prospects Blake Holub and Gavin Perry head to San Francisco as the return. Milwaukee has seven open spots on its 40-man roster, so no further moves were needed to accommodate Walker’s arrival.

Walker is projected to earn $1.6MM in 2027, his first year of arbitration eligibility. The righty was widely considered to be a non-tender candidate in the wake of his unproductive season, and it is possible the Brewers could still cut him loose prior to Friday’s non-tender deadline. However, Walker’s salary is small enough and has enough of a track record that the Brew Crew probably see him as a bounce-back candidate for next season’s bullpen.

Going to a World Series-winning team with a reputation for fixing struggling pitchers is a very nice outcome for Walker in the wake of a 2026 season that quickly went off the rails. Heading into the year as perhaps the favorite for saves in the Giants’ closer committee, Walker was rocked for a 6.46 ERA in his first 15 1/3 innings and 16 appearances before he was optioned to Triple-A in May.

San Francisco called him back up a month later but Walker was sent back and forth a couple more times en route to a 7.16 ERA, 14.8% strikeout rate, and 12.3% walk rate across 32 2/3 total big league innings. The warning signs started to emerge for Walker in 2025 when his strikeout, whiff, and chase rates dropped significantly from the 2024 campaign.

articles.title: Five Teams Interested In A.J. Minter
body: The Royals, Rangers, Phillies, Nationals, and Blue Jays are some of the teams involved in A.J. Minter’s market, MLB Network’s Jon Morosi reports. The veteran left-hander is a free agent for the second time in his career, following the expiration of the two-year, $22MM deal he signed with the Mets during the 2024-25 offseason.

Minter ended up appearing in only 36 games for New York, as a lat surgery in early May 2025 kept him off the mound for a little over a year. Finally returning this past May 26, Minter posted a 2.56 ERA, 4.3% walk rate, and 22% strikeout rate over 45 2/3 combined innings with the Mets and Twins, as Minnesota acquired the left-hander at the trade deadline.

Given that a hip surgery also cut short Minter’s 2024 season with the Braves, simply getting back to action was a nice outcome for Minter, on top of his solid bottom-line numbers. The advanced metrics were a little more unusual, as Minter’s walk rate was a career best over a full season (and way below his previous 8.6% career average) while his strikeout rate was a career worst, and significant below the 29.4K% he posted from 2017-25.

articles.title: Orioles Interested In Ketel Marte
body: The Orioles and Diamondbacks have had some talks about Ketel Marte, MLB.com’s Jake Rill reports. “No deal was imminent at the time,” Rill writes, and it isn’t known if the discussions were a due-diligence check-in on Baltimore’s part, or if the O’s have a keener interest in the three-time All-Star.

Marte’s availability is certainly the biggest storyline of the Diamondbacks’ offseason, yet the second baseman holds all the cards to a potential deal due to his no-trade rights as a 10-and-5 player. The relationship between Marte and the team may already in an awkward state due to his no-show of a game in Boston in August, which was the most public of a few instances of Marte reportedly skipping out of games in the last few years. If Marte himself wants out of Arizona, he hasn’t shared any details publicly or even with the D’Backs, as per recent reports.

To further complicate matters, Marte hit.249/.316/.432 with 22 homers over 624 plate appearances in 2026. This translated to a 103 wRC+, well below the 134 wRC+ Marte averaged in his previous seven seasons. It remains to be seen if this downturn could be health-related (Marte spent some time on the 10-day IL due to left knee inflammation following the Boston incident), some mental stress stemming from the clubhouse issues, or perhaps just the aging curve as Marte is set to enter his age-33 season.

articles.title: Pablo Sandoval Announces Retirement
body: Pablo Sandoval has announced the end of his playing career, after 14 Major League seasons and parts of 21 total seasons in pro ball. The longtime third baseman is saying his farewell after a few more games with Navegantes del Magallanes, the Venezuelan winter league club Sandoval suited up for at the very start of his career (and at a couple of other points during his two-plus decades as a player). The Turcos faced Tiburones de La Guaira in a two-game series at loanDepot Park in Miami this weekend, and Sandoval marked the occasion by hitting a grand slam in his final game in a big league ballpark.

“The Kung Fu Panda” last played in a MLB game in 2021 as a member of the Braves. He played with two Mexican League teams in 2022 and a team in Dubai in 2023, then signed a minor league deal with the Giants during Spring Training 2024 but was released prior to Opening Day. Sandoval played for the Staten Island FerryHawks of the independent Atlantic League in both 2024 and 2025, and is now officially hanging up his cleats at age 40.

articles.title: Latest On Brewers’ First Base Mix
body: The Brewers just saw this year’s first baseman Jake Bauers depart for the Red Sox on a four-year, $58MM deal, contrary to MLBTR readers’ prediction that he would accept Milwaukee’s qualifying offer. With Bauers gone, the Brewers won’t necessarily add another first baseman for the 2027 season, according to The Athletic’s Will Sammon and Ken Rosenthal. Sammon and Rosenthal write that the team could retain Andrew Vaughn in arbitration or turn to one of their prospects, while throwing cold water on the team’s chances of pursuing Ty France.

Vaughn is projected for an $8.5MM salary, according to MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz. He appeared in 104 games for the Brewers this year and took 331 trips to the plate. In that sample, he batted.306/.390/.444 with a 134 wRC+. Vaughn was quite productive against southpaws, putting up a 161 wRC+ in 133 plate appearances, though he more than held his own with a 117 wRC+ against same-handed pitchers.

The overall production was more or less a continuation of Vaughn’s output last year with Milwaukee. He came over from the White Sox that June in a cash trade for Aaron Civale, and Vaughn proceeded to put up a.308/.375/.493 triple slash in 254 plate appearances for the Brewers, good for a 142 wRC+. The main differences this year were a decline in power and improved batted ball fortune. Vaughn saw his isolated power decline from.158 to.139, and he only hit six home runs all season. He also batted.355 on balls in play, which is sure to come down.

articles.title: White Sox Interested In Hiromi Itoh
body: The White Sox are known to be seeking rotation upgrades this winter, and they’ve identified Japanese right-hander Hiromi Itoh as one of their targets. According to Francys Romero of BeisbolFR.com, the Sox sent scouts to watch Itoh and his countryman Kaima Taira in August and September, and they’re expected to be among Itoh’s suitors in free agency. Chicago’s interest in Taira was previously reported.

Itoh, Taira, and infielder Teruaki Sato were officially posted by their respective NPB teams on November 1. Ordinarily, they would have had 45 days to negotiate a contract with MLB clubs, but the looming lockout is throwing a wrench in those plans. The day after their postings, it was reported that their negotiating window would not pause in the event of a lockout, so their 45-day window is effectively reduced to just 30 days. Itoh, Taira, and Sato now have a little more than two weeks to sign with MLB clubs. If they do not, they’ll return to NPB for 2027.

Among the two starters in that trio, Itoh isn’t as flashy as Taira but should still procure a big league deal. He has a 2.91 earned run average and 902 career strikeouts in just over 1,000 innings for the Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters. In 2025, he won the Sawamura Award, the NPB equivalent of the Cy Young award. Itoh has also shown excellent control, posting walk rates of 5.5% or lower in each of the last three seasons for the Fighters.

articles.title: Phillies Sign Max Kranick To Minor League Deal
body: The Phillies are bringing in right-hander Max Kranick on a minor league deal, reports Will Sammon of The Athletic. It’s a non-roster, split contract for the Covenant Sports Group client. The precise salary terms are not clear, though Kranick will presumably earn more than the minor league minimum for any time spent there. Sammon adds that the Phillies will give Kranick a chance to work as a starter.

Kranick, 29, has pitched in parts of four major league seasons from 2021-26. He tossed 43 2/3 innings for the Pirates from 2021-22 before undergoing Tommy John surgery in June of the latter year. He spent 2023-24 recovering, then pitching at Triple-A for the Pirates and Mets’ affiliates. Resurfacing in the Majors in 2025, Kranick had a 3.65 earned run average in 37 innings for the Mets before undergoing flexor tendon surgery that July.

Kranick joined the Nationals organization this past May while he wrapped up his recovery from surgery. He debuted for the team in July but delivered an unsightly 9.33 ERA in 17 appearances. Velocity wasn’t the problem, as Kranick averaged 95.4 mph on his four-seamer, nearly matching his 2025 velocity. Instead, the righty was far too wild on the mound. He surrendered 13 walks in just 18 1/3 innings pitched, and he walked more hitters (13.8%) than he struck out (11.7%). He allowed 27 hits in total, four of which were home runs.

articles.title: Mets Among Suitors For Ty France
body: First baseman Ty France was one of the underrated gems of the 2026 season, batting.295/.363/.502 with a 141 wRC+ for the Padres after entering camp on a non-roster deal. Now, he rates as the No. 23 free agent on MLBTR’s Top 50 list as well as arguably the best first baseman available. Just over a week ago, it was reported that “multiple teams” are showing interest in France. The Mets are one of those suitors, as Mark W. Sanchez of The New York Post reports that New York has touched base with France’s camp as they look to upgrade at first base.

The Mets got terrible production at the cold corner this year, so it’s no surprise they’re exploring all options. First basemen around the league combined for a 114 wRC+ in 2026, with all but six teams getting above-average hitting out of that spot. Unfortunately, the Mets were one of those six clubs. The team ranked second worst with an 85 wRC+ at first base. Only the Diamondbacks (74 wRC+) got less production.

articles.title: Yankees Re-Sign Tim Hill To One-Year Deal
body: The Yankees are bringing back a known quantity for their bullpen. Left-hander Tim Hill is returning on a one-year, $2.25MM deal, per ESPN’s Jeff Passan. The pact includes a $2.5MM club option for the 2028 season. Hill is a client of Paragon Sports International.

Hill, who will turn 37 in Spring Training, has pitched for the Yankees since midway through the 2024 season. The soft-tossing lefty is primarily a ground ball specialist. He has a 63.2% ground ball rate for his career, and since the start of 2024, over two-thirds of batted balls against Hill have been on the ground. That’s easily the best mark among qualified relievers in that span.

For the first two years of his Yankees tenure, Hill backed that up with solid run prevention. In 111 innings with New York from 2024-25, he delivered a 2.68 earned run average, held opposing hitters to a.604 OPS, and posted a sharp 5.7% walk rate. Hill’s 44.0% hard-hit rate in that time was not great, but thanks to the gaudy ground ball numbers, he did a good job of keeping the ball in the yard. He allowed only ten home runs in that span with New York, a rate of 0.81 homers per nine innings.

articles.title: Phillies Interested In Jonathan Loaisiga
body: Reports indicate that right-hander Jonathan Loaisiga is receiving widespread interest in free agency. The Dodgers were the most recent entrant into his market alongside the Yankees, Mets, and Blue Jays. It appears the Phillies have also entered the fray for Loaisiga’s services, as reported by Jon Heyman of the New York Post. That makes at least five known suitors for the 32-year-old reliever, whom MLBTR projects to earn a two-year, $13MM deal.

Loaisiga is coming off his best season in five years. Despite having a length injury history, including IL stints in every season from 2019-25, he finally stayed off the IL in 2026 and delivered 67 innings out of the Diamondbacks’ bullpen. That was a nice surprise considering Loaisiga entered Spring Training as a non-roster invitee. Even better, he delivered a stellar 2.42 earned run average, 56.4% ground ball rate, and 5.0% walk rate, making him one of Arizona’s best relievers and a key upside play for bullpen-needy clubs in free agency.

That Loaisiga managed a 67-inning total is impressive considering he combined for just 51 1/3 innings from 2023-25 with the Yankees. Since breaking out with a 2.17 ERA in 70 2/3 innings back in 2021, Loaisiga had missed time for shoulder inflammation, elbow inflammation, a torn UCL (which required season-ending surgery in April 2024), and mid-back tightness. From 2022-25, he had a 3.81 ERA in just under 100 innings with a subpar 9.4% K-BB rate but an excellent 55.5% ground ball rate.

articles.title: Latest On Ketel Marte
body: Diamondbacks officials met with Ketel Marte’s agent Charisse Espinosa-Dash during the GM Meetings this week, but the D’Backs “but did not seem to come away with a clear idea about what teams to which Marte would be willing to approve a deal,” the Arizona Republic’s Nick Piecoro writes. Marte has full no-trade protection as a 10-and-5 player, so even though he is one of the offseason’s most prominent trade candidates, the possibility exists that Marte will remain in Arizona simply because he isn’t interested in changing teams.

It puts the D’Backs in something of an awkward position, especially since the impending lockout will interrupt all transactions activity for what could be months on end. If Marte isn’t dealt by 10:59pm CT on December 1 (when the current collective bargaining agreement expires and the league is expected to lock out the players), the uncertainty over his future will continue to linger over all of the Diamondbacks’ remaining offseason plans.

As Piecoro puts it, “the Diamondbacks seem to have little choice but to sort of blindly attempt to make the best deal possible without knowing whether Marte will approve it.” In terms of what that best deal might entail, Piecoro writes that the D’Backs have looked into all variety of trades in their early discussions about Marte — bringing in just prospects, swapping the second baseman for other established big league talents, or a trade package of both veteran and younger talent.

articles.title: Adalberto Mondesi Attempting Comeback
body: Former Royals speedster Adalberto Mondesi is trying to get back to the majors, reports Will Sammon, Ken Rosenthal, and Katie Woo of The Athletic. Mondesi is currently playing winter ball in the Dominican Republic. His last big-league stint was in 2022.

Mondesi, 31, has appeared in three games with Aguilas. He’s 4-for-12 with two doubles and a triple so far. He also has four strikeouts. It’s the first live action for Mondesi in four years. He was most recently in Boston’s organization, but knee surgery cost him all of 2023. He was released at the end of the year and never latched on elsewhere.

At his peak, Mondesi was one of the biggest threats on the bases in the league. He stole 75 bases across 2018 and 2019, his first extended look as a big leaguer. He paced the league in triples in 2019. Mondesi led the majors with 24 steals in the shortened 2020 season.

The main drawback in Mondesi’s offensive profile was contact. He punched out at an alarming clip, particularly for a player lacking premier power. Mondesi has a 30.2% strikeout rate over 1,366 career plate appearances.

Mondesi spent time at second base, third base, and shortstop with the Royals. He had up-and-down results as a defender, but generally netted out as a neutral option at each spot. He’s played both second base and shortstop with Aguilas.

articles.title: Yankees Notes: Bullpen, Morejon, Coaches
body: The Yankees had the second-best bullpen ERA in the league last season. Maintaining that level will take some work this offseason, with several key pieces hitting free agency.
General manager Brian Cashman referred to the bullpen as New York’s “main priority” during an appearance on MLB Network Radio on SiriusXM this week (h/t Bryan Hoch of MLB.com).

Hoch adds that the Yankees are interested in bringing back two members of the 2026 relief corps, Tim Hill and Paul Blackburn. The team already issued a qualifying offer to closer David Bednar. The former Pirate excelled in his first full season as New York’s stopper and will likely reject the QO. Several teams are known to be in on Hill, including the Mets, Dodgers, Cardinals, Guardians, and Giants.

The club already re-upped with Blackburn once, retaining him on a one-year, $2MM deal last winter. Blackburn originally joined the organization in 2025 after he was cut by the Mets. He struggled in eight games to finish the season and came back on a cheap deal. Blackburn emerged as one of the most effective relievers in the league in 2026, compiling a 1.59 ERA over 85 frames.
[Related: How Paul Blackburn Became An Elite Reliever]
Blackburn ranked 41st on our Top 50 Free Agents list. We predict a two-year, $15MM deal. It’s not a massive price tag, but it’s certainly a step up from Blackburn’s last free agent agreement.
Here are a few other Yankees items…

articles.title: Kris Bubic Drawing Widespread Interest
body: While Tarik Skubal is getting the big headlines, another former Dodgers lefty is also drawing plenty of attention. Will Sammon and Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic report that Kris Bubic is picking up interest “from contenders and non-contenders alike.”

Bubic has been slowed by arm injuries the past two seasons. His 2025 campaign was cut short by a rotator cuff strain. He made it through nine starts with the Royals to open this past season before going down with elbow soreness. Bubic began a rehab assignment in June, only to be shut down again with renewed elbow issues.

The Dodgers took a flyer on Bubic at the trade deadline, sending over a minor league pitcher in exchange for his services. Bubic made it back as a reliever during the final two weeks of the regular season. He put together five scoreless outings and made the club’s postseason roster. Bubic allowed runs in both of his playoff appearances, taking a loss in the NLDS and a blown save in the NLCS.

The 29-year-old Bubic debuted with Kansas City in 2020. He was a high draft pick and well-regarded prospect in the organization, but spent three seasons as a mediocre starter. Bubic had his 2023 almost entirely wiped out by Tommy John surgery. He returned as a reliever in 2024 and revived his career. The lefty posted a 2.67 ERA with an elite 32.2% strikeout rate in 27 games out of the Royals’ bullpen. Bubic reverted to the rotation in 2025 and delivered 20 starts of a 2.55 ERA and nearly a strikeout per inning.

articles.title: Astros AGM Connor Huff Resigns
body: The Astros have made a pair of major staffing additions this offseason, hiring Randy Flores as general manager and Brad Ausmus as skipper. The club also had a subtraction this week, with Flores announcing that assistant general manager Connor Huff has left the organization.

Flores told reporters, including Chandler Rome of The Athletic, that Huff resigned to take a “new, exciting opportunity outside of baseball.” Huff had been with the team since 2022. He was promoted from vice president of business and baseball operations to AGM at the end of the 2025 season. Huff replaced former assistant GM Andrew Ball.

Houston still has two AGMs on staff, Gavin Dickey and Charles Cook. Both interviewed for the role that ultimately went to Flores. Houston had a vacancy in its top front office position after moving on from Dana Brown in August. Flores mentioned that he’d been given the go-ahead to hire a replacement for Huff, though he didn’t specify whether it would be for an AGM role or a different position.

The Astros are looking to rebound after an uneven year. Brown was fired with a month left in the regular season. Manager Joe Espada was retained at the time, but it was pretty clear he wouldn’t be with the club beyond 2026. Houston backed into a division title despite a.500 record and was quickly booted from the playoffs in a sweep by the White Sox.

articles.title: Pirates Want To Limit Ryan O’Hearn’s Outfield Reps
body: The Pirates have Oneil Cruz and Bryan Reynolds as everyday options in center and left field, respectively. Right field is more of a question mark, as general manager Ben Cherington outlined this week at the GM Meetings.

Cherington told reporters, including Colin Beazley of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, that the club is looking to construct a team that doesn’t require Ryan O’Hearn to spend much time on the grass. The plan would be to have him rotate at first base and DH with Spencer Horwitz. Cherington added that ideally, O’Hearn makes just the occasional start or late-game appearance in right field.

Pittsburgh signed O’Hearn to a two-year, $29MM deal last winter. He was expected to split his time between right field and first base, with fellow free agent acquisition Marcell Ozuna handling the majority of the DH work. That’s largely how it played out, with O’Hearn making 42 starts in right field and 36 at first base. Ozuna’s ill-fated tenure with the team ended in August. O’Hearn ended up making 25 starts at DH.
[Related: Ryan O’Hearn’s Adjustments In Pittsburgh]

Capping O’Hearn’s opportunities in the outfield makes sense on multiple fronts. He posted -5 Defensive Runs Saved at the position in 2026. For his career, he’s at -16 DRS. O’Hearn has typically graded out poorly at first base as well, though he’s had some decent years over there. Perhaps more notably, O’Hearn had two separate stints on the IL with quad strains last year. The second instance cost him nearly six weeks in the second half and hurt Pittsburgh’s offense during the stretch run.

articles.title: A’s Receiving Trade Interest In Jacob Wilson
body: Jacob Wilson’s All-Star rookie season was followed up by an injury-plagued 2026 campaign, as the Athletics’ shortstop hit only.266/.298/.388 over 337 plate appearances. Wilson sprained his left shoulder in May while diving for a Gunnar Henderson grounder, and while he missed only a month on the injured list, renewed shoulder discomfort sent him back to the IL for good in late August, and Wilson underwent a season-ending surgery on his troublesome shoulder in early September.

Despite this rough sophomore year and the $66MM remaining on Wilson’s contract, the shortstop has been drawing trade interest, according to USA Today’s Bob Nightengale. This could just be some due diligence from rival clubs, or explorations to see if the A’s would bite on a lowball offer. There isn’t any indication that the A’s are even considering moving Wilson, and a trade would be pretty surprising given that Wilson signed his long-term extension with the club just last January.

It should be noted that Wilson’s extension was signed under former GM David Forst, so new president of baseball operations Taylor Smith could have a different view of Wilson as a long-term cornerstone. There haven’t been any updates on Wilson’s recovery timeline, so if he will miss a decent chunk of the 2027 season, that also might impact the Athletics’ willingness to consider trade possibilities. That said, one would also imagine clubs wouldn’t be willing to trade for Wilson without a long look at his medicals in the wake of his surgery.

articles.title: NL East Notes: Braves, Iglesias, Nationals, Thompson, Marlins
body: The Braves made a big new bullpen addition by signing Evan Phillips on Thursday, and the Tigers just added a prominent high-leverage reliever in Emilio Pagan. Even after these moves, reporter Francys Romero writes that Atlanta and Detroit are still interested in veteran closer Raisel Iglesias. For the Braves, it would mark the second straight offseason they’ve re-signed Iglesias, after re-upping with the righty on a one-year, $16MM pact.

Obviously there’s plenty of familiarity between the two sides, and Iglesias has continue to pitch so well that there isn’t much concern of a slowdown even after he enters his age-37 season. The Athletic’s Will Sammon and Ken Rosenthal note that re-signing Iglesias to strengthen the bullpen would increase the chance that the Braves will use Didier Fuentes as a starter next season, though Atlanta figures to add a more proven starter even if Fuentes is indeed stretched out in Spring Training.

articles.title: Dodgers Interested In Jonathan Loaisiga, Tim Hill
body: Right-hander Jonathan Loaisiga and left-hander Tim Hill are two of the relievers on the Dodgers’ radar, according to (respectively) ESPN’s Jesse Rogers and the New York Post’s Jon Heyman. Rogers notes that Loaisiga is “getting closer” to landing a deal, so a signing might come sooner rather than later.

Beyond Los Angeles, Loaisiga and Hill have also each drawn interest from the Yankees (their mutual former team) and Mets. The Blue Jays have been linked to Loaisiga as well, and Rogers suggests that at least one other team is also in on the right-hander. The Guardians, Giants, and Cardinals have all been linked to Hill in previous reports.

For Loaisiga in particular, this healthy market is a terrific outcome for a pitcher who had to settle for a minor league deal with the Diamondbacks last winter. The righty had shown flashes of being an elite relief arm during his eight seasons with the Yankees, yet injuries continually kept Loaisiga on the sidelines. New York declined a $5MM club option on Loaisiga after the 2025 season, and he was both healthy and very effective in delivering a 2.42 ERA over 67 innings out of Arizona’s pen in 2026.

While Loaisiga doesn’t rack up many strikeouts, he induces a ton of grounders and a lot of soft contact, plus he has a strong 6.3% walk rate in 260 innings since the start of the 2020 season. MLB Trade Rumors ranked Loaisiga 45th on our top 50 free agents list and projected a two-year, $13MM contract, making him a potential bargain for a lot of teams provided the 32-year-old can again avoid the injury bug.

articles.title: Padres Interested In Freddy Peralta, Nick Martinez, Matthew Boyd
body: The Padres have interest in free agent starters Freddy Peralta and Nick Martinez, according to ESPN’s Alden Gonzalez. Matthew Boyd is another name of interest to the team, as per Kevin Acee of the San Diego Union-Tribune, though Acee notes that the Padres have “showed some level of interest in virtually every starting pitcher on the market….rather than list the starters whose representatives the Padres talked to, suffice it to say there is hardly a starting pitcher they are not considering.”

The rotation push is understandable given that Michael King, Nick Pivetta, Walker Buehler, Casey Mize, Robbie Ray, and Griffin Canning are all free agents. This leaves San Diego with a current starting staff of Randy Vasquez, JP Sears, Joe Musgrove (who may be used in the bullpen), newly-signed swingman candidate Ryan Weiss, and maybe Yu Darvish, if the veteran still wants to continue his career.

Suffice it to say, the Padres need to fill at least four and maybe five rotation spots this winter, leaving the team searching every corner of the starting pitching market (and undoubtedly the trade market as well). Peralta, Martinez, and Boyd represent a range of starters and potential price points for the Friars. On our list of the offseason’s top 50 free agents, MLBTR projected Peralta for a five-year, $110MM contract, Martinez for two years and $42MM, and Boyd for a one-year, $13MM deal.

articles.title: AL Central Notes: White Sox, Twins, Burg, Guardians
body: The White Sox are focused on bolstering their rotation this winter, both with external additions and internal moves like moving Grant Taylor from the bullpen to a starting role. Even with Taylor leaving the relief mix, however, GM Chris Getz downplayed the idea of prioritizing the bullpen when speaking with the Chicago Sun-Times’ James Fegan and other reporters. Rather than invest heavily in relievers, the Sox could use any excess starters in bullpen roles, with perhaps a lower-cost veteran or two added later in the offseason for added depth.

Since the White Sox are so deep in infield prospects, it has been suggested that the club could trade from this depth to address other needs. Getz didn’t rule this possibility out in the future, but it is “not something that I would say we’re entertaining right now.” It’s a fair stance to take, as the Sox might not want to move any younger talent until they have a better idea of which of these infielders they view as true building blocks. Despite Chicago’s unexpected AL Central title, the Sox aren’t going to pivot entirely away from their rebuilding plan, and the current infield grouping of Miguel Vargas, Colson Montgomery, Chase Meidroth, and Munetaka Murakami all contributed heavily to the playoff run.
More from around the AL Central…

articles.title: Blue Jays Interested In Teruaki Sato
body: At least seven teams have been publicly linked to Teruaki Sato’s market, and The Athletic’s Mitch Bannon reports that the Blue Jays also have interest in the Hanshin Tigers slugger. The news comes as no surprise, given the Jays’ need for offense, their tendency to check in on virtually every free agent available, and the team’s increasing forays into the Japanese talent market.

Last winter’s signing of Kazuma Okamoto represents the high point of Toronto’s overtures to Japanese players, though Okamoto’s presence also creates a bit of an obstacle in regards to Sato, who is also a third baseman. Sato also has experience as a corner outfielder and isn’t considered a premium defender at any of his positions, so he might well end up getting a good chunk of DH time in the majors. The Blue Jays have vacancies to fill in both left field and DH, plus Sato could still get the odd turn at third base if Okamoto is given a DH day or an off-day.

Sato has been at least a productive hitter during all six of his NPB seasons, but his last two seasons in particular have been stellar, highlighted by a Triple Crown-winning campaign in 2026. Sato delivered 39 homers, 106 RBI, and a.306/.383/.609 slash line over 614 PA for the Tigers last season, and he also went deep 40 times for the 2025 club. If Sato can translate any of this power over to the majors, it would be a huge boost to a Blue Jays team that finished with a league-worst 152 home runs in 2026.

articles.title: Giants Notes: Rotation, Bullpen, Catcher
body: The Giants have made no secret of their desire to add at least one starter. They’re not planning to make a run at Tarik Skubal and seem to be out on Trevor Rogers, who’s attached to draft compensation via the qualifying offer. San Francisco has been loosely linked to Freddy Peralta and to NPB righty Kaima Taira, though there’s a decent chance they look more to the middle tiers of the market.

Logan Webb and Landen Roupp are the only two starters locked into the season-opening rotation. President of baseball operations Buster Posey has implicitly suggested that next season might be something of a bridge year with most of their top prospect talent in the lower minors. However, USA Today’s Bob Nightengale writes that they’re continuing to rebuff teams who call about Webb.

That’s not surprising, as the Giants publicly shot down speculation about trading their ace early in deadline season. Webb is signed for two more seasons. There’s a reasonable argument for listening on him if the Giants aren’t going to make an all-in push next year, but the organization clearly doesn’t want to embark on a full rebuild either. If they were going to listen on Webb, it’d have made more sense to do it over the summer when they were en route to a 97-loss season.

articles.title: Rays Rumors: DeLuca, McClanahan, Pepiot, Rasmussen
body: The Rays could make center fielder Jonny DeLuca available in trade this offseason, write Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon of The Athletic. The idea would be to open center field for Victor Mesa Jr., who played mostly right field this year.

DeLuca is coming off a career-best year in his third season as a Ray. He stole 17 bases and connected 11 home runs while batting.266/.300/.429 in a career-high 370 plate appearances. He divided his defensive workload between center and right field, playing strong defense at both spots. The 28-year-old missed a month with a right hamstring strain but was on the field much more often than he had been in 2025. The Oregon product was limited to 20 games that year by a right shoulder strain and a left hamstring injury.

The righty-hitting DeLuca provides most of his value in a speed and defense capacity. He’s a serviceable but unexceptional hitter, batting.250/.295/.389 in his career. DeLuca has had reverse platoon splits, posting a.709 OPS against righties compared to a.642 mark versus left-handed pitching. He has an aggressive approach and doesn’t make a ton of hard contact. He’s an elite runner who rates as one of the rangiest defensive outfielders in the game. DeLuca is under arbitration control for three seasons and projected by MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz for a $1.7MM salary.

articles.title: Nationals Release Kyle Nicolas
body: The Nationals released reliever Kyle Nicolas, according to the MLB.com transaction tracker. Washington designated him for assignment a week ago when they acquired Reiver Sanmartin from San Francisco.

Nicolas never pitched in a major league game with the Nats. Washington acquired the righty from the Orioles in early July, a trade most notable for being the first between the franchises after two decades of acrimony. They kept him on optional assignment to Triple-A Rochester for the rest of the season. Nicolas turned in a 3.27 ERA with a 29% strikeout rate for the Red Wings, but he walked a massive 18.7% of batters faced. Washington didn’t give him a look despite having one of the worst bullpens in the league.

A former Competitive Balance Round draftee out of Ball State, Nicolas has pitched parts of four MLB seasons between the Pirates and Reds. He’s posted an earned run average just under 5.00 across 105 1/3 career innings. Nicolas has huge stuff, sitting in the 98-99 mph range and sporting both a power slider and curveball. He’s never been able to harness it effectively, walking 14% of MLB opponents and more than 16% of batters faced at the Triple-A level.

Nicolas has never been outrighted in his career. Washington could have kept him in the farm system without a roster spot but elected to release him. That sometimes indicates a player is weighing overseas interest.

articles.title: Royals In Market For Right-Handed Hitting Outfielder
body: The Royals are looking for a right-handed hitting outfielder, general manager J.J. Picollo told reporters at the GM Meetings this week (link via ESPN’s Jesse Rogers). The GM added that an acquisition would ideally be capable of playing center field on at least a part-time basis.

That’s essentially the role Lane Thomas played for K.C. this year. They picked him up on a one-year, $5.25MM free agent contract last offseason. Thomas played reasonably well for a half-season, batting.232/.326/.393 across 97 games. He started 72 contests in the outfield, 52 of them up the middle. They traded him to Atlanta at the deadline for a pair of minor league pitchers and to dump what remained of Bailey Falter’s arbitration salary.

Thomas didn’t play particularly well for the Braves. He’s back on the market and might be available even more cheaply than he was a year ago if the Royals wanted to reengage. Tyrone Taylor, Myles Straw, Jake Meyers and Victor Robles are other possibilities as fourth/fifth outfield types. If the Royals wanted a potential everyday center fielder, Luis Robert Jr. is the top right-handed hitter on the free agent market.

articles.title: Angels, Tyler Heineman Avoid Arbitration
body: The Angels announced that they have signed catcher Tyler Heineman to a one-year deal for the 2027 season worth $1.2375MM. They also re-signed left-hander Sammy Peralta via a minor league contract with an invitation to spring training.

Heineman, 36 in June, is a journeyman catcher. He has played for the Marlins, Giants, Blue Jays, Pirates, Red Sox and Angels in his career. He had a really nice season with the Jays in 2025, backing up Alejandro Kirk. Heineman hit.289/.361/.416 in 174 plate appearances. He also got strong grades for his work behind the plate. FanGraphs credited him with 2.1 wins above replacement. He got into a couple of postseason games as the Jays made a World Series run.

Though he was 34 years old, he qualified for arbitration for the first time after that season. The Jays tendered him a contract for his age-35 season and the two sides avoided a hearing by agreeing to a salary of $1.2375. Unfortunately, he couldn’t carry things over into 2026. While Kirk was on the injured list, the Jays called up Brandon Valenzuela to share the catching duties with Heineman. Valenzuela played well as Heineman struggled. Heineman is out of options so he was designated for assignment when Kirk came off the IL.

articles.title: Cardinals Reportedly Turned Away Trade Interest In Burleson, Winn
body: The Cardinals are fielding calls on a lot of players on their roster. Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch reports that the Cards have received interested in catchers Jimmy Crooks and Pedro Pagés, shortstop Masyn Winn and first baseman Alec Burleson, though Goold notes that the club quickly turned away the interest in both Winn and Burleson.

It’s not surprising that the phone would ring. The Cardinals have been in seller mode for a while. Last offseason, they traded away Sonny Gray, Nolan Arenado, Willson Contreras and Brendan Donovan to clear payroll and make room for younger players. At this year’s deadline, they traded away Dustin May, JoJo Romero and Lars Nootbaar. Those pitchers were all impending free agents while each position player was under club control through at least 2027.

With all that selling, it’s understandable that clubs with needs would keep the lines open. The Cards seem to be planning for 2027 to be another evaluation year, so players nearing free agency would be logical trade candidates.

Burleson is under club control through 2028. The Cards could emerge as legitimate contenders in that time frame but it’s unclear how aggressively they plan to tackle things in that window. He just hit 26 home runs this year and slashed.279/.343/.473, so now would be a good time to sell high.

articles.title: Blue Jays Rumors: Valenzuela, Clement, Smith, Schneider, Pitching
body: The hot stove is warming up. The Blue Jays haven’t made a big move yet but the buzz on them continues to be that they’re exploring just about everything. Mitch Bannon of The Athletic as well as Ben-Nicholson Smith and Shi Davidi of Sportsnet have details on some of the various things that are up in the air with the club.

Bannon notes that the Jays are getting some trade interest in catcher Brandon Valenzuela. Bannon doesn’t specify which clubs are calling but notes that the Reds have had previous interest. Valenzuela had an encouraging debut this year, getting into 91 games for the Jays. He made 271 plate appearances and hit.222/.307/.372. That translates to a 93 wRC+, indicating he was 7% worse than the league average hitter. Catchers are usually 10 to 12% below par, so that’s actually decent production, especially for a backup. Valenzuela also received strong grades for his glovework. FanGraphs credited him with 2.1 wins above replacement.

The Jays could certainly keep Valenzuela as backup to Alejandro Kirk. However, if some other club considers him to be a viable everyday catcher and is willing to pay for him accordingly in terms of a trade return, it could be worth Toronto’s while. In theory, the Jays could flip Valenzuela for a bat or an arm or a package of players and then turn to free agency to find a backup for Kirk.

articles.title: Cubs Notes: Ramirez, Kelly, Hoyer, Staffing
body: The Cubs have two spots to fill in the outfield alongside newly minted NL MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong with Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki heading to free agency. The internal replacements include Pedro Ramirez, Matt Shaw, and Kevin Alcantara. Ramirez could be the leader in the clubhouse based on recent comments from GM Carter Hawkins.

The lead exec praised Ramirez’ athleticism and work ethic, factors that could help him transition into a more versatile role, as relayed by Meghan Montemurro of the Chicago Tribune. The 22-year-old primarily played second and third base in the minors, but played some first base and left field after his big-league promotion.

“There’s a risk to going with some unproven guys, but that allows you maybe to get some more proven guys in other spots,” Hawkins said. “I don’t think there’s one path that we necessarily would cross out at this juncture.”

Ramirez forced his way to the majors by hitting.312 with nine homers and 19 steals in 43 games at Triple-A. He held his own in his first taste of the highest level, slashing.261/.321/.402 across 266 plate appearances. Ramirez added six homers and nine steals. The thefts have always been a part of his profile, but the power was a big addition in 2026. He’d totaled 25 homers in four pro seasons before popping 15 this year.

articles.title: Cubs, White Sox, Padres Among Teams Interested In Kaima Taira
body: Right-hander Kaima Taira, star for the Seibu Lions of Japan’s Nippon Professional Baseball, is drawing widespread interest after being posted for major league clubs. Bruce Levine of 670 The Score in Chicago reports that both the Cubs and White Sox have “strong” interest in Taira. They were both planning to meet with agent Scott Boras this week, though the Boras Corporation of course represents a large number of this winter’s free agents beyond just Taira. Kevin Acee of the San Diego Union-Tribune writes that while the Padres have some level of interest in all three NPB stars who were posted this winter — slugger Teruaki Sato and righty Hiromi Itoh being the others — the Friars seem particularly focused on Taira.

The Blue Jays were known to have scouted Taira extensively this past season and have carried their interest into the offseason, per Sportsnet’s Shi Davidi. Toronto has done “lots of background work” on Taira, per the report. Davidi adds that Taira isn’t traveling to North America to meet with interested clubs in person but is conducting frequent Zoom calls with teams major league clubs. That presumably includes Toronto, though it’s not clear whether the two parties have formally spoken or are still lining up a time to do so. The Giants also have some interest in Taira and have discussed him internally, according to John Shea of the San Francisco Standard.

articles.title: Tigers Interested In Shota Imanaga
body: The Tigers entered the offseason in search of help in the rotation and the bullpen. They’ve already addressed the latter, adding former Reds closer Emilio Pagan this week. As far as starting pitching, Jon Morosi of MLB Network reports that left-hander Shota Imanaga is among the free agents the club is interested in.

Imanaga hit free agency last winter but ultimately stayed with the Cubs after accepting the qualifying offer. The 33-year-old is back on the market this offseason and won’t have the QO attached to him this time around. Imanaga put together 32 starts of a 3.77 ERA with nearly a strikeout per inning in 2026. He tossed a career-high 174 1/3 innings as basically the only Cubs starter to stay healthy all year.

Homers are the big issue for Imanaga. He’s a flyball pitcher with middling strikeout stuff. When the wind was blowing in at Wrigley Field, he was an elite starter. When it was blowing out, the long balls came in bunches. Only Phillies righty Aaron Nola (37) gave up more home runs than Imanaga (35) in 2026.

Comerica Park would be an upgrade for Imanaga. Statcast’s Park Factors ranked it 14th for home runs over the past three seasons. Wrigley Field comes in at No. 8 on the leaderboard. For right-handed power, there was basically no difference. Chicago ranked 11th and Detroit ranked 12th for righty homers.

articles.title: Marlins Interested In Patrick Sandoval
body: The Marlins have shown interest in free agent lefty Patrick Sandoval, reports Kevin Barral of Fish On First.

Miami’s rotation has three arms locked into rotation spots: Sandy Alcantara, Eury Pérez and Max Meyer. The final two spots, at present, are filled by swingmen Janson Junk, Ryan Gusto and Tyler Phillips. Top prospects Thomas White and Robby Snelling are effectively ready for big league looks — at least once they’re healthy. Snelling underwent UCL surgery last May just a few starts into his promising young career. White’s season ended in June after he suffered a capsule sprain in his left shoulder.

Meyer and Pérez both missed time due to injuries in 2026 as well. Given the level of injury risk and lack of back-end stability in the Miami rotation, adding some reinforcements is a natural goal. Sandoval, 30, is coming off a lackluster performance in his first season back from Tommy John surgery. He pitched in 15 games (13 of them starts) and tossed 70 1/3 innings with a 5.12 ERA, 22.7% strikeout rate, 10% walk rate and 37.8% ground-ball rate.

articles.title: Twins Promote Jonas Lovin To Assistant Pitching Coach
body: Twins general manager Jeremy Zoll told reporters this week that Jonas Lovin was promoted to the big-league staff. He’ll serve as an assistant to new pitching coach Brian Reith. Lovin has been a minor league pitching coach in Minnesota’s system for the past three seasons.

The Twins moved on from pitching coach Pete Maki and assistant Luis Ramirez at the end of this past season. Reith was hired last month, and the club was expected to find a Ramirez replacement to work with him. Bullpen coach LaTroy Hawkins remains on the staff.

“Jonas has made a huge impact on our minor-league pitching programs and development of our young pitching prospects,” Zoll told reporters, including Dan Hayes of The Athletic. “He has fantastic relationships with our young pitchers and complements Brian and LaTroy’s skill sets in ways that allow us to build a pitching coach group that will be able to serve all of our players’ individual needs on a daily basis.”

Lovin made the jump from the college to the pro coaching ranks in 2023. He spent two years as a pitching coach with High-A Cedar Rapids. Lovin was bumped to Triple-A in 2025. He had more of a roving position this past season as minor league assistant pitching coordinator.

articles.title: Mariners Notes: Infield Needs, Trade Candidates, Sloan
body: The Mariners are in the market for a boost on the left side of the infield. The flexibility of infielder Colt Emerson means the addition could be a shortstop or a third baseman, relays Adam Jude of the Seattle Times.

“We really appreciate the fact that Colt is versatile enough to go be our best third baseman on any given day,” president of baseball operations Jerry Dipoto said. “Our resting point right now is that we go into the season and Colt is our shortstop, but we don’t want to limit ourselves or limit our targets in an offseason acquisition to just a third baseman.”

Veteran J.P. Crawford took most of the reps at shortstop this past season, with Emerson and others filling in behind him. Both Crawford and Emerson also saw time at third base, along with trade acquisition Brendan Donovan. As a team, Seattle ranked dead last in OPS at the hot corner. Crawford is a free agent, and the club prefers to use Donovan in a more versatile role instead of installing him as the everyday option at third base.

Per Jude, Dipoto suggested that a trade was the most likely route toward finding an upgrade in the infield. The top exec mentioned that improving the infield defense on the left side was also a priority, which is part of the reason Donovan (-4 Defensive Runs Saved at 3B) is best-suited elsewhere. Emerson was a neutral defender at shortstop and a slight negative at third base.

articles.title: Braves Sign Evan Phillips To Three-Year Deal
body: The Braves have made their first significant splash of the offseason, announcing Thursday that they’ve signed right-hander Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35MM contract. The Apex Baseball client will be paid $11MM in 2027 and 2028 before earning $13MM in 2029.

Phillips, now 32 years old, returns to the organization that originally drafted him in the 17th round back in 2015. He made a brief major league debut with Atlanta in 2018, pitching 6 1/3 innings, before being traded to Baltimore alongside Bruce Zimmermann and Brett Cumberland in the deal that brought Kevin Gausman and Darren O’Day to Atlanta.

Phillips spent three years as a depth arm in the Orioles’ bullpen, shuffling between Triple-A Norfolk and Baltimore a dozen times before being released. The Rays signed Phillips to a minor league deal and gave him all of three innings before designating him for assignment. The Dodgers swooped in at that point, claiming Phillips off waivers, and the rest is history.

From 2022-25, Phillips was an absolute powerhouse in the Los Angeles bullpen. He pitched 184 2/3 regular season innings and logged a minuscule 2.14 ERA with a 29.6% strikeout rate, 6.6% walk rate and 43.3% ground-ball rate. He spent time both as a setup man and closer in that window, compiling 36 holds and 45 saves — converting on 90% of the opportunities he received along the way. Phillips sat 96.2 mph on his heater in that time. His opponents averaged an awful 86.7 mph off the bat with just a 33.5% hard-hit rate in that time. His ERA over that period ranked sixth among 253 qualified relieves.

articles.title: Latest On Jazz Chisholm’s Market
body: Jazz Chisholm Jr. is one of the bigger upside plays in the free agent position player class. He’s coming off a pedestrian.231/.312/.399 slash line but is a year removed from a 30-30 season. Chisholm is one of the top up-the-middle players available, relatively young at age 29, and hits the market unencumbered by the qualifying offer.
