He then spent two seasons with Seattle before going to Arizona for one and a half. The Diamondbacks traded him back to the Mariners ahead of the 2025 deadline. Between the D-backs and pennant-contending Mariners last year, Suárez swatted 49 homers for the second time in his career and slashed.228/.298/.526. Despite a low batting average and on-base percentage, he put up a solidly above-average wRC+ of 125.

articles.title: Emilio Pagán Declines Player Option
body: Reliever Emilio Pagán has declined his $10MM player option with the Reds for 2027, Francys Romero of BeisbolFR reports. Unless he signs a new deal with the Reds by 4 p.m. CT on Nov. 2, the right-hander will head to the open market.

The 35-year-old Pagán, who has pitched for six teams since he debuted with the Mariners in 2017, spent the past three seasons in Cincinnati. He originally joined the club on a two-year, $16MM guarantee in December 2023, but the first season of the contract didn’t go particularly well. Pagán had separate stints on the injured list with triceps and lat issues, and he only delivered 38 innings of 4.50 ERA ball when healthy.

The past two years went far better for Pagán, who took over as the Reds’ closer in 2025. That year, he converted 32 of 38 save opportunities and recorded a stingy 2.88 ERA with quality strikeout and walk rates of 30.0% and 8.1%, respectively, over 68 2/3 frames. He was able to keep runs off the board despite inducing ground balls just 28.7% of the time. Pagán has walked that tightrope throughout his career, having logged a 29.3% ground-ball rate over 549 1/3 innings in the majors.

articles.title: Braves Hire Dana Brown For Scouting Advisor Role
body: The Braves are reuniting with Dana Brown as a senior advisor in their amateur scouting department, as per USA Today’s Bob Nightengale. It’s a homecoming for Brown, who worked as Atlanta’s VP of scouting from 2019-22 before he was hired as the Astros’ general manager.

Brown and Braves president of baseball operations Alex Anthopoulos have a long working relationship dating back to their days in Montreal, when Anthopoulos was Brown’s assistant when Brown was hired as the Expos’ director of amateur scouting in 2002. Brown continued in that role with the Expos/Nationals through the franchise’s move to Washington and until 2009, when Anthopoulos (now the Blue Jays’ GM) hired Brown for a special assistant’s role in Toronto. Once Anthopoulos was hired by the Braves following the 2017 season, Brown reunited with Anthopoulos once more within a couple of years.

The Astros’ hiring of Brown was a rare case of a team making a front office change right after a World Series title, as former GM James Click was let go after the playoff run due to clashes with owner Jim Crane (who is known for playing a direct role in baseball operations). While Brown didn’t capture a championship during his time in Houston, he also had a much better record than most GMs who are shown the door. Houston made the ALCS in 2023 and won two AL West titles in Brown’s three full seasons as GM, and the Astros even ended up winning the division again this year, albeit with an 81-81 record.

articles.title: Two Players Elect Free Agency
body: Two players who saw regular-season action for the two World Series teams have elected minor league agency, according to the official MiLB.com transactions page. To qualify for minor league free agency, players must be outrighted off their teams’ 40-man rosters during the course of the season without being added back, and they must have either three years of MLB service time or multiple outright assignments over the course of their careers.

Dunn signed a minor league deal with the White Sox last winter, and was traded to the Rays in May. He was quickly added to the active roster as infield depth when Ben Williamson was placed on the IL, and Dunn had a.258 OPS in 12 plate appearances over nine games, appearing mostly as a late-game substitute. Tampa optioned Dunn back to Triple-A after that nine-game stint, and outrighted him off the 40-man in September.

Dunn has now played in parts of the last three MLB seasons, and has hit.197/.253/.275 over 157 PA in the Show with the Brewers and Rays. He can play all over the infield (and has played left field in the minors) and has some good base-stealing ability, so Dunn will try to parlay that skillset into another minor league contract this offseason. Dunn is out of minor league options, which will complicate his chances of sticking on a 40-man roster.

They haven’t had a winning record since 2015. Despite that long run of poor results, they have resisted rebuilding and prioritized short-term contention.

articles.title: Luis Severino To Exercise Player Option, Remain With A’s
body: Athletics right-hander Luis Severino will exercise his $22MM player option and forgo a return to the open market, as first reported by Mike Rodriguez of Rompiendo Sports. Severino will remain with the A’s in their final season in Sacramento before becoming a free agent in the 2027-28 offseason.

Although Severino previously expressed dissatisfaction with the facilities at Sutter Health Park, it’s no surprise that the veteran will stick around for the third and final year of his contract. Severino posted a 4.16 ERA over 12 starts and 62 2/3 innings before going on the 15-day injured list at the end of May with a strain of his shoulder capsule and subscapularis muscle. The injury proved to be season-ending, as Severino was able to resume throwing but didn’t get deep enough into his recovery process to even begin a minor league rehab assignment.

Between this shortened season and his so-so performance in 2025, Severino wouldn’t have made anywhere close to $22MM in free agency. Opting out of his deal also would’ve meant hitting the open market in offseason that is bound to be interrupted by a lockout, so it makes plenty of sense for Severino to take his guaranteed payday and focus entirely on returning to the mound in 2027 (Severino’s age-33 season).

articles.title: Astros Hire Randy Flores As General Manager
body: The Astros have hired Cardinals assistant GM/scouting director Randy Flores as their new general manager. The team announced the move on Friday evening.

“Randy has had a huge impact on the Cardinals over the last 10 seasons,” Houston owner Jim Crane said in the press release. “Throughout the entire interview process, we’ve been thoroughly impressed with Randy and with his background in scouting and player acquisition. We’re happy to welcome Randy and his family to the Astros and we can’t wait to get to work on bringing another championship to Houston.” Flores and Crane will meet with the media during an introductory press conference on Monday morning.

It’s a surprise turn of events. The Athletic reported on Thursday that Brewers assistant GM Matt Kleine had emerged as the frontrunner for the position. Chandler Rome of The Athletic reports that Houston offered the GM job to Kleine on Wednesday evening, hours before Milwaukee won its first World Series.

Although it’s unclear precisely what changed, The Athletic suggests that Kleine had been seeking the title ‘president of baseball operations’ earlier in the week. They write that the Milwaukee AGM never pulled his name out of the running, though it’s possible there was some kind of hangup in negotiations on title and/or salary.

articles.title: Clint Hurdle, Rockies Parting Ways
body: Clint Hurdle and the Rockies are parting ways, the baseball lifer announced on social media (link via Thomas Harding of MLB.com). Hurdle has been in the organization for the past five seasons, mostly in a special assistant role.

The 69-year-old Hurdle is better known for his first stint with the club. After playing parts of 10 seasons in the big leagues, he went into minor league managing in the late 1980s. Hurdle began coaching in the Colorado farm system in 1994, then worked his way onto the MLB staff as hitting coach. He was promoted to manager in 2002 and led the club for eight seasons, including their trip to the World Series in’07. The Rockies fired him in May’09 after a rough start to that season.

Hurdle spent a season as hitting coach in Texas before returning to the managerial ranks. He took the lead job with the Pirates in 2011. Hurdle led the club to three straight playoff appearances from 2013-15 (still the franchise’s only postseason berths since the Barry Bonds era) and won NL Manager of the Year honors in 2013. He managed parts of nine seasons with the Bucs but was fired at the tail end of the’19 campaign.

After a couple seasons out of baseball, Hurdle returned to Colorado in the special assistant capacity. He moved back onto the coaching staff in 2025, taking over as interim hitting coach and then interim bench coach when the Rox made various changes amidst a 119-loss season. He returned to the special assistant role for the’26 season, the first year under the new front office team of Paul DePodesta and Josh Byrnes.

articles.title: Michael Soroka Declines Mutual Option With D-Backs
body: Michael Soroka has officially declined his end of a $10MM mutual option with the Diamondbacks, reports Nick Piecoro of The Arizona Republic. He’ll be paid a $1MM buyout and return to free agency.

This was inevitable, as Soroka has put himself in position to do pretty well financially. The Diamondbacks picked him up on a $7.5MM deal last offseason. (He earned an additional $1.35MM in performance bonuses by starting 20 games.) He was initially slated to open the season in a swing role, but an Opening Day injured list stint for Merrill Kelly drew him into the starting five.

Soroka was one of Torey Lovullo’s more reliable starters and held a rotation spot all season. He pitched to a 3.41 earned run average across 116 innings. He led Arizona starters with a 24.1% strikeout rate while limiting his free passes to a 6% clip. Soroka tailed off a bit in the second half as he navigated injured list stints for a left glute strain and arm inflammation, yet it was mid-rotation production on a rate basis. This was also his highest workload since 2019.

The innings questions are going to keep Soroka from commanding a massive contract, but he’s very likely to secure a multi-year deal. He’s entering his age-29 season and has one of the better strikeout and walk profiles of the group of mid-tier free agent starters. Soroka has a chance at three years, with a two-year pact in the $10-12MM range feeling like a floor.

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: Tampa Bay Rays
body: The Rays posted the best record in the American League this season (98-64) and cemented their status as the Junior Circuit’s top team by toppling the Yankees and Guardians en route to the American League pennant. Tampa Bay ran into a Brewers buzzsaw in the World Series, however, falling four games to one to a dominant Milwaukee pitching staff. The Rays now face critical offseason decisions on some of their top players as they look to retool around an impressive young core and gear up for what they hope will be another deep October run in 2027.

articles.title: Angels Select Nicolò Pinazzi
body: The Angels announced that they have selected the contract of left-hander Nicolò Pinazzi. They also announced they have turned down a club option on righty Robert Stephenson, a move that was covered earlier today. Meanwhile, right-hander Jack Kochanowicz was reinstated from the 60-day injured list in a procedural move. He is recovering from Tommy John surgery and will be out until the second half of 2027, so he’ll go back on the 60-day IL once it becomes available again after the offseason.

Pinazzi, 27, hasn’t taken the typical path to a roster spot with the Angels. Born in Italy, he was signed by the Reds back in 2020. He was with that club through 2023 but was released before the beginning of the 2024 season. He spent a couple of seasons pitching in indy ball and then signed with the Halos for the 2026 campaign.

His numbers this year have been outstanding. Across four different levels, he tossed 64 innings over 48 appearances, allowing 0.84 earned runs per nine. His 12.5% walk rate is certainly high but he struck out 38.9% of batters faced and induced grounders on 60.8% of balls in play, those latter two both being excellent figures.

Brendan Gawlowski of FanGraphs profiled Pinazzi back in August. The lefty’s fastball sits in the mid-90s but he throws his breaking ball more than half the time. Pinazzi calls this pitch a cutter but admits the label is wrong. “I say cutter, but it’s definitely a slider,” he said. “I say cutter to delude myself, I throw more strikes that way.” Gawlowski notes that Pinazzi also mixes in a curveball but this cutter/slider is the money pitch.

articles.title: Guardians Select Milan Tolentino
body: The Guardians announced that they have selected the contract of infielder Milan Tolentino. They also declined a club option on right-hander Trevor Stephan as well as their end of a mutual option with righty Shawn Armstrong.

Tolentino, 25 next month, was a fourth-round pick in the 2020 draft. The fact that the Guardians are adding him to the roster now suggests he was about to qualify for minor league free agency. By giving him a roster spot, they prevent him from getting away.

He has never really been a top prospect in the system but he clearly has some tools. He has spent the past two years at the Triple-A level. He has stepped to the plate 957 times in that span, hitting 42 home runs and drawing walks at a strong 12.5% clip. The flipside is that he has also struck out as a massive 32.9% pace. That has led to a lopsided.221/.321/.445 batting line and 100 wRC+, indicating his offense works out to league average on the whole.

Defensively, Tolentino has spent most of his time at shortstop while also getting lots of action at second and third base. He very briefly dabbled in the outfield this year. The Guards have Travis Bazzana at second and José Ramírez at third. Shortstop could be covered by either Brayan Rocchio or Ángel Genao. Daniel Schneemann is on the roster and could be in a bench/utility role.

Tolentino will try to push into that mix but he has a full slate of options and could be in line for more time at Triple-A. He already has a couple of seasons at that level but it wouldn’t hurt to get some more seasoning in an attempt to cut down on the punchouts.

articles.title: Diamondbacks To Hire Ben Fritz As Pitching Coach
body: The Diamondbacks have a new pitching coach. Dennis Lin of The Athletic reports that Arizona has snaked Ben Fritz away from the Padres. He has been working as the bullpen coach in San Diego. The Snakes parted ways with pitching coach Brian Kaplan earlier this month.

Fritz, 45, was a first-round pick of the Athletics back in 2002. He pitched in the minors through 2008 but never made it to the big leagues. He kept pitching in indy ball through 2010. The Padres gave him a minor league coaching job in 2015. He got the bullpen coach job at the big league level ahead of the 2020 season. He was briefly the pitching coach in 2021. Larry Rothschild was fired from that job in August of that year. Fritz held the job the rest of the way and then Ruben Niebla was hired in October.

For what it’s worth, the Padres have had good results in the pitching department in recent years. From 2020 to 2026, San Diego pitchers posted a collective 3.86 earned run average, behind just six other clubs. The Diamondbacks had a 4.55 ERA in that same time frame, better than just three teams.

It’s always tough to determine how much credit or blame to give to an individual coach, since he can only work with the players on the roster and is also just one member of a larger staff. But it seems Fritz has a good reputation in the league. He reportedly drew some interest from other clubs last year. Lin’s report from today notes that the Rockies were interested in him for their pitching coach vacancy but the Diamondbacks have managed to bring him aboard.

articles.title: Athletics Decline Club Options On Jeffrey Springs, Jeff McNeil
body: The Athletics announced that they have declined club options on left-hander Jeffrey Springs and infielder/outfielder Jeff McNeil. Both players are now free agents.

Neither decision is too shocking. Both players are 34 years old and coming off disappointing seasons. The A’s acquired Springs from the Rays in December of 2024. At the time, their rotation was mostly young and inexperienced. The A’s signed Luis Severino and acquired Springs in the hopes of providing some veteran stability.

Springs was fine enough in his first season with the A’s. He logged 171 innings and posted a 4.11 earned run average. Considering that the club was playing in a hitter-friendly minor league park, that wasn’t too bad. His 19.4% strikeout rate was subpar but his 7.6% walk rate was good. He got a bit of help from a low.255 batting average on balls in play.

Just about everything went in the wrong direction in 2026. His BABIP ticked up closer to average, landing at.278. His strikeout rate dropped to 17.8% and his walk rate climbed to 9%. The dimensions at Sutter Health Park became a problem. He allowed 35 home runs on the year, 23 of those at home. The 35 number was seven more than the previous season despite pitching almost 30 fewer innings. The end result was a 6.18 ERA.

articles.title: Angels Decline Club Option On Robert Stephenson
body: The MLBPA announced that Robert Stephenson is now a free agent, indicating that the Angels declined their $2.5MM club option on his services for 2027. Stephenson’s tenure in Los Angeles will now end with only 10 innings pitched over three seasons.

A trade from the Pirates to the Rays in June 2023 suddenly turned Stephenson in a dominant bullpen weapon, as he posted a 2.35 ERA, 5.7% walk rate, and a stunning 42.9% strikeout rate over 38 1/3 innings in a Tampa Bay uniform. Though his overall numbers over eight MLB seasons had been much less consistent, the Angels believed that Stephenson’s breakout was legit, and he was signed to a three-year, $33MM free agent deal in January 2024.

Unfortunately for Stephenson and the Halos, he barely got a chance to prove himself on the mound. He missed all of 2024 and some of 2025 recovering from Tommy John surgery, and also battled biceps and elbow inflammation that limited him to just the 10 frames in 2025. More elbow problems emerged last spring, and Stephenson underwent a ligament and flexor repair procedure in April that kept him on the shelf for all of 2026.

The TJ procedure unlocked a clause in Stephenson’s contract that gave the Angels this extra club option year for 2027. Though $2.5MM isn’t a large sum, the team might have further concerns about Stephenson’s health, or the Angels just want to move on entirely from this failed signing. Former GM Perry Minasian signed Stephenson under the approval of owner Arte Moreno, though Minasian was fired last season and Moreno has now sold the team to Stan Kroenke’s ownership group.

articles.title: Diamondbacks Seeking Controllable Starting Pitching
body: After deciding whether or not to trade Ketel Marte, a secondary item on the Diamondbacks’ to-do list will be adding to the rotation. General manager Mike Hazen tells Nick Piecoro of The Arizona Republic that he would like to acquire a controllable starter. That is more likely to happen via trade, as Hazen is unlikely to push hard for a starter in free agency given the team is planning to reduce payroll.

The D-backs had a middling 4.28 ERA out of their rotation this year. The group’s 9.6% K-BB rate bested only the lowly Rockies, as Arizona’s starters showed good control but struggled to strike opponents out. Eduardo Rodriguez was better than expected. He posted a 2.89 ERA over 32 starts despite middling peripherals and led the staff with 3.2 fWAR. Michael Soroka and Brandon Pfaadt were the next best performers after him. Both had ERAs below 3.40, with Soroka riding an above-average 24.1% strikeout rate and Pfaadt relying on ground balls and control.

The trouble is that Soroka will become a free agent once he declines his end of a $10MM mutual option. Both sides have expressed interest in a reunion, though it remains unclear how far Arizona will go to retain Soroka while also addressing the rest of their roster. The bullpen, first base, and left-handed hitting all need to be addressed, as MLBTR’s Anthony Franco wrote in our Offseason Outlook series.

articles.title: Marlins Exercise Club Option On Sandy Alcantara
body: One of the most straightforward option decisions for any team this offseason is now official. The Marlins announced Friday that they’ve exercised their $21MM club option on right-hander Sandy Alcantara. It’s a net $19MM decision, as the Marlins would have owed Alcantara a $2MM buyout even if they’d preferred to move on and let the face of their franchise test free agency. The 2027 campaign will be the last year he’s under contract. He’s slated to become a free agent next winter.

There was never a doubt that this option would be picked up. Alcantara had a strong rebound in his second season back from Tommy John surgery. Major League Baseball’s consummate workhorse tossed 214 innings — tops in either league — and notched a 3.87 earned run average. Alcantara’s 17.1% strikeout rate was well below average, but his 6.6% walk rate was strong and his 41.9% ground-ball rate was about average.

Because of the Marlins’ perennially small payroll and frequent rebuilds, Alcantara’s name has come up in trade chatter at seemingly every turn over the years. That’s far less likely to be the case this winter, even as he heads into his final year of contractual control.

The Marlins reportedly have no interest in trading Alcantara and have every intent of keeping him and starting him on Opening Day once again next season. President of baseball operations Peter Bendix has spoken of Alcantara’s importance to the club on multiple occasions, and he’s unsurprisingly said to be a personal favorite of owner Bruce Sherman.

articles.title: Marlins Outright Five Players
body: The Marlins’ offseason housekeeping has begun. Miami has outrighted five players off the 40-man roster, according to the team’s transaction log at MLB.com. Catchers Logan Driscoll and Brian Navarreto and righties Tyler Zuber, Wikelman González and Zach Brzykcy have all cleared waivers. They’re all likely headed to minor league free agency.

The two catchers saw little to no big league time this year. Driscoll, 29 next week, didn’t appear in the majors. The Marlins added him in a cash swap with Tampa Bay just prior to the deadline. He was a depth option with the Rays and remained in that role with Miami. Driscoll raked in 14 Triple-A games for the Fish but was below-average the rest of the season with the Rays’ top affiliate. Overall, he hit.269/.367/.422 in 77 games at the Triple-A level. His only big league work to date was a 15-game cup of coffee with the 2024 Rays, wherein he batted.171/.189/.257 with a homer in 37 plate appearances.

Navarreto, 32 in December, totaled 61 plate appearances with Miami this year. He hit just.135/.193/.250 with a homer. Navarreto was originally a sixth-round pick by the Twins in 2013. He’s split his entire career between the Minnesota and Miami organizations, appearing in parts of three seasons with the latter. He’s a well below-average hitter even in Triple-A, but Navarreto is a strong defender and seasoned minor league vet who could be re-signed to give the Fish some glove-first depth to keep at their top minor league affiliate.

articles.title: Diamondbacks Expected To Field Interest On Ketel Marte
body: The Diamondbacks’ biggest offseason question is whether they’ll line up a Ketel Marte trade. Arizona fielded interest in the star second baseman early last offseason, though it seemed mostly a matter of due diligence as they explored ways to add controllable starting pitching.

There’s a good chance the team will more aggressively shop Marte this offseason — albeit with various reasons why it may be more difficult to actually make a deal. Most notably, Marte can veto any trade after securing 10-and-5 rights (10 years of service time, the last five with one club) in April.

Reports from both John Gambadoro/Alex Weiner of Arizona Sports and Nick Piecoro of The Arizona Republic indicate that the Snakes will explore Marte trades yet again. Piecoro writes that they’ve received preliminary interest from other clubs, though it’s obviously very early in the process with the trade market just reopening this morning.

Marte features prominently on MLBTR’s list of the game’s top offseason trade candidates, slotting in at #6. That’s driven in large part by comments from team officials who’ve become increasingly frustrated with Marte no-showing for certain games over the years.

articles.title: Red Sox To Trade Tsung-Che Cheng To Tigers
body: The Red Sox are trading infielder Tsung-Che Cheng to the Tigers for cash, reports Andrew Parker of Sox Prospects. He’ll occupy a spot on Detroit’s 40-man roster, which is up to either 42 or 44 depending on their option decisions for Drew Anderson and Kenley Jansen.

Boston, which already cleared one spot by trading Nate Eaton to the Athletics this afternoon, will be at 42 once Sonny Gray declines his end of a mutual option and becomes a free agent. Both teams will need to drop down to 40 by Monday evening.

Cheng spent one season on the Sox’ roster. Boston claimed him off waivers from the Nationals in February. The Taiwanese infielder made a three-game debut with the Pirates last year and bounced around the waiver wire over the 2025-26 offseason. He played a minimal role in Boston, starting 13 games at shortstop amidst a monthlong stint on the MLB roster. He hit.256 with one extra-base hit, a double, in 44 plate appearances.

The 25-year-old Cheng spent the remainder of the season on optional assignment to Triple-A Worcester. He posted a league average.241/.345/.390 slash with eight home runs. Cheng rarely expanded the strike zone and walked at a strong 14% clip. He struck out at a slightly elevated 24% rate and didn’t hit the ball with much authority. Prospect evaluators have generally praised his plate discipline and solid defensive chops around the infield, projecting him as a utility piece. He’s out of minor league options and will battle for a bench job in Detroit if he holds his 40-man spot all offseason.

articles.title: Braves Exercise Options On Ronald Acuña Jr., Ozzie Albies
body: The Braves announced they’ve picked up their options on Ronald Acuña Jr. and Ozzie Albies. Acuña will make $17MM next season, while Albies will match this year’s $7MM salary. Those were Atlanta’s only option decisions this year.

There wasn’t much suspense with either decision. The Braves weren’t going to cut either member of their core for what would’ve amounted to $7MM in savings. Acuña’s option came with a $10MM buyout that meant he’d only have been bought out had he suffered some kind of career-altering injury. Albies’ deal didn’t have a buyout but comes with a base salary akin to what solid utility infielders (e.g. Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Willi Castro) make as free agents.

The Braves have Acuña until team control for two seasons, as there’s another $17MM option on his deal for the 2028 campaign. That one doesn’t have a buyout, so it’d be a costlier decision, but it’s still highly likely to be exercised. Acuña hit 20 homers with a.255/.345/.451 slash line in a relative down year. He’s one season removed from a monster.290/.417/.518 showing after coming back from the second ACL tear of his career.

This will be the final season of the $35MM extension that Albies signed early in his career. Atlanta has tacked on $10MM by picking up two club options along the way — a $4MM buyout on his first option was already factored into that $35MM guarantee — so he made a total of $45MM over a nine-year stretch. Albies handily outperformed those salaries, though he’s been more serviceable than great going back to the start of the 2024 season.

articles.title: Athletics Outright Six Players
body: The Athletics announced that six players have been sent outright to Triple-A Las Vegas, indicating that they recently cleared waivers. They are right-handers Henry Baez, Joey Estes and Geoff Hartlieb, catcher Brian Serven, infielder Michael Stefanic and outfielder Johnathan Rodríguez.

As the offseason begins, many teams are facing roster crunches. Free agency begins today for eligible players, which opens some breathing room. But the injured list goes away five days after the World Series ends. Coming into today, RosterResource projected the A’s for a count of 46 for the offseason. Then they acquired Nate Eaton in a trade with the Red Sox. These six moves get the club down to 41.

Estes, 25, is one of the more experienced players in the group. He gave the A’s 127 2/3 innings back in 2024 with a 5.01 earned run average. Since then, he has mostly been kept in the minors as a depth arm, only making five big league appearances over the past two seasons. His Triple-A ERA was north of 5.50 in both of those campaigns. He exhausted his final option season and will be out of options going forward. He has at least seven years in the minors, meaning he’ll qualify for minor league free agency in the coming days.

articles.title: Royals Exercise Club Option On Tony Gonsolin, Decline Carlos Estévez
body: The Royals announced that they have exercised a 2027 club option on right-hander Tony Gonsolin. He will make $2.5MM next year. Right-hander Carlos Estévez has had his $13MM club option turned down. He becomes a free agent and collects a $2MM buyout.

Gonsolin is a relatively low-cost wild card for next year’s staff. From 2019 to 2023, he tossed 375 2/3 innings for the Dodgers, allowing 3.19 earned runs per nine. He had a 23.1% strikeout rate, 8.7% walk rate and 38.8% ground ball rate.

He hasn’t been much of a factor since then. He required Tommy John surgery in August of 2023, wiping out the end of that season and his 2024 campaign. In 2025, he suffered a back injury while lifting weights. He began the season on the injured list. He came off the IL in April, made seven starts with an ERA of 5.00, then returned to the IL with elbow discomfort. He would eventually require internal brace surgery in August.

He was bumped from the Dodgers roster after the season. He was still recovering from his surgery when the 2026 campaign began. He didn’t sign until August. The Royals gave him a prorated $1MM salary and a $2.5MM club option for 2027. He made four minor league rehab appearances before joining the big league club. He made one appearance in the majors, allowing five earned runs in 2 2/3 innings, before an allergic reaction put him back on the IL in late September.

articles.title: Corbin Burnes Will Not Opt Out Of Diamondbacks Deal
body: Right-hander Corbin Burnes will not take the opt-out chance in his contract with the Diamondbacks, reports Bob Nightengale of USA Today. He will make $35MM annually through the 2030 season, though $11MM is deferred annually.

There wasn’t any suspense with this decision. Burnes and the Snakes agreed to a six-year, $210MM deal in December of 2024. His agent Scott Boras would later suggest that he turned down larger offers from other clubs because his family has a home in Scottsdale.

The first two years of the agreement have mostly been wasted. Burnes made 11 starts in 2025 before requiring Tommy John surgery. He was hoping to make it back around the 2026 All-Star break but suffered a teres major strain in June, delaying his timeline. He came off the injured list in September but made just three starts, with a 7.84 earned run average, before shoulder inflammation put him back on the shelf.

Burnes is very talented and has a Cy Young trophy on his mantel but it would have been unwise to turn down $140MM with that kind of platform. The family/geography considerations made it even less likely.

He will return to the Arizona rotation in 2027 and hope for better results going forward. It’s possible he may face workload restrictions after missing most of the past two years. Time will tell on that. On paper, he’s in the rotation next to Eduardo Rodríguez, Brandon Pfaadt, Merrill Kelly and Ryne Nelson. The Snakes and Michael Soroka have mutual interest in a reunion. Even if Soroka doesn’t come back, they will likely bring in someone else to bolster the group.

articles.title: Athletics Acquire Nate Eaton From Red Sox
body: The offseason trading has begun. The Athletics have acquired outfielder Nate Eaton from the Red Sox in exchange for minor league right-hander Jareth Rayo. Bob Nightengale of USA Today first reported that Eaton was traded to the A’s. Chris Cotillo of MassLive first reported the Sox would get a minor leaguer in return. Francys Romero of BeisbolFR first identified Rayo.

Eaton, 30 in December, was on the roster bubble in Boston. He served an up-and-down depth role this year, getting shuttled between Triple-A and the majors. He hit just.160/.300/.260 in the big leagues and exhausted his final option season. It was going to be hard for him to a hold a spot on the 40-man through the offseason.

Most teams are facing a crunch in the coming days. The injured list goes away on Monday, meaning several players on the 60-day IL will need to retake roster spots. Prior to this deal, RosterResource projected the Sox for a 40-man count of 44, factoring in players coming off the IL and those bound for free agency. They still have to open three spots but moving Eaton starts the process of alleviating the logjam.

It is perhaps not a coincidence that the A’s have a new front office leader who just departed Boston. General manager David Forst was dismissed in August. In October, the club hired Taylor Smith as president of baseball operations. Smith had previously been an assistant general manager with the Red Sox and should be familiar with Eaton.

articles.title: Diamondbacks Considering First Base Work For Nolan Arenado
body: The Diamondbacks and third baseman Nolan Arenado are thinking about him playing first base next year, reports Steve Gilbert of MLB.com. This wouldn’t be about moving Arenado off the hot corner, but the extra versatility could help the club’s offseason pursuits while also keeping him healthier.

Arenado just wrapped up his age-35 season and he will turn 36 in April. His third base defense is no longer at the elite levels of earlier in his career but remains passable, depending on your metric of choice. Defensive Runs Saved was the most bearish on his 2026 work, giving him a grade of minus-four. On the other end of the spectrum, Outs Above Average and Fielding Run Value had him in positive territory, with both of those metrics giving Arenado a grade of two above par.

Though he has never played any other position, it’s understandable that the Diamondbacks would want to contemplate making him viable at first. First base is generally considered a less taxing position than third base, something the Snakes are thinking about as Arenado is squarely in his mid-30s. “I think it’s taken a toll on him physically a little bit,” general manager Mike Hazen said. “So we’re trying to be mindful of that.”

articles.title: The Braves’ Other Middle Infield Question
body: The Braves have the most glaring shortstop need in MLB. Mauricio Dubón and Ha-Seong Kim are impending free agents, leaving Jim Jarvis as the top in-house option. There’s a decent chance they’ll re-sign Dubón on a two-year deal, but he’s ideally suited as a super-utility player.

If the Astros make Jeremy Peña available before his year of club control, the Braves should be heavily involved. They’ll also surely look into younger shortstops who might be expendable on their current team (e.g. Anthony Volpe, Brayan Rocchio). The focus on shortstop has potentially overshadowed that the Braves’ other middle infield position might also need a shakeup.

Ozzie Albies has started 1117 games at the keystone for the Braves over the past nine seasons. No one else has started more than 44. Albies has been a steady, durable lineup fixture for years. He has handily outperformed the $35MM contract extension he signed in April 2019 and was a legitimate star through the’23 campaign.

articles.title: Pirates Notes: Keller, Valdez, Buchanan
body: Mitch Keller’s season ended the day before the trade deadline, when the Pirates placed him on the 60-day injured list due to a teres major strain in his right shoulder. The team didn’t provide major specifics at the time, but Aiden Stepansky of MLB.com writes that Keller is believed to have suffered a Grade 3 strain — a gruesome injury that saw his teres major muscle detach from the bone.

Keller somewhat remarkably didn’t require surgery. Doctors recommended a lengthy down period and rehab. The plan has been for him to resume throwing late this month, and he’s expected to have a normal offseason.

The injury didn’t occur on one specific pitch, it seems. Keller told Stepansky he couldn’t pinpoint the exact moment at which it occurred. That suggests he was pitching through discomfort for some time, and the results bear that out. The typically steady Keller was dinged for a 5.29 ERA in 22 starts. His 17.7% strikeout rate was a career-worst, and his 8.3% walk rate — while still solid — was his highest since 2022. He posted a sub-7% mark each year from 2023-25. Keller’s 93.3 mph average fastball was also a career-low mark. He sat at a season-low 91.9 mph in his final start before hitting the injured list.

articles.title: Tigers Re-Sign Carlos Perez To Minor League Deal
body: Veteran catcher Carlos Perez is headed back to the Tigers on a minor league deal, as relayed in a transactions update from Matt Eddy at Baseball America. Perez split the 2026 campaign between the Tigers’ and Astros’ Triple-A affiliates.

Perez, who turned 36 yesterday, has been in four different organizations over the past three seasons. He hasn’t received a big-league call at any of those stops. Houston signed him last offseason as a depth option behind Yainer Diaz and Christian Vazquez. Diaz missed time with an oblique strain over the summer, but it was César Salazar who got the call to replace him.

Houston released Perez in mid-June. After a brief stint in the Mexican League, he signed with the Tigers. Perez got off to a blazing start with Triple-A Toledo, hitting.351 with seven homers in his first 12 games. An ankle injury in early August cut his season short. It was only a 69-game sample, but Perez did finish with a 108 wRC+ and 15 homers in the minors this year.

Perez will reprise his role with the Mud Hens in 2027. He hasn’t reached the majors since 2023 with the Athletics. His 68 games with the club that season marked his first big-league opportunity since 2018. Perez has a.592 OPS across 859 MLB plate appearances. He was a plus behind the plate early in his career, but had a poor defensive season with the A’s.

articles.title: Latest On Cardinals’ Outfield Plans
body: The Cardinals are entering their second full season under president of baseball operations Chaim Bloom. St. Louis kicked off a retool once Bloom took over last winter and remained committed to that plan at the deadline despite hovering around the Wild Card picture.

St. Louis seems likely to take a similar approach next year as they remain focused on a long-term goal of building the starting pitching pipeline. The JJ Wetherholt extension is their only contract on the books, however, giving them plenty of short-term payroll capacity if they want to look outside the organization. They’ll surely bring in some help on the pitching staff and are open to a move at third base, where a group led by Nolan Gorman and Blaze Jordan was unproductive.

The rest of the Cardinals’ infield played well. They’re well positioned at catcher, designated hitter, and in right field. St. Louis ranked in the bottom third of the league in production from their left and center fielders. Those join third base as the biggest question marks in the Cardinals’ lineup, though it seems they’re less inclined to prioritize external outfield help.

articles.title: Dodgers Notes: Sasaki, Davalan
body: Dodgers right-hander Roki Sasaki made some progress in 2026 but wants to keep pushing next year. Per Dylan Hernandez of The New York Post, he wants to continue working as a starter and find enough success to be part of a playoff rotation. “In the playoffs, I think the team winning is prioritized more than anything,” Sasaki said. “I think that if I pitch well in the regular season, I should be able to throw (in the postseason). If I can’t do that, I think it would just mean I’m not good enough.”

Sasaki is two years into his big league career now. In both seasons, he was in the rotation mix during the regular season but got pushed into a bullpen role in the postseason. In both campaigns, his earned run average was a bit underwhelming, going from 4.46 last year to 4.49 in 2026. But the details around the ERA were more encouraging in 2026.

For one thing, the workload was far greater. A shoulder impingement put him on the injured list for most of 2025, limiting him to just 36 1/3 innings in the majors. In that time, his 17.4% strikeout rate, 13.7% walk rate and 38.9% ground ball rate were all worse than league average. In 2026, he did miss some time with a blister but cranked his innings tally up to 122 1/3. His 23.6% strikeout rate, 9.2% walk rate and 42.2% ground ball rate were all around average.

He also seemed to get better as the season went along. In the second half, he posted a 2.83 ERA in 41 1/3 innings, with a 25.3% strikeout rate and 8.8% walk rate. The challenge will be in putting up numbers like that consistently and over a full season.

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: Athletics
body: The A’s went from 76 wins in 2025 to a 64-98 record this year, as a swath of injuries and continued poor pitching threw a wrench into the rebuilding efforts. New president of baseball operations Taylor Smith is now tasked with getting the A’s back on track in their final year in Sacramento.

Tyler Soderstrom, LF: $84MM through 2032 (includes $2MM buyout of $27MM club option for 2033) Jacob Wilson, SS: $66MM through 2032 (includes $2MM buyout of $26MM club option for 2033) Lawrence Butler, OF: $58MM through 2031 (includes $4MM buyout of $20MM club option for 2032) Brent Rooker, OF/DH: $42MM through 2029 ($22MM club/vesting option for 2030) Luis Severino, SP: $22MM player option for 2027 Option Decisions

Luis Severino, SP: $22MM player option for 2027 Jeff McNeil, 2B/1B/OF: $15.75MM club option for 2027 ($2MM buyout, to be covered by the Mets) Jeffrey Springs, SP: $15MM club option for 2027 ($750K buyout) 2027 guarantees (assuming Severino stays, and McNeil/Springs are declined): $47.5MM Total future commitments (assuming Severino stays, and McNeil/Springs are declined): $272MM

Shea Langeliers (4.051): $8.7MM Luis Medina (3.146): $1.4MM Zack Gelof (3.050): $2.9MM Hogan Harris (2.146): $2.3MM Non-tender candidates: None Free Agents

articles.title: Joe Espada, Jason Kanzler Reportedly Finalists For Mariners Managerial Job
body: The Mariners’ managerial search may be coming to an end. Adam Jude and Ryan Divish of The Seattle Times report that former Astros skipper Joe Espada and Cubs director of player development Jason Kanzler are the finalists. Those two will have in-person interviews Tuesday and Wednesday. The report mentioned the possibility of the Mariners reaching out to coaches from the Rays or Brewers after the World Series is done but the Mariners are planning to name a new manager by the end of the week.

Both Espada and Kanzler have been connected to the job opening in previous reports but there were plenty of others in the mix and it now appears it is down to these two. The Times says there were 30 to 40 names on the initial search list and the club had conversations with many candidates. Rocco Baldelli was identified as one of them but he withdrew his name recently. Daniel Kramer of MLB.com reports that was likely due to geography, as Baldelli and his family live in Florida.

Kramer also reports that White Sox bench coach Walker McKinven and Rays senior advisor Brandon Hyde were also in the mix but no longer in the running. His report, which was published yesterday, noted that Espada and Kanzler would be getting in-person meetings but wasn’t clear if those two were considered finalists. Today’s reporting from The Times has many of the same details but goes a bit farther in framing Espada and Kanzler as finalists.

articles.title: A’s Max Muncy Undergoes Knee Debridement
body: The Athletics announced that infielder Max Muncy underwent a debridement surgery to address cartilage damage in his left knee. He also received a platelet-rich plasma injection. Muncy is expected to be fully ready for the start of camp.

Muncy finished the season on the injured list, missing the final week with the cartilage issue. It evidently required a minor procedure but shouldn’t have much impact on his offseason. Muncy is entering what could be a make or break season. He’s down to one minor league option year remaining and will need to impress a front office led by newly-hired president of baseball operations Taylor Smith, who doesn’t have the same attachment to Muncy as did former GM David Forst.

A first-round pick in 2021, Muncy has yet to establish himself in parts of two big league campaigns. He hit.214/.259/.379 as a rookie last year. Muncy’s numbers improved marginally in his sophomore season, as he batted.230/.296/.387 with nine homers across 284 plate appearances. He struck out at a concerning 32% clip while walking less than 8% of the time. Muncy has above-average bat speed but has yet to dial in a consistent enough approach against big league pitching. Twelve of his 18 career home runs have come against fastballs, and he’s struggled to make contact against any kind of secondary stuff.

articles.title: Royals Release Jorge Alfaro
body: Veteran catcher Jorge Alfaro was released by the Royals, per his MILB.com transaction tracker. Alfaro spent the 2026 season in the minors with Kansas City. He’ll head to free agency in search of another opportunity.

The 33-year-old Alfaro joined the organization on a minor league deal in December. He received an invitation to MLB Spring Training, but did not appear in a game. Alfaro was with Team Colombia in the World Baseball Classic, which was going on during spring action.

The Royals entered the year with a solid catching tandem in Salvador Perez and Carter Jensen. They cycled through veterans Elias Diaz and Luke Maile during the season with Perez banged up. Alfaro never got a look in the majors.

Alfaro slashed.223/.287/.468 in 62 games between Kansas City’s Double-A and Triple-A affiliates. He popped 15 homers and also stole a base. While the power production is impressive, Alfaro also struck out at a massive 41.5% clip.

Strikeouts have held Alfaro back for much of his career. He’s appeared in parts of nine MLB seasons with six different teams. Alfaro has punched out more than 30% of the time whenever he’s received semi-regular playing time. He has a 34% strikeout rate across 1,749 big-league plate appearances.

articles.title: Astros Hire Conner Watson As Director Of Hitting
body: The Astros have hired Conner Watson as their new director of hitting, The Athletic’s Chandler Rome reports. Watson heads to Houston after spending the last two seasons as the Guardians’ assistant director of hitting development.

The new hire continues an offseason of change for an Astros team that is looking for both a new GM and manager. In this case, Watson fills a role that has been open since August, when former director of hitting Dan Hennigan departed for a coaching job on the Wake Forest staff.

Spencer Medick was hired as Houston’s director of pitching earlier this week, so the Astros now have two division heads in place overseeing the entire organization’s pitching and hitting approaches. It is perhaps a little unusual that Medick and Watson were hired in advance of a general manager taking the wheel of baseball operations, though it perhaps tracks given how Astros owner Jim Crane is known for his active role in front office decisions.

Before joining the Guardians, Watson spent three years as a lead instructor at Driveline’s Arizona branch. He’ll now look to shake up and perhaps modernize the Astros’ hitting practices at both the major and minor league levels. While many of Houston’s coaches and manager Joe Espada won’t be returning in 2027, hitting coach Victor Rodriguez was expected to be retained, though this could potentially change depending on Watson’s plans.

articles.title: Guardians Notes: Kwan, Velazquez, Rotation
body: The Guardians won the American League Central for the third straight year and reached the doorstep of the World Series in 2026, but their season ended with a six-game loss to the Rays in the ALCS. With their championship hopes dashed again, Guardians president of baseball operations Chris Antonetti, general manager Mike Chernoff and assistant GM Matt Forman met with the media on Thursday to wrap up 2026 and discuss the upcoming offseason.
[RELATED: Guardians Offseason Outlook]

The Guardians aren’t at risk of losing outfielder Steven Kwan to free agency this winter, but the two-time All-Star only has one year of control left. MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz projects an $11.3MM salary for Kwan in his third and final trip through arbitration. That’s an eminently reasonable salary for a player of his caliber, though it’s a pricey figure for a team that had the lowest payroll in baseball (around $75MM). The Guardians have a history of trading away productive veterans with dwindling team control, evidenced by deals in which they shipped out Josh Naylor, Francisco Lindor, Corey Kluber, Carlos Carrasco, Trevor Bauer and Mike Clevinger. With that in mind, Kwan could be an offseason trade candidate. However, if we’re to believe Guardians brass, he isn’t going anywhere.
“As we sit here today, we’re expecting Steven Kwan to be a big part of a contending team next year,” Antonetti said (link via Paul Hoynes of cleveland.com).

articles.title: NL East Notes: Murphy, Mets, Marlins, Compton, Miller
body: Before Pat Murphy was promoted from bench coach to Brewers’ manager in November 2023, Murphy was known to be one of the finalists in the Mets’ 2019 managerial search that eventually resulted in the hiring of Carlos Beltran. Then-Mets GM Brodie Van Wagenen (who is now Murphy’s agent) preferred Murphy as the hire and made that recommendation to former COO Jeff Wilpon, as Van Wagenen and Murphy told the New York Post’s Joel Sherman.

Less than three months after being hired, Beltran resigned in January 2020 as part of the fallout from the Astros’ sign-stealing scandal. Murphy said the Mets reached out to him at the time and he was still interested in the managerial job, but the team ended up promoting from within by installing quality control coach Luis Rojas for the role. Van Wagenen said that decision was made with a nod to continuity, as Rojas was already a known quantity and Spring Training was just around the corner.

Needless to say, the Brewers are glad that Murphy stayed put, as the club is now three wins away from a World Series title with the skipper at the helm. It is anyone’s guess as to whether or not Murphy would’ve been able to similarly thrive in New York, but Milwaukee’s continued success under Murphy adds some salt to the Mets’ revolving door in the dugout. Counting Beltran, the Mets have had seven different managers within the last decade, and the hope that is interim-turned-permanent manager Andy Green can finally bring some stability.

articles.title: Todd Benzinger Passes Away
body: Former big leaguer Todd Benzinger passed away on Wednesday at age 63, according to a statement released by the Reds earlier this week. Three of Benzinger’s nine MLB seasons (from 1987-95) were spent in Cincinnati, with the switch-hitter playing a memorable role in the Reds’ World Series-winning squad in 1990.

A fourth-round pick for the Red Sox in the 1981 draft, Benzinger spent his first two Major League seasons with Boston before he was dealt to the Reds as part of a five-player swap in December 1988. It was a virtual homecoming for Benzinger, whose birthplace of Dayton, Kentucky is right across the Ohio River from Cincinnati. Benzinger made a bit of history in his very first at-bat as a Red, as his RBI single in the first inning on Opening Day 1989 officially ended Orel Hershiser’s regular-season scoreless-inning streak at a record 59 innings.

Acting as the Reds’ everyday first baseman in 1989, Benzinger moved into more of a platoon role the next season as both a first baseman and occasional left fielder. Benzinger did get the start at first in Game 4 of the 1990 World Series, and he’ll forever be remembered in Cincinnati for recording the final out (a Carney Lansford pop-up in foul territory) that sealed the Reds’ sweep of the Athletics.

“[Benzinger] was a super nice guy,” former Reds teammate and Hall-of-Famer Barry Larkin told MLB.com’s Mark Sheldon. “He was always a hard worker, not real loud. Just about doing his business. He was just a steady, consistent contributor. There was no craziness about him. He fit in well with the team. Just a really good, solid guy.”

articles.title: Yankees Notes: Boone, Judge, Massey
body: The Yankees made the decision to bring manager Aaron Boone back for a tenth season. Boone, who’ll become the seventh skipper in franchise history to reach a decade with the club, is under contract via the two-year extension he signed in February 2025.

Owner Hal Steinbrenner told reporters on Wednesday that there’d not yet been any conversations with Boone regarding another extension (link via Bryan Hoch of MLB.com). While that doesn’t necessarily mean they won’t discuss that at some point, Boone said that managing on an expiring deal “doesn’t bother (him) at all.” He pointed out that players and coaches frequently work without long-term contractual certainty, though many teams prefer not to have their managers or top front office executive in a lame duck capacity.

The Yankees allowed general manager Brian Cashman to hold his position on an expiring deal in 2026. The GM himself announced Wednesday that he and the team were finalizing an extension, one that’ll likely ensure that Cashman reaches three decades in the GM role. He’s already by far the longest-tenured active general manager, having ascended to the job in February 1998.

articles.title: Cardinals, Hitting Coach Brant Brown Part Ways
body: The Cardinals are moving on from hitting coach Brant Brown, as first reported by Katie Woo of The Athletic. Brown has been with the club for the past two seasons.

St. Louis ranked 16th in scoring this past season. The club finished in the bottom five in OPS, wOBA, and wRC+. The Cardinals were similarly underwhelming on offense in 2025, ranking in the bottom 10 in those three metrics.

Brown was hired heading into the 2025 campaign. He’s had several big-league stops along the way. After a decade coaching in the minors, Brown joined the Dodgers as an assistant hitting coach in 2018. He moved on to the Marlins in 2023 as their top hitting coach. Brown also had a brief stop in Seattle before coming to St. Louis.

Woo adds that the Cardinals are expected to keep the majority of manager Oli Marmol’s staff. Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch reports that outfield coach Jon Jay and third base coach Ron Warner will be retained by the team for next season. Jay and Warner were both on expiring contracts.

While the offense as a whole came up short, there were several bright spots in 2026. The biggest development was the breakout of Jordan Walker. The former top prospect blasted 29 homers and stole 22 bases en route to his first All-Star selection. Walker made some batting stance tweaks that helped him get more out of his top-of-the-charts bat speed. He lowered his groundball rate and hit more homers in 2026 than he had from 2023 through 2025.

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: Cleveland Guardians
body: The Guardians again rode another strong September to their third straight AL Central title. They nabbed a first-round bye and overcame a 2-0 deficit to bounce the White Sox en route to the ALCS. Cleveland looked generally overmatched against the best team in the American League, though, and they again face questions about whether there’s enough offensive talent to truly rank among World Series contenders.

articles.title: Two Pitchers Elect Free Agency
body: Veteran right-handers Connor Brogdon and Carlos Hernández elected free agency earlier this week, according to the MiLB.com transactions log. Both hurlers had been with the Guardians organization.

The Guardians gave Brogdon a major league contract worth $900K last winter, but the low-cost flier didn’t pan out. The 31-year-old made 16 appearances out of the bullpen and pitched to a 5.06 ERA in 16 innings. Even though Brodgon walked just three hitters, allowing five home runs made it difficult to hold a spot on the Guardians’ roster. They outrighted Brogdon twice during the season, including in late September, and he could only muster a 6.35 ERA in 11 1/3 innings when he took the ball for Triple-A Columbus.

Cleveland was the fourth major league organization for Brogdon, whom the Phillies took in the 10th round of the 2017 draft. He debuted three years later and put together the best stretch of his career from 2021-22, a 101 2/3-inning run of 3.36 ERA pitching with solid strikeout and walk percentages of 23.6 and 6.9, respectively. Big league success has eluded Brogdon since then, though, as he has combined for a 5.59 ERA in 95 frames with the Phillies, Dodgers, Angels and Guardians dating back to 2024.

articles.title: Guardians’ Kahlil Watson Undergoes Core Muscle Surgery
body: The Guardians announced this week that outfielder Kahlil Watson underwent surgery Tuesday to repair a bilateral core muscle (sports hernia) injury. The team didn’t provide an exact timetable for his recovery but noted that similar cases tend to come with a timeframe of eight to 12 weeks for returning to play.

Watson, 23, will head into the 2027 season as a depth option in Cleveland. A first-round pick by the Marlins in 2021, he initially drew top prospect fanfare but saw his production wane early in his minor league tenure. Watson went from Miami to Cleveland as part of the 2023 trade swapping out the unwanted contracts of Jean Segura and Josh Bell. He spent parts four seasons in the Guardians’ system before making his major league debut this season.

The Guardians promoted Watson in mid-June and kept him on the big league roster into late May. He totaled 91 plate appearances but managed only a tepid.239/.264/.341 with a homer and nine steals (in 10 attempts). Watson fanned a whopping 32 times in that small sample and drew just three walks. He was more productive in Triple-A, where he batted.247/.361/.455 with 19 homers, 24 steals, a 13.3% walk rate and a 26.7% strikeout rate in 442 trips to the plate. He turned in comparable numbers at the Double-A and Triple-A levels in 2025.

articles.title: Ben Sestanovich, Scott Sharp Candidates For Astros’ GM Job
body: Royals senior vice president Scott Sharp and Braves assistant general manager Ben Sestanovich are candidates for the Astros’ general manager position, reports Chandler Rome of The Athletic. They join a trio of known candidates whom Bob Nightengale of USA Today and Rome reported to be on the radar this afternoon: Matt Kleine, Josh Barfield and Randy Flores.

Sharp, 54, has spent the last two decades with Kansas City. He climbed to assistant general manager and eventually a senior vice president role under baseball operations president J.J. Picollo. He has worked in various facets of baseball operations with the Royals and frequently garnered attention from other teams for a role running a front office. Sharp has interviewed with at least the Mets, Giants and Rockies in recent years.

Sestanovich is a Harvard product who pitched for the Crimson in 2011. He worked in the Padres’ player development after graduation, then took an assistant GM role under Alex Anthopoulos with Atlanta in 2019. He’s one of five AGMs in the Braves’ front office.

Rome reported this afternoon that the Astros could have their GM hire in place before the end of the World Series. They’ll also need to settle on a new manager after moving on from Joe Espada at the end of the season.

In other hiring news, Rome reported that Houston is hiring Spencer Medick as their director of pitching. He’ll work in a non-uniform capacity to oversee the team’s pitching development. Medick had been the pitching coach for the Yankees’ Triple-A affiliate in Scranton/Wilkes-Barre.

articles.title: Astros Have Spoken To Josh Barfield, Randy Flores About GM Vacancy
body: The Astros’ general manager search has been underway for two months but could soon draw to a close. Chandler Rome of The Athletic reports that Houston could hire a new general manager before the completion of the World Series. Rome lists White Sox assistant general manager Josh Barfield, Cardinals assistant general manager Randy Flores and (as already reported earlier today) Brewers assistant general manager Matt Kleine as three candidates still in the running. That’s not necessarily an exhaustive list; Rome notes that in-house assistant GM Connor Huff has a particularly good relationship with owner Jim Crane, for instance.

Both Barfield, 43, and Flores, 51, are former big leaguers. Barfield was an infielder and fourth-round pick of the Padres. He debuted with San Diego in 2006 and had a big rookie showing but was unable to replicate that in parts of three subsequent seasons. He concluded his major league playing career with a.264/.295/.375 batting line in 1075 plate appearances.

Upon retiring, Barfield hooked on as a scout in the Diamondbacks organization. He held that role for several years before being elevated to Arizona’s assistant director of player development and, eventually, director of player development in 2019.

The White Sox hired Barfield as an assistant general manager in 2023, and he’s been in their front office since, helping to oversee the remarkable turnaround enjoyed by the South Siders in 2026. He’s had a hand in every facet of their baseball operations, ranging from player acquisition to scouting to player development and roster management.

articles.title: Poll: Does Paul Skenes Just Need To Fix His Changeup?
body: It’s obvious that Paul Skenes did not have the follow-up campaign one would have expected of a Cy Young winner. After holding opponents to a 1.97 ERA last year, that figure nearly doubled to 3.82 in 2026. Skenes still came out above average by strikeout rate (28.1%) and walk rate (6.9%), and ERA estimators like xERA (3.28) and SIERA (3.34) were a bit kinder to him than the surface-level ERA. For what it’s worth, FanGraphs valued Skenes at 4.2 wins above replacement, ranking 12th-highest among qualified starters this year. Nonetheless, it was a clear drop-off for Skenes by his lofty standards.

As MLBTR’s Charlie Wright wrote in August, Skenes’ stuff looked mostly the same this year. Apart from ditching his cutter, the righty’s four-seam fastball, splitter, sinker, slider, and changeup usage were all within 3.5% of their 2025 levels. The four-seamer remained his most common offering and averaged 96.8 mph – a 1.4 mph decrease from last year, but still well above league average. Curiously, the most drastic change in Skenes’ pitch mix was a sharp decline in the effectiveness of his changeup.

articles.title: Pirates Re-Sign Kyler Fedko To Minors Deal
body: The Pirates have agreed to re-sign outfielder Kyler Fedko to a two-year minor league deal, per Colin Beazley of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. Fedko underwent knee surgery in August to repair a torn ACL, MCL, and LCL, so he’ll be rehabbing for a good portion of the 2027 season.

The 27-year-old Fedko debuted with the Twins this year after spending parts of six seasons working through the minor leagues. He spent about a month in the Majors starting in mid-June, appearing in 14 games and taking 19 trips to the plate. Fedko walked twice and got his first RBI on a sacrifice fly, though he did not record his first big league hit. The Twins optioned him to Triple-A St. Paul on July 10th. He batted.274/.362/.545 at that level with a 128 wRC+ until the aforementioned triple knee injury ended Fedko’s season in early August. Minnesota released him on September 1st, and the Pirates picked him up three days later.

The two-year deal gives Fedko some continuity as he continues his rehab. Meanwhile, the Pirates get a no-risk depth outfielder to stash in the minors for the 2028 season (late 2027 if Fedko progresses quickly). This year was Fedko’s second at the Triple-A level. In 2025, he took 187 plate appearances for St. Paul after being promoted from Double-A in August. He batted.268/.353/.476 with a 115 wRC+, striking out at around average rates and showing penchants for power, speed, and getting on base. The latter three remained on display this year. Fedko knocked 17 home runs, stole ten bases, and walked at an 11.1% clip in 75 games for St. Paul before the injury.

articles.title: NL West Notes: Giants, Itoh, Taira, Vesia, Hernandez, R-Rod, Rockies
body: The Giants are among the big league teams who have scouted Hiromi Itoh and Kaima Taira, Susan Slusser of the San Francisco Chronicle reports. The Japanese right-handers are expected to be posted for MLB clubs this offseason, even though the impending lockout will sure interrupt their 45-day posting window unless a deal is reached between the time of posting (potentially early November) and the lockout-induced transactions freeze on December 1.

At least 15 MLB teams were thought to be scouting Taira and Itoh is also drawing plenty of interest, so it isn’t surprising to see the Giants on this list. Either righty would make a good fit on a Giants team in need of rotation help, and while Taira doesn’t have a long track record as a starter, he could conceivably transition to a role in San Francisco’s leaky bullpen if things didn’t work out as a starting pitcher. Despite the team’s increased NPB scouting presence, Slusser notes that “the Giants haven’t fared well in their pursuit of Japanese players in recent years,” with such targets as Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Roki Sasaki ending up with the arch-rival Dodgers.

articles.title: Five Players Elect Free Agency
body: Five more players who played in MLB this year have elected minor league free agency, according to the transaction tracker at MiLB.com. These players were all outrighted off teams’ 40-man rosters and have played seven-plus seasons in the minors, so the elections are mostly formalities.

The Mets acquired Bruján from Minnesota in a cash trade over the offseason. The out-of-options infielder failed to break camp and cleared waivers on Opening Day. New York called him up in early May while Francisco Lindor was injured. Bruján spent six weeks on the active roster but only started three games, going 1-11 in 13 plate appearances. The former top prospect batted.278/.385/.421 over 258 plate appearances with Triple-A Syracuse.

Mastrobuoni missed the first two months of the season due to a right calf strain. The Mariners waived him in June, called him up briefly in July, then sent him through waivers again. He batted.192 in 13 MLB games and hit.245/.338/.375 over 222 trips to the plate with Triple-A Tacoma.

Vázquez, a 27-year-old shortstop, spent virtually the entire season with Triple-A Norfolk. He had a mediocre.226/.271/.371 batting line in 52 games around a few injuries. Vázquez got a two-day stint on Baltimore’s big league roster in late August, making a lone appearance as a pinch-runner and scoring the game-winning run against the Cardinals.

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: Atlanta Braves
body: The Braves won the NL East and defeated the Phillies in the wild card round before falling to the Dodgers in the NLDS. It was a nice return to form for the Braves after their injury-marred 76-86 season in 2025, but Atlanta will need to fill some roster holes and perhaps address some broader concerns in order to be championship contenders next year.

articles.title: Rockies Fire Pitching Coach Alon Leichman
body: The Rockies have parted ways with pitching coach Alon Leichman, according to The Athletic’s Ken Rosenthal and Keith Law. Leichman held the position for just one season, as the Rox only hired the 37-year-old last December.

On paper, the quick hook isn’t necessarily a surprise given that Colorado’s pitching staff finished last in baseball in ERA (5.59), SIERA (4.58), strikeout rate (17.5%), WHIP (1.52), and opponents’ batting average (.283), plus last or close to last in multiple other categories. As is the case with any coaching firing, however, it is fair to wonder how much of the blame can be played on a coach for the shortcomings of a roster that was clearly lacking in pitching talent. In the Rockies’ case specifically, the team has spent its entire history trying to figure out how to develop and maintain quality pitching in the thin air of Coors Field.

Nobody expected Leichman to turn this around in a single year, but president of baseball operations Paul DePodesta may have planted some hints about the firing when speaking to reporters last week. The starters’ pre-game preparation under Leichman may have been an issue, as DePodesta pointed specifically to the fact that Colorado’s “run differential was worse in innings one and two than innings three and beyond combined. There were way too many games where we just got into a hole within the first two innings.”

articles.title: Reds Avoid Arbitration With Oswaldo Cabrera
body: The Reds announced that they have agreed to a one-year, Major League contract with utilityman Oswaldo Cabrera. The signing allows the two sides to avoid salary arbitration, and MLB.com’s Mark Sheldon reports that Cabrera will earn $1MM in guaranteed salary plus up to $200K in bonuses related to plate appearances.

There was some thought that Cabrera could be a non-tender candidate given his lack of career production at the big league level. However, the Reds only added Cabrera to the organization on a waiver claim on September 18, so Cincinnati might’ve always had an eye towards retaining the 27-year-old heading into the offseason. Cabrera’s modest salary is an easy fit even in the Reds’ limited budget, and the team now has some experienced depth in place.

As a rookie with the Yankees in 2022, Cabrera hit.247/.312/.429 in his first 171 plate appearances as a big leaguer, good for a 110 wRC+. This remains the high point of his offensive production, as Cabrera has since batted.230/.289/.326 over 803 PA with New York and Cincinnati. Working as a part-time bench piece in the Bronx, Cabrera’s career was interrupted in May 2025 by an ugly ankle injury that required a season-ending surgery. He made it back for the start of the 2026 minor league season and hit.288/.345/.444 over 524 PA for Scranton/Wilkes-Barre, and Cabrera also made it into seven total MLB games with the Yankees and Reds.

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: Pittsburgh Pirates
body: The Pirates took a step forward in 2026 but still missed the playoffs for an 11th consecutive season. They’re now set for a notable set of salary increases in arbitration and could lose one of the best bats available this winter to free agency.

articles.title: Reviewing The Rays, Angels, And Reds Three-Team Trade
body: The three-team deal that sent Josh Lowe to the Angels and Gavin Lux to the Rays over the winter was intriguing, if not season-altering. Los Angeles picked up an everyday outfielder to replace Taylor Ward, who was traded to the Orioles. Tampa Bay landed a Brandon Lowe replacement after sending the second baseman to Pittsburgh.

And then there’s Cincinnati. The Reds got off the $5.525MM owed to Lux in his final year of arbitration. They also picked up reliever Brock Burke from the Angels. It seemed like a fine bit of business, but not a move that would have a major impact on the season. The trade turned out to be a big win for Cincinnati, and pretty convincingly so.

Burke had a decent run with the Rangers after moving to the bullpen in 2022. He struggled in 2024 and was designated for assignment midway through the year. The Angels picked him up for the final six weeks of the season. Burke made the club in 2025 and put up a solid 3.36 ERA over 69 games. He had a year of team control remaining when he was sent to Cincinnati.

The 30-year-old Burke was tremendous in his lone season with the Reds. He delivered a 2.30 ERA across 74 1/3 innings. Burke’s 77 appearances led the National League. He was the club’s top left-handed option with Caleb Ferguson opening the year on the IL, and manager Terry Francona leaned on him early and often.

articles.title: Pirates Promote Justin Newman To Director Of Amateur Scouting
body: When he met with reporters in late September, Pirates general manager Ben Cherington revealed that he planned to hire a full-time scouting director. Two weeks later, Cherington accomplished his goal. The Pirates have promoted Justin Newman to director of amateur scouting, Colin Beazley of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports.

Newman, a University of Rochester alumnus, has worked in various positions with the Pirates since he joined their front office in 2017. He had been their director of player analysis since 2025. Newman’s main focus has been on the draft in recent years, according to Beazley. In his new position, the 31-year-old will replace Justin Horowitz, who left last October to become the Nationals’ assistant GM.

Horowitz was only with the Pirates for the 2024 and’25 drafts, but they appear to have struck gold in both years. The Pirates used their first-round picks on shortstop Konnor Griffin (ninth overall) and right-hander Seth Hernandez (sixth) when Horowitz was in the organization. Griffin was so highly regarded as a prospect that he scored a nine-year, $140MM extension last April. He went on to impress as a 20-year-old rookie. Hernandez, also 20, is on the shortlist of the best pitching prospects in baseball.

Between Horowitz’s exit and Newman’s promotion, Pittsburgh relied on assistant GM Kevan Graves to oversee its draft in 2026. With Graves at the helm, the team used the fifth overall selection on former LSU outfielder Derek Curiel. Graves also led the hiring process for the director of amateur scouting job, per Beazley.

articles.title: Paul DePodesta Discusses Rockies’ Pitching Struggles
body: If you want to take a glass-half-full approach with the long-struggling Rockies, they won 15 more games in 2026 than they did last year. If you want to take a glass-half-empty approach, they went 6-18 in September and clinched the majors’ worst record (58-104) for the second straight season. Colorado has lost triple-digit games four years in a row, and the team hasn’t come close to going.500 or better since a 91-72 effort in 2018. The Rockies’ ace that year was left-hander Kyle Freeland, who overcame hitter-friendly Coors Field to finish fourth in National League Cy Young voting.
[RELATED: Rockies Offseason Outlook]

While Freeland is still a Rockie to this day, he has not approached the success he had eight years ago. He was good for 202 1/3 innings of 2.85 ERA ball then, but the soft-tossing 33-year-old just wrapped up a season in which he posted a 6.65 ERA in 135 1/3 frames. Freeland was a major part of a staff that ranked last in the sport in ERA (5.59), and the Rockies’ run prevention issues weren’t limited to Coors Field. They had a better road ERA (5.35; it was 5.83 at home), but they still came in second to last in that category.

Meanwhile, although the Rockies’ offense tied for last in the league in wRC+ (91), only six teams scored more runs. It’s clear pitching was the main culprit for yet another rough season. President of baseball operations Paul DePodesta acknowledged as much at his end-of-season press conference on Tuesday, as Kyle Newman of the Denver Post relays.

articles.title: The Pirates Nailed The Brandon Lowe Trade
body: The Astros went into last offseason in search of rotation depth. The Rays were looking to offload a cumbersome contract (by their standards). Enter the Pirates, who seized the opportunity and came away with a tremendous trade haul.

Pittsburgh landed second baseman Brandon Lowe, left-hander Mason Montgomery, and outfielder Jake Mangum in the three-team deal. The club sent right-hander Mike Burrows to Houston. The Astros routed a pair of prospects (outfielder Jacob Melton, righty Anderson Brito) to the Rays.

While all three players acquired in the swap made an impact for Pittsburgh, Lowe was the headliner. He smashed 35 home runs as a critical piece in a lineup that has lacked thump in recent years. Lowe finished with an.824 OPS, his best mark since his breakout 2021 season.

The Pirates finished sixth in scoring this season. They flirted with the top spot at times over the summer, but faded late as injuries to key bats thinned out the lineup. It was a huge turnaround after the club finished dead last in runs per game in 2025. Pittsburgh had finished in the bottom 10 in scoring every season since 2018. Even that year, the team ranked 20th. It’s been an inept offense for quite some time.

articles.title: 12 Players Elect Free Agency
body: Now that the season is over, we’ll start seeing several players choose to become minor league free agents. Major League free agents (i.e. players with six-plus years of big league service time) will hit the open market five days after the end of the World Series, but eligible minor leaguers can already start electing free agency.

To qualify, these players must have been all outrighted off their team’s 40-man rosters during the 2026 season without being added back. These players also must have multiple career outrights on their resume, and/or at least three years of Major League service time.

MLB Trade Rumors will offer periodic updates over the coming weeks about many other players hitting the market in this fashion. These free agent decisions are all listed on the official MLB.com or MILB.com transactions pages, for further reference.
